4   CALCulate Subsystem
    The CALCulate subsystem exists to perform postacquisition data processing. Functions in
    the SENSe subsystem are related to data acquisition, while the CALCulate subsystem
    operates on the data acquired by a SENSe function.
                                                                                                      1
    The CALCulate subsystem is logically between the SENSe subsystem and data output to
    either the bus or the display. When a measurement is triggered by a MEASure command, an           2
    INITiate command, or meeting the prevailing TRIGger conditions, the SENSe subsystem               3
    collects data. This data is transformed by CALCulate, as specified, and then passed on to the
    selected output. In effect, the collection of new data triggers the CALCulate subsystem. The      4
    CALCulate subsystem may also be directed by command to perform a transform, making it             5
    possible to change the configuration of CALCulate and consequently derive a different set of
    results from the same SENSed data set without reacquiring sense data.                             6
    The CALCulate subsystem consists of a number of independent subsystems. Each of the               7
    subsystems is a sub-block of the CALCulate block. The data flows through the sub-blocks in        8
    a serial fashion, through the first sub-block, then onto the second sub-block and so on. The
    manner in which these sub-blocks are arranged is specified in the PATH command. It is             9
    permissible for a CALCulate block to have more than one instance of any of the sub-blocks.      10
    Instances of the same sub-block are differentiated by a numeric suffix. For example, two
    independent filters would exist as the :CALCulate:FILTer1 and the :CALCulate:FILTer2            11
    subsystem sub-blocks.                                                                           12    TWIR01p13




    Note: The notation Xn* indicates the complex conjugate of a number. So:                         13
        XX* = MAG2(X) = |X|2

         4.1        :AVERage subsystem
                    CALCulate:AVERage                                                                                         HP054
                                                                                                                              FL005




                    This subsystem provides an analytical post-processing function. The AVERage subsystem
                    combines successive measurements to produce a new composite result. The new result has
                    the same number of points and control axis as the original measurement.
 1
                    A :COUNt command is provided to specify the number of measurements to combine. When
 2                  :COUNT averages are reached, the TerminalCONtrol switch specifies the operation of the
 3                  average subsystem. The TerminalCONtrol switch can be configured to continue replacing
                    old values with new values (MOVing), to exponentially weight new measurements
     4              (EXPonential), to automatically repeat (REPeat), or to continue adding new measurements in
 5                  the NORMal fashon, as specified by :TYPE.

 6                  The average operation differs from CALC:SMOOthing in the fact that AVERage combines
                    the jth point of each measurement with the jth point of preceeding measurements, whereas in
 7                  SMOOthing the jth point is processed with adjacent points (...., j-2, j-1, j, j+1, j+2, ...) of the
 8                  current measurement set.

 9                  A typical device action for CALC:AVERage

4.1.2     :COUNt <numeric_value>
          CALCulate:AVERage:COUNt                                                                                   HP054




          Specifies the number of measurements to combine using the :TYPE setting. After :COUNt
          measurements have been averaged, the operation of the AVERage subsystem is controlled
          by the setting of the :TCONtrol node.
                                                                                                             1
          The count for array based results is independent of the number of points in the result array.
          For example, an instrument which normally provides a measurement result which is a 401
                                                                                                             2
          point array would specify an average count of two to average two results, not 802.                 3
          When averaging is ON, some devices may automatically set :COUNt values in the TRIGger              4
          subsystem based on the AVER:COUNt value, such that the TRIGger subsystem provides
          enough triggers for the average.
                                                                                                             5
          At *RST, this value is device dependent.
                                                                                                             6
4.1.2.1     :AUTO <Boolean> | ONCE
                                                                                                             7
          CALCulate:AVERage:COUNt:AUTO                                                                       8      HP054




          AUTO ON causes the device to select a value for :COUNt which is appropriate for the
          current measurement. Selecting AUTO ONCE will have the effect of setting AUTO ON and
                                                                                                             9
          then OFF.                                                                                         10
          At *RST, this value is set to OFF.                                                                11

          CALCulate:AVERage:STATe

         4.7.1     :UPHase
12                 CALCulate:FORMat:UPHase                                                                        HP003




13                 The UPHase subsystem is used to specify how unwrapped phase is computed. A reference
                   position is specified which is used as an estimate of what the unwrapped phase of calculated
14                 result should be. The calculated result is constrained to be within +/- 180 degrees of the
15                 reference position. Other points are calculated to produce a result which is compatible with
                   the above constraint and does not “wrap” when cardinal points such as +/- 180 degrees are
16                 crossed. The reference position would typically be a well known point in a measurement
17                 such as the center of a band pass filter.

4.8       :GDAPerture                                                                                        15
          CALCulate:GDAPerture
          Group Delay Aperture is defined as the negative of the derivative of phase with respect to         16
          frequency. The group delay format requires specifying an aperture over which the                   17
          measurement is made. Since the frequency span of the measurement is known, the frequency
          step over the entire span can be thought of as d(freq) This function permits the setting of that   18
          aperture. APERture is tightly coupled to SPAN by the equation:                                     19
                 APERture = GDAPerture:SPAN/(SENSe|SOURce):FREQuency:SPAN
                                                                                                             20
4.8.1     :SPAN <numeric_value>
          CALCulate:GDAPerture:SPAN                                                                          21
          Specifies the aperture in Hertz. Minimum value is instrument-dependent.                            22
          At *RST, this function is set to MIN.                                                              23

          Specifies the aperture as a ratio of desired aperture span/measured frequency span.                25

         4.9        :IMMediate
                    CALCulate:IMMediate
                    Causes the CALCulate subsystem to reprocess existing SENSe data without reacquiring the
                    data. This permits the user to change a CALCulate subsystem, setting and output new results
                    without initiating a data acquisition.
 1
                    Note that CALC:IMMediate? is semantically equivalent to CALC:IMM;DATA?. The query
 2                  form outputs the results of the new calculation.
 3                  This command describes an event and therefore has no associated *RST condition.
     4   4.9.1      :AUTO <Boolean>
                    CALCulate:IMMediate:AUTO
 5                                                                                                                           HP068




                    The AUTO command is used to specify if the CALCulate subsystem continually transforms
 6                  the data (AUTO ON) whenever any changes are made which would affect the CALCulate
 7                  subsystem output. With CALC:IMM:AUTO set to OFF, CALCulate only produces new data
                    when data is received or when the CALC:IMMediate command is received. Once
 8                  CALC:IMM:AUTO is set to ON, the CALCulate Subsystem shall produce results when any
 9                  CALC subsystem command is processed, even when new data is not being received. This
                    allows the user to make configuration changes in the CALCulate subsystem and immediately
10                  have new CALC:DATA results on the same sensed data.
11                  At *RST, this value is set to OFF.
12
         4.10       :INTegral
13                  CALCulate:INTegral                                                                                   PH071
14                  This subsystem provides a point to point integration of a data set. The result is an estimate of
                    the integral of the input. The units of the result of this process is the product of the currently
15                  selected amplitude units of the integrated data and the units of the X- axis.
16       4.10.1     :STATe <Boolean>
                    CALCulate:INTegral:STATe                                                                             PH071
17
                    Determines whether the integrate function is enabled.
18
                    At *RST this function is OFF
19
         4.10.2     :TYPE SCALar | MOVing
20                  CALCulate:INTegral:TYPE                                                                              PH071
21                  Specifies whether the result is a single value (SCALar) or a set of data points (MOVing). If
                    SCALar is selected the result is an estimate of the definite integral over the entire data set. If
22                  MOVing is selected each point in the integrated data set is the integral up to the
23                  corresponding point in the original data set.

24                  At *RST this function is set to a device dependent value.

25       4.11       :LIMit
                    CALCulate:LIMit
26                                                                                                                           HP007




                    The LIMit node collects together the commands associated with controlling and getting
                    reports from a single LIMit test. The LIMit test may defined as an UPPer limit, a LOWer

         4-18     CALCulate:IMMediate
                                   1999 SCPI Command Reference

           limit, or both. A LIMit test may be defined as being scalar, that is UPPer or LOWer are
           provided a single value each.
                                                                                                                    HP007




           Alternatively, UPPer or LOWer may be defined as a series of points (a vector) representing a
           waveform limit. For such a vector limit test, each point in the series (vector) must be
           qualified by where it occurs with respect to the control (typically the X) axis. The CONTrol         1
           node is used to define the points along the control axis. UPPer and LOWer represent the
           dependent (typically the Y) axis, and are given values corresponding to these control axis
                                                                                                                2
           points. That is, the first value for UPPer and LOWer corresponds to the first value of               3
           CONTrol, the second value for UPPer and LOWer corresponds to the second value of
           CONTrol, and so on. UPPer, LOWer and CONTrol shall contain the same number of points,
                                                                                                                4
           or an error shall be generated when data processing commences. For scalar limit tests, as            5
           described earlier, the CONTrol subsystem is not used.
                                                                                                                6   HP007




           If the data and the limit are scalar (single values), then LIMit shall produce results for each
           piece of scalar data tested. If the data and the limit are both vectors, then LIMit shall produce
                                                                                                                7
           results for each vector data tested. If the limit is scalar and the data is a vector, then LIMit     8
           shall perform a the limit test by treating the scalar limit as an equivalent vector (all points
           having the same value).
                                                                                                                9
4.11.1     :STATe <Boolean>
                                                                                                               10
           CALCulate:LIMit:STATe                                                                               11   HP007




           Is used to set or query if the LIMit test is active or not.
                                                                                                               12
           At *RST, this is set to OFF.
                                                                                                               13
4.11.2     :CONTrol
           CALCulate:LIMit:CONTrol                                                                             14   HP007

           where the limit test is not based on a single point.

4.12.1     [:EXPRession] <numeric_expression>
           CALCulate:MATH:EXPRession                                                                        23   TWIR01p13




           This subsystem controls which expression is used by the CALCulate block.                         24
4.12.1.1     :CATalog?                                                                                      25
           CALCulate:MATH:EXPRession:CATalog?                                                               HP083a
                                                                                                            26


                                                                              CALCulate:MATH         4-21
                                          1999 SCPI Command Reference

                    The CATalog query lists all the defined expressions. Response is a list of comma-separated
                    strings. Each string contains the name of an expression. If no expressions are currently
                    defined, the response ia a null string ("").
         4.12.1.2     [:DEFine] <numeric_expression>
 1                  CALCulate:MATH:EXPRession:DEFine                                                               HP083a
                    Defines the expression used for the math operations. The <numeric_expression> may
 2                  contain any of the following as operands and they may occur in any combination:
 3                             A <trace_name>
     4                         The reserved keyword IMPLied
 5                             The <data_handle> associated with another block
 6                  The reserved keyword IMPLied, refers to the IMPLied output of the previous CALCulate
 7                  sub-block. The ordering of the sub-blocks is specified by the PATH command. If the MATH
                    subsystem appears first in the PATH, then the IMPLied keyword refers to the <data_handle>
 8                  specified with the FEED command.
 9                  For example, to subtract a reference trace from the SENSe data, the following command
10                  would configure the MATH appropriately.
                       CALCulate:MATH:EXPRession (IMPLied - MY-TRACE)
11
                    This example assumes that the FEED command has been configured to select the appropriate
12                  SENSe <data_handle>. The IMPLied CALCulate data flow can be ignored and the SENSe
13                  data may be used directly in a <numeric_expression>:
                       CALCulate:MATH:EXPRession ( “SENSe1:POWer 3" - MY-TRACE)
14
                    At *RST, this function is undefined.
15
         4.12.1.3     :DELete
16                  CALCulate:MATH:EXPRession:DELete                                                               HP083a
17                  The DELete subsytem deletes expressions.
18       4.12.1.3.1   [:SELected] <expression_name>
                    CALCulate:MATH:EXPRession:DELete:SELected                                                      HP083a
19                  This command causes the selected expression to be deleted.

                    This command causes the all expressions to be deleted.

         4.12.1.4     :NAME <expression_name>
23                  CALCulate:MATH:EXPRession:NAME                                                                 HP083a
24                  The NAME command defines the name of the expression to be selected. If the expression
                    name, <expression_name>, already exists, then that existing expression shall be selected. If
25                  the expression name does not exist, then the new name shall be selected, but no expression
26                  shall be defined by this selection. <expression_name> is character data.
                    At *RST the value of NAME is device dependent.

4.13     :SMOothing
         CALCulate:SMOothing                                                                              2
         This subsystem specifies point-to-point smoothing of a data set. A data point in a smoothed      3
         data set is the average of adjacent points from a single original data set. Smoothing differs
         from averaging, in which a given point is the average of corresponding points from multiple      4
         data sets or acquisitions.                                                                       5

4.15     :TRANsform
         CALCulate:TRANsform                                                                             22
         TRANsform is the subsystem that permits sense data to be transformed from one domain to
                                                                                                         23
         another. Examples are from frequency domain to time domain or time domain to frequency
         domain. This is different from a SENSe:FUNC selection of domain because in SENSe, the           24
         data is actually collected in the selected domain, while in CALCulation:TRANsform, the
                                                                                                         25
         data is computed, for example, by use of Fourier Transform.
                                                                                                         26


                                                                      CALCulate:SMOothing 4-23
                                           1999 SCPI Command Reference

         4.15.1     :HISTogram
                    CALCulate:TRANsform:HISTogram                                                                   PH070
                    This subsystem transforms the data into a histogram. The histogram provides an amplitude
                    distribution of the incoming signal. The points in a histogram specify the ratio between the
                    number number of times a data point is within a particular amplitude belt and the total
 1                  number of incoming data points that participate in the transformation. The ratio is expressed
 2                  as a percentage.
 3                  The resolution of the histogram is specified by the number of points of the output signal. It
                    determines the amplitude belt wherein the data points are counted, using the equation:
     4
                    amplitude belt = amplitude range / histogram points
 5
                    The units of the amplitude range are the currently selected amplitude units of the data to be
 6                  transformed.
 7       4.15.1.1     :COUNt <numeric_value>
 8                  CALCulate:TRANsform:HISTogram:COUNt                                                             PH070
                    This specifies the number of measurements to include in the histogram.
 9
                    For scalar measurements, COUNt is the number of incoming data points that are used to
10                  create the histogram.
11                  The COUNt for array based results is independent of the number of points in the result array.
12                  For example, an instrument which normally provides a measurement result which is a 401
                    point array would specify a histogram count of two to create a histogram based on 802 data
13                  points.
14                  At *RST this value is device dependent
15       4.15.1.2     :ORDinate RATio | PERCent | PCT | COUNt
16                  CALCulate:TRANsform:HISTogram:ORDinate                                                          PH070
                    When ORDinate is set to RATio, the output of the HISTogram function is an absolute ratio.
17                  When ORDinate is set to PERCent, the output of the HISTogram function is PERCent
18                  (RATio*100). When ORDinate is set to COUNt, the output of the HISTogram function is
                    the number of points in that amplitude belt.
19
                    PCT is provided as a synonym for PERCent since IEEE 488.2 allows the use of PCT as a
20                  numeric suffix.
21                  At *RST this value is device dependent.
22       4.15.1.3     :POINts <numeric_value>
23                  CALCulate:TRANsform:HISTogram:POINts                                                            PH070
                    Specifies the number of POINts (amplitude belts) in the histogram.
24
                    At *RST this value is device dependent.
25
         4.15.1.4     :RANGe
26                  CALCulate:TRANsform:HISTogram:RANGe                                                             PH070
                    This node collects the commands used to control the size of the amplitude belts.

         4-24     CALCulate:TRANsform
                                  1999 SCPI Command Reference

5   CALibration Subsystem

    Instrument CALibration commands tend to be very class specific. Such commands properly
    belong in Volume 4 “Instrument Classes”. Therefore, expanded commands for controlling      1
    instrument calibration may not be found in Volume 2 “Command Reference”.

         5.1         [:ALL]
                     CALibration:ALL
                     The CALibrate:ALL command performs the same function as the CALibrate:ALL? except                 TK029
                     there is no response. An instrument shall report calibration errors through the
                     status-reporting mechanism.
 1
                     If this command is implemented as overlapped it shall be included in the No Operation             TK029
 2                   Pending flag (see IEEE 488.2 chapter 12).
 3                   While this command is executing the CALibrating bit of the Operation Status Condition             TK029
 4                   register shall be set (see 9.3 of Syntax & Style).

     5   5.2         [:ALL]?
                     CALibration:ALL?
 6                   The ALL? query performs a full calibration of the instrument and responds with a
 7                   <numeric_value> indicating the success of the calibration. A zero shall be returned if
                     calibration is completed successfully; otherwise a nonzero value which represents the
 8                   appropriate error number shall be returned. An instrument shall still report calibration errors
 9                   through the status-reporting mechanism, even though an error is reported by the value of the
                     query response.
10       5.3         :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
11                   CALibration:AUTO
                     AUTO sets whether or not the instrument should perform auto calibration at
12                   device-dependent intervals without user intervention.
13                   At *RST, AUTO OFF is selected.
14       5.4         :BINertia
                     CALibration:BINertia
15
                     Base Inertia
16
                     For chassis dynamometers, this node describes the procedure to determine the base
17                   mechanical inertia of the dynamometer roll system (all rotating mechanical components
18                   outside of the control loop). This procedure consists of an acceleration and deceleration of
                     the dynamometer rolls, from which a mechanical inertia calculation is made. The
19                   dynamometer is motored from an initial speed to a final speed at a given constant
20                   acceleration, and this interval is timed. Immediately, the dynamometer is motored back from
                     the final speed to the initial speed at the same constant acceleration (inverted), and this
21                   interval is timed. For this pair of intervals, the force transducer output is continuously
22                   measured, and the average interval force calculated. The average acceleration is calculated
                     using the interval initial and final speed values, and the interval time. This data is used to
23                   calculate the mechanical inertia (Inertia=Force/acceleration).
24       5.4.1       :AVERage?
25                   CALibration:BINertia:AVERage?
                     This query returns the running average of all base inertia values acquired since the last
26                   CALibration:BINertia:INITiate was invoked.



         5-2     CALibration[:ALL]
                                 1999 SCPI Command Reference

        At *RST, this value is set to 16.

        Begin motoring the dynamometer through the ACCeleration/deceleration pairs, using
        :SOURce:ACCeleration as the acceleration/deceleration rate, from LSPeed to HSPeed and
                                                                                                          4
        back, NRUNs times. All query commands must be accepted and responded to while this                5
        command is executing. This command describes an event and therefore has no associated
        *RST condition.

        When this command is initiated for dynamometers, the dynamometer must:
                                                                                                          7
           Check critical ancillaries, if any, for proper conditions: Brakes Off, Motor Contactor On,     8
           parameters within dynamometer safety limits. For conditions that prohibit operation of         9
           this procedure, issue appropriate warning messages, and execute the Idle Procedure.
                                                                                                         10
           Set the DYNO operation condition register Base Inertia Procedure bit indicating the Base
           Inertia is executing. Note: The DYNO operation condition register will be further defined     11
           in Volume 4.                                                                                  12
           Accelerate/decelerate the dynamometer through the speed intervals, recording time,            13
           average acceleration, average force for the specified number of runs. The data is placed
           in the BaseInertia table after each acceleration/deceleration is run. Update the              14
           :CALibration:BINertia:SDEViation value based on this run. End the procedure when the          15
           specified runs are complete.

           Clear the DYNO operation condition register Base Insrtia Procedure bit indicating the
           Base Inertia is not executing.                                                                17
           Issue the process complete message.                                                           18
           Execute the Idle Procedure.                                                                   19
           Update the on-line mechanical inertia value, if desired.                                      20

                    CALibration:DATA
 9                  Transfers the calibration data as arbitrary block program data. The query form returns the

11                  in addition to the execution error.
12       5.6        :PLOSs
                    CALibration:PLOSs
13
                    Parasitic Loss
14
                    For chassis dynamometers this node describes the commands associated with the parasitic
15                  loss procedure. This procedure measures and, if requested, updates the parasitic loss
16                  corrections for the dynamometer. The parasitic losses are measured by operating the
                    dynamometer at various selected speeds and measuring the force required to maintain the
17                  constant speed. This procedure uses the :MEMory table ’PARasitic’ that defines the speed
18                  points at which parasitic loss measurements are taken. The parasitic loss coefficients are
                    calculated at the end of the procedure and reside in the memory table PCOefficient.
19
         5.6.1      :APCoeff
20                  <numeric_value>,<numeric_value>,<numeric_value>[,<numeric_value>]
                    :CALibration:PLOSs:APCoeff
21
                    Active Parasitic Coefficients - APCoefficients
22
                    This is the presently active parasitic loss curve used by the dynamometer. The dynamometer
23                  will maintain coefficients for forward and reverse operations. The appropriate values must
24                  be placed in the APCoeff table, based on roll rotation.

25       5.6.2      :INITiate
                    :CALibration:PLOSs:INITiate
26                  This command starts the parasitic loss procedure. This is an overlapped command. This
                    command describes an event and therefore has no associated *RST condition.


         5-4     CALibration:DATA
                               1999 SCPI Command Reference

        When this command is initiated for dynamometers, the dynamometer must:
           Check critical ancillaries, if any, for proper conditions: Brakes Off, Motor Contactor On,
           parameters within dynamometer safety limits. For conditions that prohibit operation of
           this procedure, issue appropriate warning messages, and execute the Idle Procedure.
           Set the DYNO operation condition register Parasitic Loss Procedure bit indicating the             1
           Parasitic Loss procedure is executing. Note: The DYNO operation condition register will           2
           be further defined in Volume 4.
                                                                                                             3
           Accelerate dynamometer to the first speed point defined in the PARasitic memory table.
           Stabilize at speed point for defined stabilization time.                                          4
           Average the force at the roll surface required to maintain the speed set point over the           5
           latency time. The average force value is placed in the PARasitic table for the specified          6
           speed point. Continue until all speed points have been executed in the PARasitic table.
           The first zero speed in the PARasitic table ends the procedure.                                   7
           Perform a curve fit on the PARasitic table data and place the coefficients in the memory          8
           table PCoeff.                                                                                     9
           Clear the DYNO operation condition register Parasitic Loss Procedure bit indicating the          10
           parasitic loss procedure is not executing.
                                                                                                            11
           Issue the process complete message.
                                                                                                            12
           Execute the Idle Procedure.

13                 dynamometer at a fixed speed over a period of time. Warm-up completion is defined by

                   and comparing them to a target value tolerance.

8   DISPlay Subsystem
    The DISPlay subsystem controls the selection and presentation of textual, graphical, and
    TRACe information. This information includes measurement data, user-interaction displays,
    and data presented to the instrument by the controller. DISPlay is independent of, and does
    not modify, how data is returned to the controller.                                                  1
    Multiple DISPlay subsystems are used to represent independent display medium. A front                2
    panel mounted display and an attached terminal used only for information display are                 3
    examples of independent displays. Conversely, an instrument with many dedicated
    indicators is considered to have one general display because of the dependencies in operation        4
    that exist between the indicators.                                                                   5
    Within a DISPlay, information may be separated into individual WINDows (this is always               6
    the case for instruments with dedicated indicators). Each window is considered to consist of
    three overlapped planes, one each for text, graphics, and trace data. Thus, text, graphics, and      7
    trace information may be presented at the same time in a given window.                               8
    Most of the *RST conditions in the DISPlay subsystem are device-dependent, to                        9
    accommodate for typical display functions that exist for each of the various categories of
    instrumentation.                                                                                    10

                    DISPlay:ANNotation

                    from OFF to ON.
 1
                    The ANNotation parameters are set to ON at *RST, unless SYSTem:SECurity is enabled.
 2
         8.1.1      [:ALL] <Boolean>
 3                  DISPlay:ANNotation:ALL

 4                  Controls ALL of the annotation information.

10       8.2        :BRIGhtness <numeric_value>
                    DISPlay:BRIGhtness
11                  Controls the intensity of the display. The range of the parameter is 0 to 1, where 1 is full
12                  intensity and 0 is fully blanked.

13       8.3        :CMAP
                    DISPlay:CMAP
14                  The CMAP subsystem controls the physical color associated with logical color numbers in
15                  the color map of the display. On a monochrome DISPlay, the CMAP may be used to
                    represent different intensity levels of the same shade. When a color is redefined, all
16                  information associated with that color number may change immediately.
17                  Two methods are available for defining a particular color, HSL and RGB models. If both are
18                  implemented in a device, then they shall be coupled such that redefining a color with one
                    model shall be reflected in the values of the other model.
19
                    At *RST, COLor[1] shall represent “black,” and COLor2 shall represent “white” or the
20                  actual color of a monochrome display.
21       8.3.1      :DEFault
22                  DISPlay:CMAP:DEFault
                    Sets the color map to the instrument’s default values for all colors, except that COLor[1]
23
                    shall be represent “black,” and COLor2 shall represent “white” or the actual color of a
24                  monochrome display.
25       8.3.2      :COLor
                    DISPlay:CMAP:COLor
26
                    This subsystem controls the color map for the instrument.



         8-4     DISPlay:ANNotation
                                 1999 SCPI Command Reference

8.3.2.1     :HSL <hue>,<sat>,<lum>
          DISPlay:CMAP:COLor:HSL
          The HSL command sets the instrument’s color map based on the Hue/Saturation/Luminance
          levels color model. A query of HSL shall return three <NR2>s separated by commas.
          Hue ranges from zero to one, circularly, with a value of zero resulting in the same hue as a      1
          value of one. The approximate color progression is (starting at zero): red, orange, yellow,
          green, cyan, blue, magenta, and back to red.
                                                                                                            2
          Saturation is the amount of pure color to be mixed with white. The saturation value ranges
                                                                                                            3
          from zero to one, with zero specifying no color (only white or gray, depending on intensity)      4
          and one specifying no white.
                                                                                                            5
          Luminance specifies the brightness per unit area of the color. A luminance of zero results in
          black; a luminance of one results in the brightest color available.
                                                                                                            6
          At *RST, these parameters are set to the DEFault values, equivalent to executing DEFault
                                                                                                            7
          command. The HSL command is coupled to the RGB command. Changing values in either                 8
          will affect the values of the other.
                                                                                                            9
8.3.2.2     :RGB <red>,<green>,<blue>
          DISPlay:CMAP:COLor:RGB                                                                           10
          The RGB command sets the instrument’s color map based on the Red/Green/Blue color                11
          model. A query of RGB shall return three <NR2>s separated by commas.
                                                                                                           12
          Red ranges from zero to one, with zero indicating “no red” and one indicating “full intensity
          red.”
                                                                                                           13
          Green ranges from zero to one, with zero indicating “no green” and one indicating “full
                                                                                                           14
          intensity green.”                                                                                15
          Blue ranges from zero to one, with zero indicating “no blue” and one indicating “full            16
          intensity blue.”
                                                                                                           17
          At *RST, these parameters are set to the DEFault values, equivalent to executing DEFault
                                                                                                           18
          command. The RGB command is coupled to the HSL command. Changing values in either
          will affect the values of the other.                                                             19
8.4       :CONTrast <numeric_value>                                                                        20
          DISPlay:CONTrast
                                                                                                           21
          Determines the relative difference in brightness between “full” intensity and “no” intensity
          as displayed. The parameter ranges in value from 0 to 1; 0 indicates no difference between       22
          data and background, and 1 indicates maximum contrast.                                           23
8.5       :ENABle <Boolean>                                                                                24
          DISPlay:ENABle
                                                                                                           25
          Controls whether the whole display is visible. If SYSTem:SECurity is enabled, DISPlay
          cannot be switched from OFF to ON.                                                               26
          ENABle is set to ON at *RST, unless SYSTem:SECurity is enabled.

         8.7        [:WINDow]
10                  DISPlay:WINDow

11                  The WINDow subtree contains commands to enable a window, to set its size and location,
                    and control its contents. Multiple instances of WINDow may exist under a particular
12                  DISPlay.
13       8.7.1      :BACKground
                    DISPlay:WINDow:BACKground
14
                    This subsystem controls the characteristics of the window background.
15
         8.7.1.1      :COLor <numeric_value>
16                  DISPlay:WINDow:BACKground:COLor

17                  Selects from the CMAP the value given by <numeric_value> to become the background
                    color.
18
         8.7.2      :GEOMetry
19                  DISPlay:WINDow:GEOMetry

20                  This subtree is used to define the position and size of the WINDow with respect to the
                    display. A window may be specified by using any two of LLEFt, URIGht or SIZE
21                  commands, since SIZe = URIGht - LLEFt. If any one of these commands is implemented,
22                  then all three shall be implemented and the coupling between them shall be maintained.

23                  For the GEOMetry subtree, the lower left corner of the whole display is defined to be (0,0);
                    zero in the horizontal direction and zero in the vertical direction. The upper right corner is
24                  defined to be (1,1).
25                  The effect of changing the size or aspect ratio of a WINDow that already is displaying
26                  information is device-dependent. The device may choose to rescale the information to fit the
                    new WINDow or it may leave the information unchanged, clipping it where it exceeds the
                    WINDow boundaries.

         8-6     DISPlay:MENU
                                 1999 SCPI Command Reference

8.7.2.1     :LLEFt <numeric_value>,<numeric_value>
          DISPlay:WINDow:GEOMetry:LLEFt

          to 1.
8.7.2.2     :SIZE <numeric_value>,<numeric_value>                                                              1
          DISPlay:WINDow:GEOMetry:SIZE
          This specifies (or queries) the size of the display window. The first parameter represents the
                                                                                                               2
          length in the horizontal direction, and the second parameter represents the length in the            3
          vertical direction.
                                                                                                               4
          The parameters may be set in the range greater than zero to 1. Where the existence of a
          window can be represented by an icon, the device shall accept SIZE 0,0 to indicate the
                                                                                                               5
          window is to be replaced by an icon.                                                                 6
          If a window is represented by an icon, any valid SIZE command with non-zero parameters               7
          shall reset the size of the window, and shall cause the icon to be replaced by the window.
                                                                                                               8
8.7.2.3     :URIGht <numeric_value>,<numeric_value>
          DISPlay:WINDow:GEOMetry:URIGht                                                                       9

         8.7.3.4      [:DRAW] <numeric_value>,<numeric_value>
                    DISPlay:WINDow:GRAPhics:DRAW
                    Draws a line from the current “pen” position to the specified X and Y coordinate (the first
                    parameter is X, the second is Y; both parameters are required). The current line type and pen
                    number are used.
 1
         8.7.3.5      :PCL <block>
 2                  DISPlay:WINDow:GRAPhics:PCL
 3                  Graphics and text data are sent to the instrument using Hewlett-Packard “<esc>*” terminal-
                    and printer-style escape sequences. These are described in the Hewlett-Packard “Printer
 4                  Command Language” document. Some escape sequences may interact with global
 5                  parameters such as color selection. The effect of these changes is global in scope and not
                    restricted to the :GRAPhics subsystem.
 6
         8.7.3.6      :HPGL <block>
 7                  DISPlay:WINDow:GRAPhics:HPGL
     8              Graphics and text data are sent to the instrument using HP-GL (Hewlett-Packard-Graphics
                    Language) plotter language. Some HP-GL sequences will interact with global parameters
 9                  such as color selection; the effect of these changes is global in scope and not restricted to the
10                  :GRAPhics subsystem.
11       8.7.3.7      :IDRaw <numeric_value>,<numeric_value>
                    DISPlay:WINDow:GRAPhics:IDRaw
12                  Draws a line from the current pen position to a new position determined by adding an X

                    DISPlay:WINDow:GRAPhics:IMOVe
15                  Updates the current pen position by adding an X offset (first parameter) and a Y offset
16                  (second parameter) to the current coordinates. No line is drawn.
17       8.7.3.9      :LABel <string>
                    DISPlay:WINDow:GRAPhics:LABel
18                  Places text on the graphics display at the current pen position, using the current pen, with the

                    DISPlay:WINDow:GRAPhics:LDIRection
21                  Defines the angle (in radians) at which labels are drawn. An angle of 0 is normal horizontal
22                  printing. The angle increases counter-clockwise; PI/2 is bottom-to-top.
23       8.7.3.11     :LTYPe <numeric_value>[,<numeric_value>]
                    DISPlay:WINDow:GRAPhics:LTYPe

26
                    dashes.

           The TEXT subtree allows for the display of textual information in the WINDow. For                     8
           example, it allows direct control of the WINDow by the controller, using it as a VDT (Visual
           Display Terminal) output device.
                                                                                                                 9
           For the TEXT subtree, the upper left corner of the WINDow is defined to be (1,1). The lower
                                                                                                                10
           right corner is dependent on the WINDow:SIZE and the TEXT:Character SIZE selected.                   11
8.7.5.1      :ATTRibutes <Boolean>                                                                              12
           DISPlay:WINDow:TEXT:ATTRibutes
           ATTRibutes allows the device to interpret the ANSI Standard Terminal escape sequences
                                                                                                                13
           when displaying TEXT:DATA. Escape sequences that generate an inquiry are not permitted.              14
           The device may absorb escape sequences that it cannot interpret to prevent them from
           appearing on the display.
                                                                                                                15
           If ATTRibutes is ON, escape sequences embedded in the data are used to control the
                                                                                                                16
           attributes of the string, such as blinking, or underline. ATTRibutes set to OFF disables the         17
           interpretation of display sequences, but does not affect the current display. A blinking
                                                                                                                18
           display keeps on blinking until it is overwritten. The device may absorb the escape
           sequences to prevent them from appearing on the display.                                             19
8.7.5.2      :CLEar                                                                                             20
           DISPlay:WINDow:TEXT:CLEar
                                                                                                                21
           Erases the text from the WINDow.
                                                                                                                22
           This command defines an event, and therefore has no query form or *RST value.
                                                                                                                23
8.7.5.3      :COLor <numeric_value>
           DISPlay:WINDow:TEXT:COLor                                                                            24
           Selects from the CMAP the value given by <numeric_value> to become the color for the
                                                                                                                25
           next DATA stream.
                                                                                                                26

         8.7.6.6       :X
                     DISPlay:WINDow:TRACe:X
                     This subsystem controls the setting of the X axis. The X axis is displayed horizontally, and it
                     is usually the independent variable of the data, such as time or frequency. The :X node is
                     used to define the parameters associated with the X axis. It is only available when the format
 1                   of the data is Cartesian.
 2       8.7.6.6.1     :LABel <string>
 3                   DISPlay:WINDow:TRACe:X:LABel
                     Specifies custom axis labeling.
 4
         8.7.6.6.2     [:SCALe]
 5                   DISPlay:WINDow:TRACe:X:SCALe                                                                      HP006




 6                   The SCALe subtree is used to define which portion of the (TRACe) data is to be displayed,
                     by defining the end points of the axis as they appear in the WINDow. The values are in the
 7                   same UNITs as the UNIT of data for the x axis. The x scale can be defined in terms of
     8               CENTer, LEFT, RIGHt and/or PDIVision, where the following equations express the
                     relationship of these parameters:
 9                           RIGHt - LEFT = (RIGHt - CENTer) * 2 = PDIVision * # of graticule divisions.
10                   If an instrument implements x axis scaling, the commands RIGHt and LEFT must be
11                   implemented, while implementing PDIVision and CENTer are optional.
12       8.7.6.6.2.1    :AUTO <Boolean> | ONCE
                     DISPlay:WINDow:TRACe:X:SCALe:AUTO
13
                                                                                                                       HP004




                     The AUTO ON command sets the display to always configure the scaling on the particular
14                   axis to best display the data. This rescaling may affect the values of any of the parameters
                     under the SCALe node. When AUTO is ON the display may be rescaled after each
15                   measurement or sweep. Setting AUTO to ONCE, turns auto ON, adjusting the scaling of the
16                   axis for one measurement and then turns auto OFF. Turning AUTO ON can change any of
                     the parameters which can be set under the SCALe node.
17
                     At *RST AUTO is set to OFF.
18
         8.7.6.6.2.2    :CENTer <numeric_value>
19                   DISPlay:WINDow:TRACe:X:SCALe:CENTer                                                               HP006




20                   Set or queries the value represented by the center point of the x-axis. This value may be
                     bounded by the range of the data. When a new CENTer value is entered, the PDIVision
21                   value is kept constant and the RIGHT and LEFT values are changed.
22                   At *RST, this parameter value is device dependent.
23
         8.7.6.6.2.3    :LEFT <numeric_value>
24                   DISPlay:WINDow:TRACe:X:SCALe:LEFT                                                                 HP006




                     Set or queries the value represented by the minimum (left) edge of the x-axis. This value
25
                     may be bounded by the range of the data. When a new LEFT value is entered, the PDIVision
26                   value is kept constant and the CENTer and RIGHT values are changed.
                     At *RST, this parameter value is device dependent.

         8-12   DISPlay[:WINDow]
                                   1999 SCPI Command Reference

            DISPlay:WINDow:TRACe:X:SCALe:PDIVision                                                                   HP006




            Set or query the value between two grid graticules (value “per division”). When a new
            PDIVision value is entered, the parameter set as the PDIVision:LINK is held constant and
            the other two are changed.
                                                                                                                 1
            At *RST, this parameter value is device dependent.
                                                                                                                 2
8.7.6.6.2.4.1      :LINK LEFT | CENTer | RIGHt
            DISPlay:WINDow:TRACe:X:SCALe:PDIVision:LINK                                                          3   HP006




            LINK selects the parameter, either CENTer, LEFT or RIGHt that shall not be changed when              4
            the PDIVision value is changed. For example, if LINK is set to LEFT, then changing
            PDIVision shall cause CENTer and RIGHt, not LEFT, to change.                                         5
            At *RST the value of LINK is device dependent.                                                       6

9     FORMat Subsystem
      The FORMat subsystem sets a data format for transferring numeric and array information.
      This data format is used for both command and response data by those commands that are
      specifically designated to be affected by the FORMat subsystem. The designation is either
      given as part of a command description, or in the definition of block or array data used by a        1
      command. The data format for command data may override the definition of FORMat if the               2
      data received is self typing (indicates its type), for the duration of that data transfer.
                                                                                                           3
      KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                                NOTES
      FORMat                                                                                               4
         :BORDer             NORMal|SWAPped                                                                5
        [:DATA]              <type> [,<length>]
         :DINTerchange       <Boolean>                                                                     6
         :SREGister          ASCii | BINary | HEXadecimal | OCTal                            1992          7  PH066




9.1   :BORDer NORMal|SWAPped                                                                               8
      FORMat:READings:BORDer
                                                                                                           9
      Byte ORDer. Controls whether binary data is transferred in normal or swapped byte order.
                                                                                                          10
      At *RST, this value is set to NORMal.
                                                                                                          11
9.2   [:DATA] <type>[,<length>]
      FORMat:READings:DATA
                                                                                                          12
      The DATA command selects the data format; the <type> and type <length>. Valid types are             13
                                                                                                          TK055
      ASCii, INTeger, UINTeger, REAL, HEXadecimal, OCTal, BINary, and PACKed. The
                                                                                                          14
      <length> parameter is optional for all types; its meaning is dependent on the type selected.
                                                                                                          15
      The <length> parameter is an <NRf>. In the query response <length> is returned as <NR1>.            TK033
                                                                                                          16
      If the type INTeger, UINTeger, REAL, or PACKed is selected the data is transferred in a             TK055
      block. The types ASCii, HEXadecimal, OCTal, and BINary are self typing. That is, the                17
      syntax designates the type. In these cases, the FORMat subsystem is only necessary to
                                                                                                          18
      determine the output format.
                                                                                                          19
      At *RST, ASCii is selected as the default type, the type length is device-dependent.
                                                                                                          20
      The various types are defined as:
                                                                                                          21
      <type>          Interpretation:
                                                                                                          22
      ASCii           Numeric data is transferred as ASCii bytes in <NR1>, <NR2> or <NR3>
                      format, as appropriate. The numbers are separated by commas as specified            23
                      in IEEE 488.2. Forgiving listening allows ASCii input to always be valid.
                                                                                                          24
                      The optional <length> parameter specifies the number of significant digits to
                      be returned.                                                                        25
                      A <length> value of zero indicates that the device selects the number of            26
                                                                                                          TK033
                      significant digits to be returned. When a <length> of zero has been


                                                                           FORMat:BORDer            9-1
                                        1999 SCPI Command Reference

                                  specified, the FORMat[:DATA]? query shall return zero as its second
                                  parameter.
                  BINary          Data is encoded as a non-decimal numeric, base 2, preceded by “#B” as
                                  specified in IEEE 488.2. The <length> parameter is the number of binary
 1                                digits in each number (not including the “#B”).
 2                HEXadecimal Data is encoded as a non-decimal numeric, base 16, preceded by “#H” as
                              specified in IEEE 488.2. The <length> parameter is the number of
 3                            hexadecimal digits in each number (not including the “#H”).
 4                INTeger         Data is transferred in a definite length block as signed integers of the length
 5                                specified (in bits; default is 16). Scaling and offset, if required for
                                  interpretation of measurement data, are determined by measurement
 6                                parameters set in some other subsystem. Valid values of <length> for
 7                                INTeger data are 8, 16 and 32.
 8                OCTal           Data is encoded as a non-decimal numeric, base 8, preceded by “#Q” as
                                  specified in IEEE 488.2. The <length> parameter is the number of octal
     9                            digits in each number (not including the “#Q”).
10                PACKed          Data is transferred in a definite length block, in a manner specified in the
11                                device documentation. The <length> parameter may be used to convey
                                  additional information about the device-dependent format.
12
                  REAL            Data is transferred in a definite length block as IEEE 754 floating point
13                                numbers of the specified length (in bits; default is 64). Valid values of
14                                <length> for REAL data are 32 and 64.
15                UINTeger        Data is transferred in a definite length block as unsigned integers of the        TK055
                                  length specified (in bits; default is 16). Scaling and offset, if required for
16                                interpretation of measurement data, are determined by measurement
17                                parameters set in some other subsystem. Valid values of <length> for
                                  UINTeger data are 8, 16, 32 and 64.
18
19       9.3      :DINTerchange <Boolean>
                  FORMat:READings:DINTerchange                                                                       DIF01
20                Determines whether measurement data is formatted as a <dif_expression>. See Data
21                Interchange Format, Volume 3. When DINTerchange ON is selected, returned data is
                  encapsulated in this structure.
22
                  The commands which are affected by this switch are a device dependent subset of those             TK032a
23                affected by the FORMat:DATA command, but at a minimum shall include SENSe:DATA?,
24                CALCulate:DATA?, TRACe:DATA?, MEASure?, READ?, and FETCh?
25                The DIF encoding format for its DATA(CURVe(VALues)) block follows that specified in               TK032a
                  FORMat[:DATA] and FORMat:BORDer.
26
                  At *RST this function is set to OFF.


         9-2   FORMat:DINTerchange
                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

9.4   :SREGister ASCii | BINary | HEXadecimal | OCTal
      FORMat:SREGister                                                                                 PH066




      This command selects the data type of the response to queries for any CONDition, EVENt
      and ENABle register and for PTRansition and NTRansition filters that belong to the status
      subsystem. Note that this includes the IEEE 488.2 status register queries.
                                                                                                   1
      ASCii           The data is transferred as ASCii bytes in <NR1> format. This argument is
                      required if the command is implemented.                                      2
      BINary          The data is encoded as non-decimal numeric, base 2, preceded by ‘#B’ as      3
                      specified in IEEE 488.2                                                      4
      HEXadecimal The data is encoded as non-decimal numeric, base 16, preceded by ‘#H’ as         5
                  specified in IEEE 488.2
                                                                                                   6
      OCTal           The data is encoded as non-decimal numeric, base 8, preceded by ‘#Q’ as
                      specified in IEEE 488.2                                                      7
      At *RST, ASCii is selected as the default response data type.                                8

         9-4   FORMat:SREGister
                            1999 SCPI Command Reference


10   HCOPy                                                                                             HP063e
     The Hard COPy subsystem controls the setup of plotting and printing to an external device.
     The Hard COPy subsystem does not perform any data formatting, that is it does not convert
     the data from one representation to another, such as COMPlex to POLar. Instead HCOPy
     adds the necessary page formatting (dependent upon the hard copy device language) to turn          1
     the data into an acceptable form for the hard copy device.                                         2
     The HCOPy subsystem may FEED data from SENSe or CALCulate, and this data may be                    3
     printed or plotted. A FEED may be established from a DISPlay:WINDow. In this case the
     HCOPy output shall reflect what is currently displayed in that WINDow. In particular, any          4
     scaling and offset that applies shall be employed.                                                 5
     The selection of the interface and any address information is accomplished in the                  6
     SYSTem:COMMunicate subsystem. DATA may be streamed to an external device without
     sending it through the HCOPy subsystem, where no page formatting commands are needed.              7
     The HCOPy subsystem gives a user several ways to select and initiate a plot or print. A user       8
     may request all aspects of the data be plotted or printed, or the user may select a subset that    9
     is of interest.
                                                                                                       10
     The ITEM subsystem provides the means to select the desired aspects of the data in one of
     two ways. First, the ITEM of interest can be directly plotted or printed. For example, the        11
     TRACe data can be plotted or printed immediately by using the                                     12
     HCOPy:ITEM:...:IMMediate command or the HCOPy:ITEM:...:DATA? query.
     Alternatively, the user may set the STATe to ON for all the ITEMs of interest, and then use       13
     the HCOPy:IMMediate command or the HCOPy:DATA? query to plot or print the selected                14
     items in one transaction with the hard copy device.
                                                                                                       15
     If the user wishes to plot or print all the data, pointed to by the FEED, and does not want to
     individually initiate each ITEM or change each ITEM’s STATe to ON, the user can send the          16
     HCOPy:ITEM:ALL[:IMMediate] command or the HCOPy:ITEM:ALL:DATA? query.                             17
     The :HCOPy:SDUMp:IMMediate command and the :HCOPy:SDUMp:DATA? query allow                         18
     the user to do a Screen DUMp of the whole DISPlay, mimicking the traditional role of a
     camera recorder, and provide a simple hard copy scheme for instruments with a DISPlay.            19
     The HCOPy subsystem provides two schemes, IMMediate and DATA?, for getting hard                   20
     copy data out of an instrument. First, all of the IMMediate events can be implemented and         21
     used where the instrument is capable of directly controlling the interface. For example,
     RS-232, Centronics, or GPIB where the instrument can talk directly to the hard copy device        22
     by becoming the active controller. Any instrument which requires control of the system            23
     interface to execute the IMMediate command shall also implement the *PCB common
     command, see IEEE 488.2 10.21.                                                                    24
     IMMediate can also be used on GPIB when the active controller addresses the instrument to         25
     talk and the hard copy device to listen while monitoring the data flow by shadow                  26
     handshaking. The format of the data sent in response to an IMMediate command is not
     necessarily an IEEE 488.2 format. This behavior is allowed by IEEE 488.2 section 8.1.

                                                                                     HCOPy      10-1
                                        1999 SCPI Command Reference


                    WARNING:
                    The IEEE 488.2 message exchange protocol requirements are violated when the
                    IMMediate command generates a response that is sent when the instrument is addressed
                    to talk. The instrument shall revert to the normal message exchange protocol if it
 1                  receives a device clear or any data on the system interface. Designers should use the
 2                  control passing method rather than shadow handshaking method to avoid this escape of
                    the IEEE 488.2 message exchange protocol.
 3
 4                Second, the DATA? query exists for use on buses, such as GPIB, where the data flow from
                  the instrument to the hard copy device by way of a separate controller is acceptable or
 5                necessary. It is also useful when the controller wants to store formatted data for later use.
 6                The instrument returns the formatted data in an <INDEFINITE LENGTH ARBITRARY
                  RESPONSE DATA> element, see IEEE 488.2 section 8.7.10. This response data element
 7                has a leading #0 and a trailing NL^END. The controller could strip the header and trailer and
 8                send the remainder to an appropriate printer or plotter. The indefinite form is used because
                  the block’s size or nature may prevent the instrument from computing the block’s length
 9                until after it is sent.
     10           A device may implement IMMediate or DATA? or both of these forms to plot or print
11                results.
12                The result from HCOPy can also be fed to the Mass MEMory subsystem. The user could
                  then retreive the results from the stored files at a more convenient time.

          10.1     :ABORt
16                 Hard COPy:ABORt

17                 Abort the current hard copy operation. A new program message automatically aborts any
                   incomplete response from an :HCOPy:...:DATA? query as that is an INTERRUPTED
18                 condition.
19        10.2     :DATA?
                   Hard COPy:DATA?
20
                   This query initiates the plot or print according to the current Hard COPy setup parameters.
21                 All of the items under the ITEM node which are turned ON (STATe ON) are encapsulated in
22                 an <INDEFINITE LENGTH ARBITRARY RESPONSE DATA> element.
          10.3     :DESTination<data_handle>
23                 Hard COPy:DESTination
24                 An event which sets all :FEED connections which had been set to “HCOPy” to “”. The
                   :FEED connection pointed to by <data handle> is set to “HCOPy”. Any <data_handle>
25
                   which can be used as a parameter to :DESTination shall have a :FEED command under it
26                 which can be set to “HCOPy”.
