10.4       :DEVice
           Hard COPy:DEVice
           This subsystem is used to set and query characteristics relating to the hard copy device and
           its output.
10.4.1     :CMAP                                                                                             1
           Hard COPy:DEVice:CMAP
           The CMAP subsystem controls the physical color associated with logical color numbers in           2
           the color map of the display. On a monochrome DISPlay, the CMAP may be used to                    3
           represent different intensity levels of the same shade. When a color is redefined, all
           information associated with that color number may change immediately.                             4
           Two methods are available for defining a particular color, HSL and RGB models. If both are        5
           implemented in a device, then they shall be coupled such that redefining a color with one         6
           model shall be reflected in the values of the other model.
                                                                                                             7
           At *RST, COLor[1] shall represent “black,” and COLor2 shall represent “white” or the
           actual color of a monochrome display.                                                             8
10.4.1.1    :COLor                                                                                           9
           Hard COPy:DEVice:CMAP:COLor
                                                                                                            10
           This subsystem controls the color map for the instrument.
                                                                                                            11
10.4.1.1.1 :HSL <hue>,<sat>,<lum>
           Hard COPy:DEVice:CMAP:COLor:HSL                                                                  12
           The HSL command sets the instrument’s color map based on the Hue/Saturation/Luminance            13
           levels color model. A query of HSL shall return three <NR2>s separated by commas.
                                                                                                            14
           Hue ranges from zero to one, circularly, with a value of zero resulting in the same hue as a
           value of one. The approximate color progression is (starting at zero): red, orange, yellow,      15
           green, cyan, blue, magenta, and back to red.                                                     16
           Saturation is the amount of pure color to be mixed with white. The saturation value ranges       17
           from zero to one, with zero specifying no color (only white or gray, depending on intensity)
           and one specifying no white.                                                                     18
           Luminance specifies the brightness per unit area of the color. A luminance of zero results in    19
           black; a luminance of one results in the brightest color available.                              20
           At *RST, these parameters are set to the DEFault values, equivalent to executing DEFault         21
           command. The HSL command is coupled to the RGB command. Changing values in either
           will affect the values of the other.                                                             22
10.4.1.1.2 :RGB <red>,<green>,<blue>                                                                        23
           Hard COPy:DEVice:CMAP:COLor:RGB                                                                  24
           The RGB command sets the instrument’s color map based on the Red/Green/Blue color
           model. A query of RGB shall return three <NR2>s separated by commas.                             25
           Red ranges from zero to one, with zero indicating “no red” and one indicating “full intensity    26
           red.”


                                                                                 HCOPy:DEVice        10-5
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

                     Green ranges from zero to one, with zero indicating “no green” and one indicating “full
                     intensity green.”
                     Blue ranges from zero to one, with zero indicating “no blue” and one indicating “full
                     intensity blue.”
 1                   At *RST, these parameters are set to the DEFault values, equivalent to executing DEFault
 2                   command. The RGB command is coupled to the HSL command. Changing values in either
                     will affect the values of the other.
 3
          10.4.1.2    :DEFault
 4                   Hard COPy:DEVice:CMAP:DEFault
 5                   Sets the color map to the instrument’s default values for all colors, except that COLor[1]
                     shall be represent “black,” and COLor2 shall represent “white” or the actual color of a
 6                   monochrome display.
 7        10.4.2     :COLor <Boolean>
 8                   Hard COPy:DEVice:COLor
                     Sets or queries whether color information should be sent as part of the plot or print
 9                   information, in those languages that support both color and monochrome (black and white).
     10              At *RST, the value of this parameter is OFF.
11        10.4.3     :LANGuage PCL[<n>] | HPGL[<n>] | POSTscript[<n>]
12                   Hard COPy:DEVice:LANGuage
                     Selects the control language or data format to be used when sending out plot or print
13                   information.
14                   PCL             Hewlett-Packard’s Printer Control Language.
15                   HPGL            Hewlett-Packard’s Graphics Language.
16                                   Information about PCL and HPGL is available by contacting:
17                                        HP Peripheral Developer Program
                                          16399 West Bernardo Drive
18                                        San Diego, CA 92127-1899
19                                        (619) 487-4100
20                   POSTscript      Adobe Systems printer language.
21                                   Information about PostScript is available by contacting:
                                          Adobe Systems Incorporated
22                                        1585 Charleston Road
23                                        Mountain View, CA 94039-7900
                                          (415) 961-4400
24
                     The optional number, [<n>], following the languages, refers to a specific version of that
25
                     language.
26
                     At *RST, the value of this parameter is device dependent.

10.4.4     :MODE TABLe | GRAPh
           Hard COPy:DEVice:MODE
           Sets or queries how the data is to be represented in the hard copy. TABLe implies the data is
           formatted into a table rather than a pictorial form. Only characters appear on the output.
           GRAPh implies the format is a graph or picture. The graph may be generated using vectors,
           raster, or other available technology.
                                                                                                               1
           At *RST, the value of this setting is device dependent.
                                                                                                               2
10.4.5     :RESolution <numeric_value>
                                                                                                               3
           Hard COPy:DEVice:RESolution                                                                         4
           Sets or queries the resolution of the result on the hard copy device. This setting is generally
           used to affect the quality of the output from a raster printer.
                                                                                                               5
           At *RST, the value of this parameter is device dependent.
                                                                                                               6
10.4.5.1    :UNIT <SUFFIX PROGRAM DATA>
                                                                                                               7
           Hard COPy:DEVice:RESolution:UNIT                                                                    8
           Sets or queries the units of the RESolution setting.
                                                                                                               9
           At *RST, the value of this parameter is device dependent.
                                                                                                              10
10.4.6     :SPEed <numeric_value>
           Hard COPy:DEVice:SPEed                                                                             11
           Sets or queries the speed at which vectors are drawn. This setting is generally used to affect     12
           the quality of the output from a pen plotter.
                                                                                                              13
           At *RST, the value of this parameter is device dependent.
                                                                                                              14
10.4.6.1    :UNIT <SUFFIX PROGRAM DATA>
           Hard COPy:DEVice:SPEed:UNIT                                                                        15
           Sets or queries the units of the SPEed setting.                                                    16
           At *RST, the value of this parameter is cm/sec.                                                    17
10.5       :FEED <data_handle>                                                                                18
           Hard COPy:FEED
           Sets or queries the data flow to be fed into the Hard COPy block.                                  19
           At *RST, the value of this parameter is device dependent.                                          20
10.6       [:IMMediate]                                                                                       21
           Hard COPy:IMMediate
                                                                                                              22
           This command immediately initiates the plot or print according to the current Hard COPy
           setup parameters. All of the items under the ITEM node which are turned ON (STATe ON)              23
           are plotted or printed.                                                                            24
10.7       :ITEM
           Hard COPy:ITEM
                                                                                                              25
           The :ITEM subsystem collects together commands to configure what items of data will be             26
           plotted or printed, and how that data shall appear.


                                                                  HCOPy:FEED <data_handle>             10-7
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

                     Most data item nodes have :COLor nodes to allow the user to set the color of the specific
                     data item. The parameter to the COLor node selects either the actual pen number of the
                     hardcopy device, or the color map number, whichever value the hardcopy device expects.
                     Some devices may elect not to support some or all of the COLor nodes. For example, a
                     device which has a color DISPlay may elect to use just the existing colors in the DISPlay
 1                   when plotting or printing a color hardcopy.
 2        10.7.1     :ALL
 3                   Hard COPy:ITEM:ALL
                     This subsystem is used to plot or print all ITEMs.

10.8       :PAGE                                                                                              16

           This subsystem contains commands to set up parameters relating to the medium of the plot
           or print output.                                                                                   18
10.8.1     :DIMensions                                                                                        19
           Hard COPy:PAGE:DIMensions
                                                                                                              20
           Sets the plot or print dimensions. Different plotters or printers allow the user to set the page
           dimensions in different ways, such as length, width dimensions of the page, selecting a            21
           standard page size, or setting “corners” of the page in terms of plotter units (that is p1 and     22
           p2). A device will likely support the setting of plot or print dimensions in a subset of these
           ways, depending on which plotter or printer(s) it supports. The interaction of the various         23
           dimension commands is device dependent.                                                            24
10.8.1.1    :AUTO <Boolean>                                                                                   25
           Hard COPy:PAGE:DIMensions:AUTO
           When AUTO is on the device selects the default page dimensions. When AUTO is OFF the               26
           page dimensions are set by the other setting in this subsystem.

11.1     :ATTenuation <numeric_value>                                                                     7
         INPut:ATTenuation
                                                                                                          8
         Sets the input ATTenuation. The default units are in the current relative amplitude units.
                                                                                                          9
         This should only be used where the setting is not reflected within the SENSe system. For
         example, setting the input attenuation to 10 dB will cause the measured signal to decrease in   10
         amplitude by 10 dB.                                                                             11
         This setting is not coupled to INPut:GAIN. If both ATTenuation and GAIN were set to 10          12
         dB, the net result would be a signal of the original amplitude.
                                                                                                         13
         At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
                                                                                                         14
11.1.1   :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
         INPut:ATTenuation:AUTO                                                                          15
         AUTO ON changes the ATTenuation to achieve maximum sensitivity without overloading              16
         the input channel. Programming a specified ATTenuation sets AUTO OFF.
                                                                                                         17
         At *RST, this value is set to ON.
                                                                                                         18
11.1.2   :STATe <Boolean>                                                                                RS013
         INPut:ATTenuation:STATe                                                                         19
         Turns the input attenuator ON and OFF. OFF means, that any attenuation circuits are taken       20
         out of the signal path, thus, no distortion to the signal will happen.
                                                                                                         21
         At *RST, this value is device dependent.
                                                                                                         22

11.4       :FILTer
           INPut:FILTer
           The FILTer function allows a filter to be inserted in the path of the measurement signal. The
           FREQuency function allows the programming of a specific break frequency. The STATe
           command enables the filter.
                                                                                                            1
11.4.1     :AWEighting
           INPut:FILTer:AWEighting                                                                          2   HP036




           Controls the “A” weighting input filter. This is a human hearing compensation filter             3
           described in the IEC Recommendation 179 and ANSI S1.4.
                                                                                                            4
11.4.1.1     [:STATe] <Boolean>
           INPut:FILTer:AWEighting:STATe                                                                    5   HP036




           Turns the “A” weighting input filter on and off.                                                 6
           At *RST this value is device-dependent.                                                          7

                                                                                                           11

                                                                                                           12
           At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
                                                                                                           13
11.4.2.2     [:STATe] <Boolean>
           INPut:FILTer:HPASs:STATe                                                                        14

          11.5       :GAIN <numeric_value>
                     INPut:GAIN
                     Sets the input GAIN. The default units are in the current relative amplitude units.
                     This should only be used where the setting is not reflected within the SENSe system. For
 1                   example, setting the input gain to 10 dB will cause the measured signal to increase in
                     amplitude by 10 dB.
 2
                     This setting is not coupled to INPut:ATTenuation. If both ATTenuation and GAIN were set
 3                   to 10 dB, the net result would be a signal of the original amplitude.
 4                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.

                     INPut:GAIN:AUTO

                     AUTO ON changes the GAIN to achieve maximum sensitivity without overloading the input
 7                   channel.

 9        11.5.2     :STATe <Boolean>                                                                                  RS013
                     INPut:GAIN:STATe
10
                     Turns the input gain (preamplifier) ON and OFF. OFF means, that any preamplifier circuits
     11              are taken out of the signal path, thus, no distortion to the signal will happen. OFF is not the
12                   same as INPut:GAIN 0 dB, because an isolation preamplifier will have that gain.

13                   At *RST, this value is device dependent.

11.9     :OFFSet <numeric_value>
         INPut:OFFSet                                                                                          TWOS01




         Sets or queries the input OFFSet. OFFSet may take on positive and negative values. The
         OFFSet shall be subtracted from the input, thus making OFFSet more positive shall make the
         signal more negative. The default units are in the current amplitude units
                                                                                                            1
         Introducing an OFFSet in the input has the effect of offsetting the input signal, prior to
         detection in the SENSe block. Any offset introduced in the input block shall not be corrected      2
         for in the sensor and subsquently the sensor results. For example, if the current amplitude        3
         units are in volts, a value of 5 shall decrease the input signal by 5 volts.
                                                                                                            4
         At *RST, the value of OFFSet is device-dependent.
                                                                                                            5
11.9.1   :STATe <Boolean>
         INPut:OFFSet:STATe                                                                                 6  TWOS01




         Turns the effect of OFFSet ON or OFF.                                                              7
         At *RST, STATe shall be OFF.                                                                       8
11.10    :POLarity NORMal|INVerted                                                                         TK019
                                                                                                            9
         INPut:POLarity
         Sets or queries the input polarity. NORMal causes the input signal to pass through the INPut     10
         block without inversion. INVerted causes the polarity of the input signal to be reversed. Any    11
         inversion introduced in the INPut block shall not be corrected for in the sensor and
         subsequently the sensor results.                                                                 12
         At *RST, this value is NORMal.                                                                   13
11.11    :POLarization <numeric_value>                                                                    14
                                                                                                          RS010a
         INPut:POLarization
                                                                                                          15
         Sets the polarization of the input. The default units are radian.
                                                                                                          16
         At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
                                                                                                          17
11.11.1 :HORizontal                                                                                       RS010a
         INPut:POLarization:HORizontal                                                                    18
         Sets the polarization of the input to zero. This command is an event. Therefore it has no        19
         associated query or meaning at *RST.

12       INSTrument Subsystem
         An instrument may support multiple logical instruments. A dual channel power supply for
         example is considered as two logical instruments. The logical instruments are not required to
         have identical functionality, nor does the functionality have to be available simultaneously.
         The INSTrument subsystem provides a mechanism to identify and select logical instruments            1
         by either name or number. In this way a particular logical instrument could be selected and it      2
         would respond to commands, such as MEASure, in the same manner as a dedicated
         instrument having the same functionality as the logical instrument. The INSTrument                  3
         identifiers have no fixed correspondence to the numeric suffixes allowed with command               4
         headers.
                                                                                                             5
         KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                              NOTES
         INSTrument                                                                                          6
            :CATalog?                                                        [query only]        1994       TK026
                                                                                                             7
               :FULL?                                                        [query only]        1994       TK026
            :COUPle                                                                                          8
               [:<subsystem>]     ALL|NONE|<list>                                                            9
            :DEFine                                                                            1999
               :GROup            <identifier>,<identifier_list>                                1999         10
               [:NAME]           <identifier>,<numeric_value>                                  1999         11
            :DELete                                                                            1999         TK026
              [:NAME]            <identifier>                                [event; no query] 1994         12

12.1     :CATalog?                                                                                          16
                                                                                                            TK026
         INSTrument:CATalog?                                                                                17
         The CATalog query returns a comma-separated list of strings which contains the names of
         all logical instruments and groups. If no logical instruments are defined, a single null string    18
         is returned.                                                                                       19
         Some instruments may have one or more intrinsic (permanent) <identifier>’s. These are              20
                                                                                                            TK026
         listed along with any user-named <identifier>’s.
                                                                                                            21
12.1.1   :FULL?                                                                                             TK026
         INSTrument:CATalog?:FULL?                                                                          22
         CATalog:FULL? query returns a list of string - number pairs. The string contains the name          23
                                                                                                            TK026
         of the logical instrument. The immediately following NR1-formatted number is its
         associated logical instrument number. All response data elements are comma separated. If no        24
         logical instrument is defined, a null string followed by a zero is returned.                       25
         Intrinsic <identifier>’s associated with logical instrument numbers are listed along with any      26
                                                                                                            TK026
         user-named <identifier>’s and numbers.

          12.2       :COUPle[:<subsystem>] ALL|NONE|<list>                                                            TK026
                     INSTrument:COUPle
                     Defines a coupling between various logical instruments or between various channels within
                     an instrument. The COUPle command consists of an optional subsystem node followed by a
 1                   single parameter.

 2                   The subsystem node denotes a SCPI subsection which can either affect each instrument
                     individually, or affect all instruments/channels collectively. This node is used only when the
 3                   user can turn this coupling ON or OFF. Predefined couplings need not use this node. If no
 4                   node follows the COUPle command, then the entire instrument is assumed to be coupled.
                     Coupling a node lower in the tree overrides any couplings which are assigned at a higher
 5                   level.
 6                   The parameter indicates to which logical instruments the specified coupling is to apply. ALL
 7                   indicates that specified coupling is to apply to all logical instruments. NONE indicates that
                     specified coupling is to removed. A list of instruments specifies a particular set of logical
 8                   instruments to be coupled.
 9                   Within SCPI certain subsystems, such as SYSTem, STATus, MEMory, MMEMory, TEST
10                   and DIAGnostic, are considered common to all logical instruments. That is, they appear
                     coupled across all logical instruments, and they cannot be uncoupled. The IEEE common
11                   commands are assumed to always operate on all logical instruments.
     12              At *RST, all subsystems are uncoupled as far as the instrument hardware allows.
13        12.3       :DEFine
                     INSTrument:DEFine
14
          12.3.1     :GROup <identifier>,<identifier_list>
15                   INSTrument:DEFine:GROup
16                   Defines or queries a group of instruments. The <identifier> is character data. The
                     <identifier_list> is a comma-separated list of strings which contains the names of logical
17                   instruments. The defined instruments can be queried using :INSTrument:DEFine:GROup?
18                   <identifier>. No instrument selection is performed by this command. Any instrument
                     implementing the :GROup command shall define which commands are affected by groups.
19
                     When groups are defined and used, and data is set or queried, the following rules shall apply
20                   unless otherwise noted:
21                      When setting a list of values, each value will apply to the corresponding instrument in the
22                      selected group. If the number of values does not correspond to the number of instruments
                        selected, no action is taken and error -115 is reported.
23
                        When a set of values is required by a command, one set of values may be sent for each
24                      instrument in the group. For instance,
25                      FOO a,b;
26                              becomes
                        FOO a1,b1,a2,b2,...

          12-2     INSTrument Subsystem
                                 1999 SCPI Command Reference

            If a single parameter value is supplied for a command that expects one value per group
            member, the value is applied to every instrument in the currently selected group.
            Note that commands that take an arbitrary number of optional parameters need to have
            some way to determine how many parameters apply to each member of the group.
             When queried, the command shall return the value(s) for each instrument in the currently         1
             selected group.                                                                                  2
         When groups are defined and used, events will be sent to all instruments in the currently
         selected group.                                                                                      3
12.3.2   [:NAME] <identifier>,<numeric_value>                                                                 4
         INSTrument:DEFine[:NAME]                                                                             5
         The command form defines a logical instrument name, <identifier>, and associates it with a
         logical instrument number, <numeric_value>. The <identifier> is in character data format.            6
         The query form takes only <identifier> as a parameter and returns the logical instrument             7
         number.                                                                                              8
12.4     :DELete                                                                                              9
         INSTrument:DELete
         The DELete subsystem disassociates <identifier>’s from logical instrument numbers or                10
         groups of instrument <identifier>’s. After the :DELete command executes, the <identifier>           11
         is no longer accessible until it is redefined. The instrument behaves as if the <identifier>
         never existed.                                                                                      12
12.4.1   :ALL                                                                                                13
         INSTrument:DELete:ALL
                                                                                                             14
         This command is an event that disassociates all identifiers from their logical instrument
         numbers or identifier list, except for the currently selected identifier and any intrinsic          15
         identifier definitions. There is no query form.                                                     16
         The situation of “nothing to delete” does not cause an execution error.                             TK026
                                                                                                             17
         This command is an event, and therefore has no *RST value associated with it.                       TK026
                                                                                                             18
         *RST has no effect.                                                                                 TK026
                                                                                                             19
12.4.2   [:NAME] <identifier>                                                                                20
         INSTrument:DELete:NAME
         This command is an event, which disassociates the named <identifier> from its logical               21
         instrument number or identifier list. There is no query form.                                       22
         Attempting to delete the currently selected logical instrument or any intrinsic (permanent)         TK026
                                                                                                             23
         <identifier> - number associations results in an -221, (settings conflict) execution error.
                                                                                                             24
         This command is an event, and therefore has no *RST value associated with it.                       TK026
                                                                                                             25

          12.5     :NSELect <numeric_value>                                                                               JPChange




                   INSTrument:NSELect                                                                                     JPChange




                   This command is used in conjunction with the SELect command. It serves the same purpose,
                   except that it uses a numeric value instead of the identifier used in the SELect command.
                   When queried it shall return the logical instrument number. Note that the numbering used for
 1                 logical instruments shall directly correspond to the numbers used in status reporting for
 2                 multiple instruments; specifically the STATus:QUEStionable:INSTrument and
                   STATus:OPERation:INSTrument commands. By selecting an instrument with either SELect
 3                 or NSELect and querying the selected instrument with the other command, the equivalence
 4                 between the instrument number and identifier can be determined. For example, by selecting
                   a logical instrument using the SELect command with its name identifier and then querying
 5                 which logical instrument is selected with the NSELect command, the corresponding numeric
 6                 value shall be returned.

 7                 Assigning numeric values to logical instrument identifiers is not appropriate for instrument
                   groups. Therefore, NSELect returns an error if a group has been selected.
 8                                                                                                                  HP066,JPChange




 9        12.6     [:SELect] <identifier>
                   INSTrument:SELect
10                 This command selects a path or entire instrument or group as the default. When a logical
11                 instrument or a group is selected, all other logical instruments or groups are unavailable for
                   programming until selected. If group logical identifiers are not used, and either :SELect or
     12            :NSELect commands are implemented, then both of the commands must be implemented.
13                 Character data names may be predefined by the instrument.
14                 At *RST, a device-dependent instrument is selected.
15        12.7     :STATe <Boolean>
                   INSTrument:STATe
16                 Turns the selected logical instrument ON or OFF. A logical instrument does not have to be
17                 turned OFF before another logical instrument is selected. That is, several logical instruments
                   may be active, while only one may be selected. When an instrument is active, measurements
18                 occur and signals are generated. When inactive, measurements do not occur and signals are
19                 not generated. When a logical instrument is selected, yet is inactive, all commands shall be
                   processed so that the logical instrument shall reflect the state changes requested when the
20                 logical instrument is turned on. The exception to this are commands which would normally
21                 cause trigger events in an active logical instrument. Any of these commands shall cause an
                   execution error (-200) to be generated.
22
                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.

          12-4   INSTrument Subsystem
                           1999 SCPI Command Reference


13   MEMory Subsystem
     The purpose of the memory subsystem is to manage instrument memory. This specifically
     excludes memory used for mass storage, which is defined in the MMEMory Subsystem.
     Instrument memory may be used to store several data types (e.g. ASCii, BINary, instrument
     STATe, TRACe or MACRo.) The data types available for a given instrument are                     1
     device-dependent.                                                                               2
     An instrument may support either fixed or dynamic allocation of instrument memory,              3
     between the different data types. With fixed allocation a certain amount of memory is
     dedicated to each of the supported data types. The dedicated memory is unavailable for use      4
     by any other data type. Alternatively, with dynamic allocation, instrument memory is shared     5
     between the various data types supported on a demand basis.
                                                                                                     6
     In the MEMory:TABLe subsystems, many fundamental measurement are defined as
     subnodes below :TABLe, such as MEMory:TABLe:FREQuency, :VOLTage, :POWer, etc.                   7
     These nodes define standardized entries in the table (note that these entries can be            8
     conceptualized as either a column or a row). While it makes sense to define widely used
     entries in the SCPI Volume 2 standard, there is sometimes a desire to standardize very          9
     instrument class specific names. Where instrument class specific names require                 10
     standardization, and little or no overlap is expected with other instrument classes, these
     instrument class specific MEMory:TABLe nodes are defined in the Volume 4, Instrument           11
     classes chapter to which they apply.                                                           12
     As an example, the SCPI commands for Chassis Dynamometers :FORCe :SPEed and TIME               13
     are defined in Volume 2 under :MEMory:TABLe. These are fundamental measurements,
     and might be used by many instruments. However Deceleration RATe is deemed to be               14
     specific to dynamometers and is defined in Volume 4.                                           15

                                                                                                                        HP058A




                   * NOTE: The commands marked with an asterisk query or set values inside of predefined
                   emissions bench memory tables. The tables involved are as follows:
                   Table            Column Name(s)                    Description
                   CPIxxRyy         CPOint,TOLerance,WFACtorWT        Linearization input cut point tables
 1                 GasBottle        BNUMber,CONCentration,LABel       Gas bottle table
                   LSIxxRyy         CPOint,EXPected,RAW,CCURve,NCURve Linearization results tables
 2                 VERify           BNUMber1,BNUMber2,...BNUMber      Verify gas table
 3                 QLIxxRyy         LOG                               Linearization log tables
                   QNIxxRyy         LOG                               NOx efficiency log tables
 4                 SDRift           DFACtory,DLASt,DLINearize         Span Drift results table
 5                 SpanGas          BNUMber1,BNUMber2,...BNUMber      Span Gas table
                   TopGas           BNUMber1,BNUMber2,...BNUMber      Top Gas table
 6                 ZDRift           DFACtory,DLASt,DLINearize         Zero Drift results table
 7                 ZeroGas          BNUMber1,BNUMber2,...BNUMber      Zero Gas table
 8                 The <name> parameter is used to define a user label, which shall be <character program
 9                 data>. This label can then be used by the application in place of the specified data defined
                   here or in other subsystems. The <name> parameter is sent as <character data>, rather than
10                 as a string, because that is the simplest IEEE 488.2 type that meets the requirements. When a
11                 name is returned, for example, in response to a CATalog? query, it must be sent as <string
                   response data>, so that a null string (“”) can indicate that nothing is defined.
12
                   The MEMory capabilities of an instrument are not part of the instrument state and are not
     13            affected by *RST or *RCL. They may survive a power cycle, but this capability is optional.
14                 If the instrument implements SYSTem:SECure mode, MEMory:DELete:ALL must be
                   executed when SYSTem:SEC OFF is executed.
15
          13.1     :CATalog
16                 MEMory:CATalog

17                 The CATalog queries return information on the current contents and state of the instrument’s
                   memory. The returned data shall be in the following form:
18                       <numeric_value>,<numeric_value> {,<string>}
19                 The instrument shall return two numeric parameters and as many strings as there are items in
20                 the directory list. The first parameter shall indicate the total amount of storage currently
                   used, in bytes. The second parameter shall indicate the total amount of storage available, also
21                 in bytes. Each string parameter returned shall indicate the name, type and size of one in the
22                 directory list, thus:
                           <name>,<type>,<size>
23
                   The <name>, <type> and <size> are all character data. The <name> is the exact name of a
24                 file as it appears in the directory list, including an extension if present. The <size> provides
25                 the size of the file in bytes. The <type> is indicated by the name of the major subsystem or
                   one of the following:
26
                              ASCii — An ASCII text file                                                              EdChange




          13-4   MEMory Subsystem
                                 1999 SCPI Command Reference


                    BINary — A binary file
                                                                                                                EdChange




                    MACRo — An instrument macro                                                                 EdChange




                    STATe — An instrument state                                                                 EdChange




                    TABLe — A table of data                                                                 1     HP058A




         The qualified CATalog query for TRACe memory is specified in the TRACe subsystem.                  2
13.1.1   [:ALL]?                                                                                            3
         MEMory:CATalog:ALL?                                                                                4
         If the CATalog query is qualified by the optional ALL node then the query shall return a
         directory list and memory sizes related to all allocatable items in instrument memory. Note        5
         that this includes all allocatable objects, such as trace, etc.                                    6
13.1.2   :ASCii?                                                                                            7
         MEMory:CATalog:ASCii?
         If the CATalog query is qualified by the ASCii node then the query shall return the directory      8
         list related only to ASCii items in instrument memory. The memory usage and availability           9
         parameters shall reflect values that correspond to values for ASCii data. In an instrument that
         has dedicated memory for ASCii data types, values reported shall be different from the total
                                                                                                           10
         given by a CATalog of ALL types.                                                                  11
13.1.3   :BINary?                                                                                          12
         MEMory:CATalog:BINary?
         If the CATalog query is qualified by the BINary node then the query shall return the
                                                                                                           13
         directory list related only to BINary items in instrument memory. The memory usage and            14
         availability parameters shall reflect values that correspond to values for BINary data. In an
         instrument that has dedicated memory for BINary data types, values reported shall be
                                                                                                           15
         different from the total given by a CATalog of ALL types.                                         16
13.1.4   :MACRo?                                                                                           17
         MEMory:CATalog:MACRo?
         If the CATalog query is qualified by the MACRo node then the query shall return the
                                                                                                           18
         directory list related only to MACRo items in instrument memory. The memory usage and             19
         availability parameters shall reflect values that correspond to values for MACRo data. In an
         instrument that has dedicated memory for MACRo data types, values reported shall be
                                                                                                           20
         different from the total given by a CATalog of ALL types.                                         21
13.1.5   :STATe?                                                                                           22
         MEMory:CATalog:STATe?
         If the CATalog query is qualified by the STATe node then the query shall return the
                                                                                                           23
         directory list related only to STATe items in instrument memory. The memory usage and             24
         availability parameters shall reflect values that correspond to values for STATe data. In an
         instrument that has dedicated memory for STATe data types, values reported shall be
                                                                                                           25
         different from the total given by a CATalog of ALL types.                                         26

          13.1.6     :TABLe?
                     MEMory:CATalog:TABLe?                                                                              HP058A




                     If the CATalog query is qualified by the TABLe node then the query shall return the
                     directory list related only to TABLe items in instrument memory. The memory usage and

 1                   an instrument that has dedicated memory for TABLe data types, the values reported shall be

 3        13.2       :CLEar                                                                                         PH076
                     MEMory:CLEar
 4
                     The commands from this subsystem remove the data that is stored in instrument memory.
 5                   This subsystem differs from the DELete subsystem in that CLEar removes the data contents
 6                   but does not affect the memory definitions such as memory type and structure, available
                     space, and the name of the associated instrument memory.
 7
          13.2.1     [:NAME] <name>                                                                                 PH076
 8                   MEMory:CLEar:NAME

 9                   This command is a default node and removes all data from the instrument memory
                     associated with <name>. The NAMe command does not affect the related memory
10                   definitions.
11                   This command is an event with no associated query form and *RST condition.
12        13.2.2     :TABLe                                                                                         PH076
                     MEMory:CLEar:TABLe
     13
                     The CLEar:TABLe command removes the data values from all element lists in the SELected
14                   TABLe. This command does not affect the space and structure of the table as specified with
15                   the table’s DEFine command. Executing a POINts? query for any table element after the
                     CLEar:TABLe command, would return 0.
16
                     This command is an event with no associated query form and *RST condition.
17
          13.3       :COPY                                                                                          PH076
18                   MEMory:COPY

19                   The COPY subsystem copies the data from an existing instrument memory item into another,
                     named memory item.
20
          13.3.1     [:NAME] <name>,<name>                                                                          PH076
21                   MEMory:COPY:NAME

22                   This command is a default node that copies the data contents from the memory item
                     associated with the <name> specified in the first parameter to a memory item associated
23                   with the <name> specified by the second parameter.
24                   When the memory item to which data is copied is of a different type, or has an incompatible
25                   structure, an execution error - 294 (Incompatible type) is generated. When the specified
                     destination name does not exist, the device may create a new memory item of the same type
26                   and structure as the source. In that case, the destination name is to be associated with the
                     new created memory item.


          13-6     MEMory Subsystem
                              1999 SCPI Command Reference

         This command is an event with no associated query form and *RST condition.
13.3.2   :TABLe <name>                                                                                PH076
         MEMory:COPY:TABLe
         The COPY:TABLe command copies the data values of all element lists from the SELected
         TABLe to the memory table associated with the specified <name>.                               1
         When the memory item to which data is copied is of a different type, or has an incompatible   2
         structure, an execution error -294 (Incompatible type) is generated. When the TABLe name
         does not exist, the device may define a new memeory table with the same structure as the
                                                                                                       3
         selected table. In that case, the specified TABLe name is associated with the new created     4
         memory table.
                                                                                                       5
         This command is an event with no associated query form and *RST condition.
                                                                                                       6
13.4     :DATA<name>,<data>                                                                          TK023B
         MEMory:DATA                                                                                   7
         The command form is MEMory:DATA <name>,<data>. The command loads <data> into                  8
                                                                                                     TK023B
         the memory location <name>. <data> is in 488.2 block format. <name> is character data.
                                                                                                       9
         The query form is MEMory:DATA? <name> with the response being the associated <data>         TK023B
         in block format.
                                                                                                      10
         MEMory:DATA? response is not affected by the FORMat subsystem.
                                                                                                      11
                                                                                                     TK023B
13.5     :DELete                                                                                      12
         MEMory:DELete
                                                                                                      13
         The DELete command purges the specified definition from instrument memory and makes it
         available for reuse.                                                                         14
13.5.1   :ALL                                                                                         15
         MEMory:DELete:ALL
                                                                                                      16
         The ALL command removes all memory names, key definitions, and data, and it returns
         memory to “available.”                                                                       17
13.5.2   [:NAME] <name>                                                                               18
         MEMory:DELete:NAME
                                                                                                      19
         The NAME command is an optional node and deletes the definition associated with <name>.
                                                                                                      20
13.6     :EXCHange                                                                                     PH076
         MEMory:EXCHange                                                                              21
         The EXCHange subsystem allows for swapping the data contents between two memory              22
         items.
                                                                                                      23
13.6.1   [:NAME] <name>,<name>                                                                         PH076
         MEMory:EXCHange:NAME                                                                         24
         This command is a default node which swaps the data contents between the memory items        25
         associated with the <name> parameters.
                                                                                                      26
         When the memory items between which the data is swapped are of different type, or have an
         incompatible structure, an execution error -294 (Incompatible type) is generated.

                                                                      MEMory Subsystem        13-7
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

                     This command is an event with no associated query form and *RST condition.
          13.6.2     :TABLe <name>                                                                                   PH076
                     MEMory:EXCHange:TABLe
                     This command swaps the data contents between the SELected TABLe and the memory table
 1                   that is associated with the <name> parameter.
 2                   When the memory item associated with the specified <name> parameter is not a TABLe, or
                     the tables between which the data is swapped have an incompatible structure, an execution
 3                   error -294 (Incompatible type) is generated.
 4                   This command is an event with no associated query form and *RST condition.
 5        13.7       :FREE
                     MEMory:FREE
 6
                     Returns information on the user memory space as follows:
 7                         <bytes available>,<bytes in use>
 8                   where the returned data for both shall be in <NR1> format.
 9                   The qualified FREE query for TRACe only memory usage is specified in the TRACe
10                   subsystem.

11        13.7.1     [:ALL]?
                     MEMory:FREE:ALL?
12                   If the FREE query is qualified by the optional ALL node then the query shall return memory
     13              sizes related to all items in instrument memory.

14        13.7.2     :ASCii?
                     MEMory:FREE:ASCii?
15                   If the FREE query is qualified by the ASCii node then the memory usage and availability
16                   shall reflect the values that correspond to values for ASCii data. In an instrument that has
                     dedicated memory for ASCii data types, these values reported shall be different from the
17                   total given by a FREE query of ALL types.
18        13.7.3     :BINary?
                     MEMory:FREE:BINary?
19

20                   shall reflect the values that correspond to values for BINary data. In an instrument that has
21                   dedicated memory for BINary data types, these values reported shall be different from the
                     total given by a FREE query of ALL types.
22
          13.7.4     :MACRo?

13.8     :NSTates?                                                                                          7
         MEMory:NSTates?
         The Number of STates query requests that the instrument return the number of *SAV/*RCL             8
         states available in the instrument. The instrument shall return a <NR1> value which is one         9
         greater than the maximum that can be sent as a parameter to the *SAV and *RCL commands.
                                                                                                           10
13.9     :STATe                                                                                           TK023B
         MEMory:STATe                                                                                      11
         Collects commands relating to memory STATe data.                                                 TK023B
                                                                                                           12
13.9.1   :CATalog?                                                                                        TK023B
                                                                                                           13
         MEMory:STATe:CATalog?
         This query requests a list of defined names in the MEMory:STATe subsystem. The                    14
                                                                                                          TK023B
         instrument returns a list of defined <name>’s in a comma separated list. Each <name> is           15
         returned in a quoted string. If no names are defined, a single null string is returned. There is
         no command form.                                                                                  16
13.9.2   :DEFine <name> , <register_number>                                                                17
                                                                                                          TK023B
         MEMory:STATe:DEFine
                                                                                                           18
         :DEfine associates a <name> with a *SAV/*RCL register number where <name> is in                  TK023B
         character data format. <register_number> is in <NRf> format.                                      19
         The query form of this command, MEMory:STATe:DEFine? <name> returns the associated TK023B         20
         <register_number> in <NR1> format.                                                                21
         *RST has no effect on this command.                                                              TK023B
                                                                                                           22
13.10    :TYPE? <name>                                                                                     23
         MEMory:TYPE?
         The TYPE query requests information about a defined name. The instrument must return a            24
         string indicating the subsystem where the name was defined. If the name is not defined, a         25
         null string is returned. For example, if VAT3 was previously defined by:
                 ROUTe:MODule:DEFine VAT3,(@20000(0:9))                                                    26


                                                                          MEMory Subsystem         13-9
                                         1999 SCPI Command Reference

                   then the query:
                          MEMory:TYPE? VAT3
                   requests a return of
                          “ROUT:MOD:”
 1        13.11    :TABLe
                   MEMory:TABLe
 2                                                                                                                HP058A




                   The MEMory:TABLe command allows the user to DEFine a TABLe and to write data to
 3                 and read data from it.
 4        13.11.1 :BNUMber <numeric_value> {,<numeric_value>}
                   :MEMory:TABLe:BNUMber
 5
                   BNUMber is the gas bottle number. This command sets the gas bottle number, which is a
 6                 positive integer.
 7                 NOTE: For Emissions benches, BNUMber<n> are bottle ID number columns in the
 8                 GasBottle, ZeroGas, SpanGas, Verify, and TopGas tables. In the ZeroGas, SpanGas, Verify,
                   and TopGas tables, there are columns BNUMber<n>, where n corresponds to the analyzer
 9                 range number. In GasBottle, there is a single BNUMber column.
10        13.11.1.1 :POINts?
                   :MEMory:TABLe:BNUMber:POINts?
11
                   This command returns the number of points in column BNUMber, for the currently selected
12                 table.
     13   13.11.2 :CCURve <numeric_value> {,<numeric_value>}
                   :MEMory:TABLe:CCURve
14
                   CCURve sets the value of concentration in ppm using the current curve in linearization
15                 tables. This command sets the values of CCURve.
16        13.11.2.1 :POINts?
                   :MEMory:TABLe:CCURve:POINts?
17
                   This command returns the number of points in column CCURve, for the currently selected
18                 table.
19        13.11.3 :CONCentration <numeric_value> {,<numeric_value>}
                   :MEMory:TABLe:CONCentration
20
                   CONCentration is the gas concentration in ppm. This command sets the values of
21                 CONCentration.
22        13.11.3.1 :POINts?
23                 :MEMory:TABLe:CONCentration:POINts?
                   This command returns the number of points in column CONCentration, for the currently
24                 selected table.

                   DFACtory is the maximum allowable drift from factory settings.
 6
                   For emissions benches, this is the zero or span factory setting in the tables ZDRift and
 7                 SDRift respectively. This command sets the values of DFACtory. Drift from factory setting
 8                 is calculated as follows:
 9                 Zero Drift                (Z∗− Zf)
                                     ZDf =              ∗ 100
10                                              fs

11                 Span Drift                (S∗− Sf)
                                     SDf =              ∗ 100
12                                              fs

     13            where        Z* and S* are the currently read zero and span values in ppm
                                Zf and Sf are the factory settings stored in DFACtory in ppm
14                              fs is the full scale CONCentration in ppm
15                              ZDf is the zero drift in PCT
                                SDf is the span drift in PCT
16
                   Note: a ratio of 1.0 = 100 PCT

 1        13.11.11 :DEFine <structure_string>[,<numeric_value>]
                   MEMory:TABLe:DEFine
 2
                                                                                                                      HP058A




                   The DEFine subsystem is used to allocate space and define the structure of TABLe in the
 3                 instrument memory. The <name> of the TABLe is specified by SELect.
 4                 The string parameter <structure_string> specifies the structure of the TABLe being defined,
                   it contains a comma separated list of the elements. Any item lists under MEMory:TABLe,
 5                 such as FREQuency or VOLTage:PHASe, may be specified as elements in the table
 6                 structure. The item lists maybe specified in long or short form, optional nodes if sent shall be
                   accepted without error. The item lists available and the legal combinations of these item lists
 7                 are device dependent. All lists are empty (0 length) when DEFined.
 8                 The second parameter, is the size of the TABLe. This is the maximum number of POINts in
 9                 each of the lists. Computations based on device dependent internal data formats will be made
                   to determine the number of bytes. For example, if the TABLe will have two lists and the
10                 internal storage requires 8 bytes for a number, then an entry of 10 will allocate 160 bytes. If
11                 there is insufficient room, execution error -225 (Out of memory) will be generated. The size
                   of the table parameter is optional. The algorithm to allocate memory is device dependent
12                 when this parameter is omitted.
     13            The DEFine query returns both the <structure_string> and a numeric value for the size (in
14                 points) of memory allocated for the table. The elements of the structure string are returned in
                   the short form, with any optional nodes omitted.
15

14     MMEMory Subsystem
       The Mass MEMory subsystem provides mass storage capabilities for instruments. All mass
       memory device commands are contained in the MMEMory subsystem. The mass storage
       may be either internal or external to the instrument. If the mass memory device is external,
       then the instrument must have controller capability on the mass memory device bus.                1
       The CLOSe, FEED, NAME, and OPEN commands permit the streaming of data from                        2
       anywhere in the data flow into a file; this is particularly useful for saving HCOPy output.       3
                                                                                                        HP063e
       Mass storage media may be formatted in any one of a number of standard formats.                   4
     Selecting Mass Memory Devices                                                                       5
       When an instrument has multiple attached mass storage devices, the desired mass storage
                                                                                                         6
       unit is selected with the mass storage unit specifier <msus>. The syntax of the <msus> string
       is instrument specific. Each instrument’s documentation shall describe the syntax applicable      7
       to that instrument. For example:
                                                                                                         8
               “C:”
                “:700,2”                                                                                 9
                “fileserv”
                                                                                                        10
       Note that some file systems do not make use of the <msus> concept.
                                                                                                        11
     File Names                                                                                         12
       The <file_name> parameter described in the commands in this subsystem is a string. The
       contents of the string are dependent on the needs of the format of the mass storage media. In    13
       particular, the file name may contain characters for specifying subdirectories (that is, \ for   14
       DOS, / for HFS) and the separator for extensions in DOS (that is, period).
                                                                                                        15
       The following commands are provided for mass memory device operations.
