 9        14.1     :CATalog? [<msus>]
                   MMEMory:CATalog?
10                 The CATalog command is query-only and returns information on the current contents and
11                 state of the mass storage media. Upon a CATalog? query, the instrument shall read the
                   specified mass memory device and returns its directory information in the following format:
12                         <numeric_value>,<numeric_value> {,<file_entry>}
13                 The instrument shall return two numeric parameters and as many strings as there are files in
     14            the directory list. The first parameter shall indicate the total amount of storage currently used
                   in bytes. The second parameter shall indicate the total amount of storage available, also in
15                 bytes. The <file_entry> is a string. Each <file_entry> shall indicate the name, type, and size
16                 of one file in the directory list:
                           <file_name>,<file_type>,<file_size>
17
                   Note that this syntax places some restrictions on the <file_name> (for example, commas are
18                 not allowed.) The <file_name> is the exact name of a file as it appears in the directory list,
19                 including an extension if present. The <file_size> provides the size of the file in bytes. The
                   <file_type> is indicated by one of the following:
20
                              ASCii — An ASCii text file
21
                              BINary — A binary file
22
                              STATe — Instrument (setting) state
23
                              TRACe — Trace (display) data
24
                              MACRo — An instrument macro
25
                   For media which cannot determine the file type from the directory information (i.e. DOS,
26                 HFS) this field shall be left blank.



          14-2   MMEMory
                              1999 SCPI Command Reference

14.2   :CDIRectory [<directory_name>]
       MMEMory:CDIRectory
       Changes the default directory for a mass memory file system. The <directory_name>                   TK044
       parameter is a string. The contents of the <directory_name> parameter are dependent on the
       file system being accessed. If no parameter is specified, the directory is set to the *RST
       value.                                                                                               1
       At *RST, this value is set to the root for DOS file systems and to a device-dependent value          2
                                                                                                           TK044
       for other file systems such as HFS.                                                                  3
14.3   :CLOSe                                                                                              HP063e
       MMEMory:CLOSe
                                                                                                            4
       The CLOSe event causes the selected file specified in NAME to be closed. An attempt to               5
       CLOSe a file that was not open shall cause an error -256, (File name not found) to be                6
       generated.
14.4   :COPY <file_source>,<file_destination>
                                                                                                            7
       MMEMory:COPY                                                                                         8
       The COPY command copies an existing file to a new file.
                                                                                                            9
       Two forms of parameters are allowed. The first form has two parameters. In this form, the
       first parameter specifies the source file, and the second parameter specifies the destination
                                                                                                           10
       file.                                                                                               11
       The second form has four parameters. In this form, the first and third parameter specify the        12
       file_names. The second and fourth parameters specify the <msus>. The first pair of
       parameters specifies the source file. The second pair specifies the destination file. An error is
                                                                                                           13
       generated if the source file doesn’t exist. An error may be generated if the destination file       14
       already exists.
                                                                                                           15
       This command defines an event and thus has no *RST state or query form.
                                                                                                           16
14.5   :DATA <file_name>, <data>                                                                           TK054
       MMEMory:DATA                                                                                        17
       The command form is MMEMory:DATA <file_name>,<data>. The command loads <data>                       18
       into the file <file_name>. <data> is in 488.2 block format. <file_name> is string data.
                                                                                                           19
       The query form is MMEMory:DATA? <file_name> with the response being the associated
                                                                                                           20
       <data> in block format.
                                                                                                           21
       MMEMory:DATA? response is not affected by the FORMat subsystem.
14.6   :DELete <file_name>[,<msus>]                                                                        22
       MMEMory:DELete                                                                                      23
       The DELete command removes a file from the specified mass storage device. The
       <file_name> parameter specifies the file_name to be removed.                                        24
       This command defines an event, and it has no *RST condition or query form.                          25
                                                                                                           26


                                                                                     MMEMory 14-3
                                           1999 SCPI Command Reference

          14.7       :FEED <data_handle>                                                                             HP063e
                     MMEMory:FEED
                     Sets or queries the <data_handle> to be used to feed data into the file specified by NAME.
                     New data arriving from <data_handle> always overwrites the contents of the file specified
                     by NAME. If the <data_handle> generates new data and the file is not OPEN an error -256,
 1                   (File name not found) shall be generated.
 2                   At *RST, the value of FEED is device dependent.
 3        14.8       :INITialize [<msus>[,(LIF|DOS|HFS)[,<numeric_value>]]]
                     MMEMory:INITialize
 4
                     The INITialize command is used to initialize the specified mass storage media. If the
 5                   <msus> is not specified, the default is used. The default is the <msus> selected at *RST, not
 6                   the currently selected <msus>. The second parameter specifies the type of media to be
                     formatted. The <numeric_value> parameter is used to specify the format, interleave, sector
 7                   sizes, and other media-dependent information. Execution of the command attempts to
 8                   initialize the media. Previous data on the media, if any, is destroyed.

 9                   This command is an event and does not have a query form or a *RST condition.
          14.9       :LOAD and :STORe
10                   MMEMory:LOAD and :STORe
11                   The LOAD and STORe subsystems transfer information between the mass memory device
                     and the instrument’s memory. The LOAD commands transfer from mass memory device to
12                   internal memory, and STORe transfers from internal memory to the mass memory device.
13                   When information is loaded, the instrument uses the file type information to determine
     14              whether the data is in internal (BINary) or transportable (ASCii) form.
15                   The <file_name> parameter is a quoted string and the <label> refers to an internal identifier
                     for the instrument trace or macro.
16
                     The LOAD and STORe commands do not have query forms.
17
          14.9.1     :DINTerchange <label>,<file_name>[,<msus>]
18                   MMEMory:LOAD:DINTerchange
19                   Specifies that the device transfer DINTerchange formatted data.
20        14.9.1.1    :TRACe <label>,<file_name>[,<msus>]
                     MMEMory:LOAD:DINTerchange:TRACe
21                   The specified trace or array is loaded from or stored to the mass memory device in
22                   DINTerchange format.
23        14.9.2     :MACRo <label>,<file_name>[,<msus>]
                     MMEMory:LOAD:MACRo
24
                     The specified macro is loaded from or stored to the mass memory device.
25
          14.9.3     :STATe <numeric_value>,<file_name>[,<msus>]
26                   MMEMory:LOAD:STATe
                     The specified instrument state is stored or loaded. The <numeric_value> parameter refers to
                     the state number, which corresponds to the numbers found in *SAV and *RCL.

14.11    :MOVE (<src_file>,<dest_file>)                                                                     8
               |(<src_file>,<src_msus>,<dest_file>,<dest_msus>)                                             9
         MMEMory:MOVE                                                                                           HP048




         The MOVE command moves an existing file to another file name.                                     10
         Two forms of the parameter are allowed. The first form has two parameters. In this form the       11
         first parameter, <src_file>, specifies the file to be renamed, and the second parameter,          12
         <dest_file>, specifies the new name of the file.
                                                                                                           13
         The move operation is performed on the default mass storage device.
                                                                                                           14
         The second form has four parameters. The first two parameters, <src_file> and <src_msus>,
         specify the file name and storage device of the source file and the second two parameters,        15
         <dest_file> and <dest_msus>, specify the new file name and new storage device for the             16
         source file.
                                                                                                           17
         Some instruments may not support the moving of a file across mass storage devices and thus
         shall generate error -250, “Mass Storage Error”, when the msus parameters are not the same.       18
         If the <src_file> does not exist, the instrument shall generate error -256, “File name not        19
         found”. If the <dest_file> already exists, the instrument shall generate error -257, “File name   20
         error”.
                                                                                                           21
         This command is an event-only command and thus has no *RST value, and no query form.
                                                                                                           22

         MMEMory:NAME                                                                                      23
         Sets or queries the name of the file specification used by the CLOSe and OPEN commands.

          14.13     :OPEN                                                                                           HP063e
                    MMEMory:OPEN
                    The OPEN event causes the selected file specified in NAME to be opened. An attempt to
                    OPEN a file that is already opened shall cause an error -257, (File name error) to be
                    generated. If the selected file is non-existent, it is created.
 1
          14.14     :PACK [<msus>]
 2                  MMEMory:PACK                                                                                         HP037




                    This command causes the mass storage device to be packed, such that unused memory
 3
                    between files is recovered and packed together. If an instrument, which supports file packing
 4                  (ie: implements the MMEM:PACK command), receives the MMEM:PACK command but
 5                  the current disk format does not support file packing, the instrument shall generate an error
                    -250 (Mass Storage Error). If the <msus> is not specified the default is used.
 6
                    This command defines an event and thus has no *RST state or query form.

16   PROGram Subsystem
     The purpose of the PROGram subsystem is to provide the administrative features needed to
     generate and control one or more user-programmed tasks resident in an instrument. Two
     distinct methods of accessing a particular program are provided in the PROGram
     subysystem. One method employs EXPLicit reference for each command, allowing access to           1
     all programs, but requires the program name to be always specified. The other method             2
     allows a single program to be SELected at a time, and the related commands access only the
     currently selected program. If the EXPLicit method is implemented, then the SELected             3
     method shall also be implemented.                                                                4
     A *RST received from a remote controller, via the device interface, shall cause all programs     5
     to be stopped.
                                                                                                      6
     A *RST generated by a program running in the device shall cause the same effect as a *RST
     received from a remote controller, with the exception that the program that generated the        7
     *RST shall not be forced to stop. It is necessary for a *RST to behave in this manner so that    8
     a program, when run on either a remote controller or the device, shall have the same effect.
                                                                                                      9
     KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                               NOTES
     PROGram                                                                                         10
       :CATalog?                                                         [query only]                11
      [:SELected]
         :DEFine            <program>                                                                12
         :DELete                                                         [no query]                  13
           [:SELected]
            :ALL                                                                                     14
         :EXECute           <program_command>                            [no query]                  15
         :MALLocate         <nbytes>|DEFault
         :NAME              <progname>                                                               16
         :NUMBer            <varname>{,<nvalues>}                                                    17
         :STATe             (RUN|PAUSe|STOP|CONTinue)
         :STRing            <varname>{,<svalues>}                                                    18
         :WAIT                                                                            1991       19   HP009




       :EXPLicit
         :DEFine            <progname>,<program>                                                     20
         :DEFine?           <progname>                        [query only]                           21
         :DELete            <progname>
         :EXECute           <progname>,<program_command>      [no query]                             22
         :MALLocate         <progname>,(<nbytes>|DEFault)                                            23
         :NUMBer            <progname>,<varname>{,<nvalues>}
         :STATe             <progname>,(RUN|PAUSe|STOP|CONTinue)                                     24
         :STRing            <progname>,<varname>{,<svalues>}                                         25
         :WAIT              <progname>                                                    1991
                                                                                                     26


                                                                                PROGram 16-1
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference
                                                                                                                     HP009




          16.1       :CATalog?
                     PROGram:CATalog?
                     The CATalog query commands lists all the defined programs. Response is a list of
                     comma-separated strings. Each string contains the name of a program. If no programs are
 1                   currently defined, then response is a null string ( “” ).
 2
          16.2       [:SELected]
 3                   PROGram:SELected
                     All the commands under this node access only the program that has been selected by the
 4
                     NAME command.
 5
          16.2.1     :DEFine <program>
 6                   PROGram:SELected:DEFine

 7                   The DEFine command is used to create and download programs. The DEFine query is used
                     to upload programs. The program name used for the definition is the currently selected
 8                   program name.
 9                   In the DEFine command, the selected program name shall represent a unique name. That is,
10                   to download and overwrite an existing program with the same program name, the existing
                     program must be DELeted first. If such an attempt is made without deleting first, an “Illegal
11                   program name” error (-282) shall be generated.
12                   The <program> shall be block data. The contents are device-dependent. When overflow
13                   occurs a program error (-28X) shall be generated.

14                   In the DEFine query, the selected program shall be returned. The <program> shall be
                     uploaded as definite length arbitary block response data.
15
          16.2.2     :DELete
     16              PROGram:SELected:DELete

17                   The DELete command deletes downloaded programs.

18        16.2.2.1     [:SELected]
                     PROGram:SELected:DELete:SELected
19                   This command causes the selected program to be deleted.
20        16.2.2.2     :ALL
                     PROGram:SELected:DELete:ALL
21
                     ALL is used to specify that all programs in the device are to be deleted. If any of the
22                   programs are in the RUN state, a “Program currently running” error (-284) shall be
23                   generated and no programs shall be deleted.

24        16.2.3     :EXECute <program_command>
                     PROGram:SELected:EXECute
25                   The EXECute command executes the <program_command> in the selected program
26                   environment. <program_command> is string data representing any legal program command.
                     If the string data is not legal, then a “Program syntax error” (-285) shall be generated. The
                     selected program shall be in either the PAUSed or STOPped state before the EXECute

          16-2     PROGram:CATalog?
                               1999 SCPI Command Reference

         command shall be allowed. If the program is in the RUN state, a “Program currently
         running” error (-284) shall be generated.
16.2.4   :MALLocate <nbytes>|DEFault
         PROGram:SELected:MALLocate
         The Memory ALLocate command is used to reserve memory space in the device for use by             1
         the selected program. If DEFault is specified, then the device shall calculate the amount of
         memory needed. <nbytes> is numerical data which specifies the required memory in bytes.

17     ROUTe Subsystem
       In the SCPI instrument model, the block where user accessibility to the actual signals occurs
       is called “signal routing.” In some instruments this function may be trivial and thus
       commands for this block would not be required. In such cases the ports associated with the
       INPut or OUTput blocks are available directly to the user, typically on the instrument’s front    1
       panel. The ROUTe commands apply equally to instruments whose primary purpose is to                2
       provide signal routing and to instruments that provide some routing capability “in front of”
       the INPut and/or OUTput blocks.                                                                   3
       The ROUTe node may be optional in a particular instrument. This capability is intended for        4
       instruments whose primary function is signal routing. The ROUTe node cannot be optional if        5
       either SENSe or SOURce is optional, since only one node at a given level may be optional.

17.1   :CLOSe <channel_list>                                                                            25
       ROUTe:CLOSe                                                                                           HP062




       The CLOSe command allows specific individual channels to be closed or queried. If all the        26
       specified channels cannot be closed, an execution error is reported.


                                                                        ROUTe Subsystem          17-1
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

                     For example, suppose a module contains a coaxial multiplexor, and only one channel on a
                     bank is able to be closed at a time. If a command tries to close two channels on the same
                     bank, the instrument should report an execution error.
                     CLOSe may be an overlapped command. The *OPC mechanism may be used to determine
 1                   when switches are actually closed or opened. The sequence in which channels are closed is
                     not guaranteed.
 2
                     The CLOSe? query allows the condition of individual switches to be queried. The instrument
 3                   returns a 1 or 0 for each channel in the list, in the same order that the list is specified. A
 4                   response of 1 means the channel is closed and a 0 means the channel is open.
 5                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
 6        17.1.1     :STATe?
                     ROUTe:CLOSe:STATe?
 7                   The ROUTe:CLOSe:STATe? query, which has no parameters, returns an IEEE 488.2
 8                   definite length block which contains a <channel_list> of all the closed switches in the entire
                     instrument.

                     This command causes flow from the specified sample point to the selected instrument(s). An
14                   execution error -200 shall occur if the <sample_point> references a configuration that cannot
15                   be achieved by the device. This command can also query the currently selected
                     <sample_point>. The query response is a string. Each string contains a <sample_point>. If a
16                   <sample_point> is not currently selected, then the response is NONE.
     17              At *RST the selected path goes to the idle state (NONE).
18                   For emissions benches, the :ROUTe:SAMPle command is used to route gases from the
19                   source to the measurement instrument. This command causes gases to flow to the
                     instruments from the specified sample point. No measurement sequence is executed,
20                   however subsequent SENSe:DATA? queries will reflect the current values of the gases
21                   flowing through the analyzers. Gas routing may be implied during predefined procedures.
                     On *RST the selected path goes to the idle state (NONE).

24                      BAG — Causes gases from the specified bag sampling system to flow through the

                        tunnel of a diesel sampling system

   PRE — Gasses from between the engine and the catalytic converter.

          17.6     :SCAN <channel_list>
                   ROUTe:SCAN                                                                                               HP062




                   The SCAN command specifies or queries a list of channels for the instrument to sequence              KI002
                   through. The instrument will automatically step through the list of channels provided when
                   the trigger subsystem device action occurs. The device action is to open the channel
 1                 previously closed, then to close the next channel in the list. Whether this action is
 2                 break-before-make is device-dependent.

 3                 The INITiate[:IMMediate] command must be sent in order to initiate scanning.

 4                 Execution of the SCAN command, and the resulting scan operation, may or may not open
                   any channels which are already closed.
 5
                   If the <channel_list> parameter contains a <channel_range>, the instrument will expand the
 6                 range into its individual channels, and scan each channel individually. For example,
 7                 (@1,3:5,9) will be scanned identically to (@1,3,4,5,9).

 8                 The query, which has no parameter, returns the scan list. The format of the response is an
                   IEEE 488.2 definite length block which contains a <channel_list>. The instrument may
 9                 return the scan list exactly as it was received, or it may return an equivalent list with paths or
10                 ranges expanded.

11                 Note: The query form was added in 1994.

12        17.7     TERMinals FRONt|REAR|BOTH|NONE                                                                       KI003
                   ROUTe:TERMinals                                                                                          HP052




13                 FRONt opens the rear terminals and closes the front terminals (break before make). REAR              KI003
14                 opens the front terminals and closes the rear terminals (also break before make). BOTH
                   closes both the front and rear terminals in a device-dependent order. NONE opens both the
15                 front and rear terminals in a device-dependent order.
16                 At *RST, TERM is set to FRONt.

18   SENSe Subsystem
     The SENSe setup commands are divided into several sections. Each section or subsystem
     deals with controls that directly affect device-specific settings of the device and not those
     related to the signal-oriented characteristics. These commands are referenced through the
     SENSe node.                                                                                         1
     The SENSe node may be optional in a particular device. The reason that the SENSe is                 2
     optional is to allow devices which are primarily sensors to accept shorter commands. The            3
     SENSe node cannot be optional if either SOURce or ROUTe is optional, since only one
     node at a given level may be optional. For example, a typical counter may elect to make the         4
     SENSe node optional, since the most frequently used commands would be under the SENSe               5
     subsystem. If the counter also contained either source or routing functionality, these would
     be controlled through their respective nodes; however, the SOURce or ROUTe nodes would              6
     be required. An optional node, such as SENSe, implies that the device shall accept and              7
     process commands with or without the optional node and have the same result. That is, the
     device is required to accept the optional node, if sent, without error.                             8
     In some instances, a sensor may contain subservient source or sensor functions. In such             9
     cases, the additional subservient functionality shall be placed as SENSe or SOURce                 10
     subnodes under the SENSe subsystem. Further, no optional nodes (SENSe, SOURce or
     ROUTe) are permitted if such subservient functionality exists in a device. Otherwise               11
     conflicts in interpreting commands would occur, for example, between SENSe and                     12
     [SOURce:]SENSe if the SOURce were allowed to be optional.
                                                                                                        13
     The FREQuency subsystem contains several sets of commands which have complex
     couplings. This includes the swept commands STARt, STOP, CENTer, and SPAN as one                   14
     set. Sending any one of a set singly will affect two others of the set. However, if two are sent   15
     in a single message unit, then these two should be set to the values specified and the other
     two changed. This is in accordance with the style guidelines and IEEE 488.2. If any                16
     command in the set is implemented then all the commands in the set shall be implemented.           17
     If the requested setting is unachievable given the other instrument settings, then an error        18
     must be generated (-221 “Settings conflict”). The device may resolve the conflict in a
     device-dependent manner (for example, change STARt, STOP, CENTer, and/or SPAN) to                  19
     resolve the error. Note that when more than one of the four sweep settings are received in the     20
     same program message unit, the sweep will be determined by the last two received.
                                                                                                         PH075
                                                                                                        21
     The coupled commands may define commands as subnodes which alter these couplings. The
     command description will define how the couplings are altered. However, any command                22
     which alters couplings must default to the couplings described in this section as the *RST         23
     couplings.
                                                                                                        24
     When CENTer or SPAN is changed the following couplings apply:
                      SPAN         = SPAN                                                               25
                      CENTer       = CENTer                                                             26
                      STOP         = CENTer + (SPAN/2)
                      STARt        = CENTer - (SPAN/2)

                                                                                     SENSe:      18-1
                                          1999 SCPI Command Reference

                   When STARt or STOP changed the following couplings apply:
                            STARt = STARt                CENTer = (STARt + STOP)/2
                            STOP      = STOP             SPAN      = STOP - STARt
                   The CURRent, VOLTage and POWer subsystems contain several commands which have
 1                 complex couplings. These commands exist under RANGe: they are UPPer, LOWer, OFFset,
                   and PTPeak. UPPer and LOWer are considered as one set, with OFFSet and PTPeak as
 2                 another set. Sending any one of a set singly shall affect the two values of those commands in
 3                 the other set. However, if two are sent in a single message unit, then these two should be set
                   to the values specified and the unspecified two values shall be changed. This is in
 4                 accordance with the style guidelines and IEEE 488.2. If either OFFSet or PTPeak is
 5                 implemented, then all four commands, UPPer, LOWer, OFFSet, and PTPeak shall also be
                   implemented.
 6
                   When UPPer or LOWer is changed the following couplings apply:
 7                          UPPer    = UPPer              OFFSet = (UPPer + LOWer)/2
 8                          LOWer = LOWer                 PTPeak = UPPer - LOWer
 9                 When OFFSet or PTPeak is changed the following couplings apply:
                            OFFSet = OFFSet                UPPer = OFFSet + (PTPeak/2)
10                          PTPeak = PTPeak                LOWer = OFFSet - (PTPeak/2)
11                 The SENSe subsystem for the dynamometer contains the commands needed to sense
12                 real-time measurements taken from the dynamometer system. This includes force, speed,
                   frictional losses, acceleration rate, distance, and simulation error. These commands are used
13                 in conjunction with the TRIGer Subsystem for collecting data in blocks. See SCPI 1995
14                 Volume 2 Command Reference chapter 18 section 11 for further detail on the DATA and
                   FUNCtion subsystems.

          18.2       AVERage Subsystem
                     SENSe:AVERage                                                                                              HP054




                     The purpose of this subsystem is to control averaging used to improve the measurement. For                 FL005




                     example to improve the accuracy or to acquire maximum/minimum measurements.
                     Analytical post-acquisition statistical functions are controlled within the CALCulate block.
 1                   The AVERage subsystem combines successive measurements to produce a new composite
 2                   result. The new result has the same number of points and control axis as the original
                     measurement.
 3
                     A :COUNt command is provided to specify the number of measurements to combine. When                        HP054




 4                   :COUNT averages are reached, the TerminalCONtrol switch specifies the operation of the
 5                   average subsystem. The TerminalCONtrol switch can be configured to continue replacing
                     old values with new values (MOVing), to exponentially weight new measurements
 6                   (EXPonential), to automatically repeat (REPeat), or to continue adding new measurements in
 7                   the NORMal fashon, as specified by :TYPE.

 8                   The average operation differs from CALC:SMOOthing in the fact that AVERage combines                        HP054




                     the jth point of each measurement with the jth point of preceeding measurements, whereas in
 9                   SMOOthing the jth point is processed with adjacent points (...., j-2, j-1, j, j+1, j+2, ...) of the
10                   current measurement set.

11                   Note: The notation Xn* indicates the complex conjugate of a number. So:
                         XX* = MAG2(X) = |X|2

          18.4      CONCentration Subsystem
                    SENSe:CONCentration
                    This subsystem configures the CONCentration measurement functions and parameters. An
                    instance of this subsystem exists for each range in an instrument. The data defined and
                    queried and the events will only be performed on the currently selected range of the
 1                  currently selected instrument(s).
 2                  KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                                COMMENTS
 3                  :CONCentration                                                                          1999
                      :CSET                 <numeric_value>,<numeric_value>                                 1999
 4                    :LOWer                <numeric_value>                                                 1999
 5                    :LSET                 POLYnomial<n> | SRATional<n>,<numeric_value>                    1999
                      :RANGe                                                                                1999
 6                      :AUTO                                                                               1999
 7                        :LOWer            <numeric_value>                                                 1999
                         [:STATe]           <Boolean>                                                       1999
 8                        :UPPer            <numeric_value>                                                 1999
 9                     [:FIXed]             <numeric_value>                                                 1999
                      :TALign               <numeric_value>                                                 1999
10                    :UPPer                <numeric_value>                                                 1999
11        18.4.1    :CSET <numeric_value>,<numeric_value>
                    :SENSe:CONCentration:CSET
12
                    This command specifies or queries the correction set(s) used for the current range(s). The
13                  parameters are the slope and the Y intercept used in the latest correction calculation.
14                  At *RST these values are not changed.
15        18.4.2    :LOWer <numeric_value>
                    :SENSe:CONCentration:LOWer
16
                    This command specifies or queries the lowest measurable concentration for the
17                  currently-selected range for the selected instruments.
     18             At *RST these values are not changed.
19        18.4.3    :LSET POLYnomial<n> | SRATional<n>,<numeric_value>{,<numeric_value>}
                    :SENSe:CONCentration:LSET
20
                    This command sets or returns the curve fit type and coefficients that are currently in use.
21                  Coefficients are listed starting with the 0th order term. The first parameter is the curve type,
22                  which consists of either POLYnomial for a polynomial curve fit or SRATional for a simple
                    rational polynomial curve fit, followed by a positive integer <n>, which is the curve order.
23                  The additional parameters are the curve coefficients. These are listed starting with the 0th
24                  order term. Note that the number of coefficients depends on the order of the curve - there are
                    exactly n+1 coefficients for a curve of order n. The parameter list for LSET includes a curve
25                  type and associated coefficients for the currently selected range of each currently selected
26                  analyzer. See :CALibration:LINearize:CURVe:FIT for examples.
                    Note that the :CALibration:LINearize:ACCept command sets the parameter values.

18.5     CONDition Subsystem
         SENSe:CONDition
         This subsystem controls the electrical characteristics of a sensor that determines the ON or
         OFF condition of a digital signal.
         KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                               COMMENTS                    1
         :CONDition                                                                               1993   PH074
           LEVel                 <numeric_value> | TTL | ECL                                      1993   2
                                                                                                         PH074
18.5.1   :LEVel <numeric_value> | TTL ECL                                                                 3
         SENSe:CONDition:LEVel
                                                                                                          4
         This command specifies the characteristics that causes the transition between an ON and
         OFF condition of the sensed signal. When the value of the input signal exceeds the specified     5
         level, the condition is qualified as ON or 1 (True) for positive logic type, and qualified as    6
         OFF or 0 (False) when it is associated with negative types of logic. For positive logic, the
         condition is sensed as OFF or 0 (False) when the input value is below the level; for negative    7
         logic this value is qualified as an ON or 1 (True) condition.                                    8
         The default units are the amplitude units associated with the currently sensed signal.           9
         At *RST this value is device dependent.                                                         10

          18.6     CORRection Subsystem
                   SENSe:CORRection
                   The correction subsystem provides for known external losses or gains. In contrast to
                   CALibration, these losses usually are dependent on individual measurement setups.

 1                 Correction data may be entered and stored in several ways. A mechanism is provided to
                   automatically measure a reference standard(s) and store the resulting “correction set” in a
 2                 trace. The trace can be selected at any time as the active “correction set”. This trace could
 3                 also be generated by an external device and transferred to the instrument over a computer
                   interface. Commands are also provided to enter individual losses, gains, offsets, delays, etc.
 4                 that the instrument should use in correcting the data. An instrument is not required to
 5                 implement all of the methods.

 6                 The commands in this subsystem are designed to correct for losses, gains, and offsets in
                   external probes or transducers. For instance, they can be used to inform the sensor that a 10X
 7                 probe has been attached to the instrument. This way, the data and measurement results will
 8                 be corrected so that they are not 1/10th their actual value. In instruments that automatically
                   detect the attachment of a probe, these commands may not be necessary.
 9
                   KEYWORD              PARAMETER FORM                                   COMMENTS
10                 :CORRection
11                   :AUTO                                                               [event]          1999
                     :CALCulate                                                          [event]          1999
12                   :COLLect

18.6.3     :COLLect
           SENSe:CORRection:COLLect                                                                          17
           Deals with the collection of the correction data. This data is collected directly by the device   18
           by measurements of standards.
                                                                                                             19
18.6.3.1     [:ACQuire] STANdard
           SENSe:CORRection:COLLect:ACQuire
                                                                                                             20
           A measurement will be performed and saved as the data for standard of the chosen                  21
           correction method. The number of standards required to be measured for the correction is
                                                                                                             22
           determined by the method chosen. If a standard is specified that does not exist in the chosen
           method, then an error is generated and no measurement is taken. This measurement will not         23
           affect any of the users settings for regular measurements.
                                                                                                             24
           For complex corrections, several standards will be measured and then followed by a SAVE
                                                                                                             25
           command. The parameter on the save command will be the name of the correction set.The
           standards themselves are device-specific.                                                         26
           This command is an event, does not have a *RST value, and is not queryable.

          18.6.3.2     :METHod TPORt
                     SENSe:CORRection:COLLect:METHod
                     Selects the correction method to be used for the correction that is about to be performed. If
                     only one correction method exists in the instrument then this command is not required.
 1                   The various settings of the parameters have the following meanings:
 2                   TPORt Two Port
 3                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
 4        18.6.3.3     :SAVE [<trace_name>]
                     SENSe:CORRection:COLLect:SAVE
 5                   Calculates the correction data using the current method selection and then saves the
 6                   correction data. If only one correction array exists then it is saved there. Otherwise it is saved
                     in the set specified by <trace_name>. Note that the parameter <trace_name>must be defined
 7                   and exist in the instrument. This command will not create a trace. Trace definition is done in
 8                   the trace subsystem. Note that the correction array may be a single value.
 9                   Depending on the complexity of the correction method chosen, a calculation may or may not
                     be performed on the measured arrays to determine the correction data. For example, if the
10                   chosen method has only one standard, then no calculation will be performed.
11                   This command is an event, does not have a *RST value, and is not queryable.

          18.6.7     :LOSS|:GAIN|:SLOPe
 5                   SENSe:CORRection:LOSS
 6                   These commands are used either to provide a mechanism to apply simple correction or to
                     correct external factors that have not been accounted for in the correction set. These
 7                   correction factors are typically applied to measurements made at the device input; however,
 8                   in cases where measurements can be at the device output a separate set of correction factors
                     may be applied.
 9
                     Loss, gain and slope effect the measurement values as a multiplier for linear units such as
10                   VOLT and as additive (or subtractive) value for logarithmic units such as DB.
11                   :LOSS      This command is used to set the anticipated loss in the system, excluding those
12                              factors covered by the active correction set. The device then corrects every
                                measurement by this factor to compensate for the loss. LOSS is coupled to GAIN
13                              by the equation LOSS = 1/GAIN when the default unit is linear and
14                              LOSS=-GAIN when the default unit is logarithmic.
15                   :GAIN      This command is used to set the anticipated gain in the system, excluding those
                                factors covered by the active correction set. The device then corrects every
16                              measurement by this factor to compensate for the gain. GAIN Is coupled to LOSS
17                              by the equation GAIN=1/LOSS when the default unit is linear and GAIN=-LOSS
                                when the default unit is logarithmic.
     18
                     :SLOPe     This node defines an increasing or decreasing value that is added to the signal.
19                              This correction value is zero at a zero value of the x axis and increase or
20                              decreases from there.
                                                                                                                        HP075




21        18.6.7.1     [:INPut]|:OUTPut
22                   SENSe:CORRection:LOSS:INPut
                     The INPut and OUTPut nodes are used to reference measurements made at the instrument’s
23
                     input and output, respectively. Most sensor instruments are only capable of making
24                   measurements at its input ports; however, some instruments are capable of making
                     measurements on output ports that are sourcing a signal.
25
          18.6.7.1.1    :AUTO ON|OFF
26                   SENSe:CORRection:LOSS:INPut:AUTO

18.7.1.5       :RANGe
           SENSe:CURRent:AC:RANGe
           Sets the range for the amplitude sensor function. The RANGe endpoints may be specified in
           terms of the UPPer endpoint and the LOWer endpoint, alternatively the midpoint of the
           RANGe (OFFSet) and the span of the RANGe (PTPeak) may be used. A non-symmetrical
           range around zero may cause some instruments to introduce an actual offset to the signal
                                                                                                              1
           entering the SENSe block.                                                                          2
18.7.1.5.1     [:UPPer] <numeric_value>                                                                       3
           SENSe:CURRent:AC:RANGe:UPPer
           Specifies the most positive signal level expected for the sensor input.
                                                                                                              4
           At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
                                                                                                              5
18.7.1.5.2     :LOWer <numeric_value>
                                                                                                              6
           SENSe:CURRent:AC:RANGe:LOWer                                                                       7
           Specifies the most negative signal level expected for the sensor input. This allows setting for
           the best dynamic range. This function is coupled to UPPer in a device-dependent manner.
                                                                                                              8
           At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
                                                                                                              9
18.7.1.5.3     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
                                                                                                             10
           SENSe:CURRent:AC:RANGe:AUTO                                                                       11
           Sets the RANGe to the value determined to give the most dynamic range without
           overloading. The actual algorithm is device-dependent.
                                                                                                             12
           At *RST, AUTO is set to ON.
                                                                                                             13
18.7.1.5.3.1    :DIRection UP|DOWN|EITHer
                                                                                                             14
           SENSe:CURRent:AC:RANGe:AUTO:DIRection                                                             15
           The DIRection command defines the manner in which AUTO works. When UP is selected,
           the instrument shall only change the range automatically to ranges larger than the current
                                                                                                             16
           range, as the input signal dictates. When DOWN is selected, the instrument shall only             17
           change the range automatically to ranges smaller than the current range, as the input signal
                                                                                                             18
           dictates. When EITHer is selected the instrument may range in either direction.
                                                                                                             19
           At *RST, DIRection shall be set to EITHer.
                                                                                                             20
18.7.1.5.3.2    :LLIMit <numeric_value>
           SENSe:CURRent:AC:RANGe:AUTO:LLIMit                                                                21
           The Lower LIMit command sets the smallest range to which the instrument will go while
                                                                                                             22
           autoranging. When AUTO is ON and the present RANGe is outside the new limits, the
           instrument may change the RANGe to a value inside the limits or wait until the next time the      23
           autoranging algorithm is performed.
                                                                                                             24
           At *RST, LLIMit shall be set to MINimum.
                                                                                                             25
18.7.1.5.3.3    :ULIMit <numeric_value>
           SENSe:CURRent:AC:RANGe:AUTO:ULIMit
                                                                                                             26
           The Upper LIMit command sets the largest range to which the instrument will go while

          18.8      DETector Subsystem
                    SENSe:DETector
                    This subsystem controls the acquisition of data points, including how to choose points and
                    the linear characteristics of the sensor.

 1                  KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                                NOTES
                    :DETector
 2                    :BANDwidth           <numeric_value>                                                1991
 3                   |:BWIDth                                                                             1991
                     [:FUNCtion]           GROund|NEGative|POSitive|SAMPle|SIGNal
 4                                         |PAVerage | AAVerage|RMS                                       1991
 5                     :AUTO               <Boolean>|ONCE
                     :SHAPe                LINear|LOGarithmic
 6
          18.8.1    :BANDwidth | BWIDth
 7                  <numeric_value>
 8                  SENSe:DETector:BANDwidth

 9                  The BANDwidth function controls the bandwidth after an intermediate signal has been
                    processed within the SENSe block. Instruments must accept both forms, if they accept either.
10
          18.8.2    [:FUNCtion] <detector function>
11                  SENSe:DETector:FUNCtion

12                  Specifies the detector sampling characteristics. The various settings have the following
                    meanings:
13
                              GROund: The input detector is grounded. Thus no signal is acquired.
14
                              NEGative: The minimum signal detected during the acquisition of the particular
15                            point is chosen.
16                            POSitive: The maximum signal detected during the acquisition of the particular
17                            point is chosen.

     18                       SAMPle: A single arbitrary point detected is chosen.

19                            SIGNal: The detector chooses points so that envelope noise is maximized and
                              positive signals above some threshold are also maximized.
20
                              PAVerage: PeakAVerage is the average of the minimum and maximum
21                            excursions of the signal. PAV = ( absolute minimum peak + absolute maximum
22                            peak) / 2

23                            AAVerage: AbsoluteAVerage averages the absolute values of a sine wave input
                              and processes the value to read RMS values.
24
                              RMS: True Root Mean Square signal detector.
25
                    At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
26


          18-30    SENSe:DETector
                                  1999 SCPI Command Reference

           SENSe:DETector:FUNCtion:AUTO

           selected, the detector type is determined by the system in order to give the “best” quality of

18.12   FREQuency Subsystem
        SENSe:FREQuency
        The FREQuency subsystem controls the frequency characteristics of the instrument. Two
        types of controls are included in this subsystem. The first is frequency sensor controls, such
        as RANGe. The second is frequency sweep controls, such as STARt, or tuning controls such
        as CW.                                                                                            1
        Unless otherwise noted, the default unit for all <numeric_values> in this subsystem are in Hz.    2
        KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                                NOTES                        3
        :FREQuency             <numeric_value>                                                            4
          :APERture            <numeric_value>
          :CENTer              <numeric_value>                                                            5
         [:CW|:FIXed]          <numeric_value>                                                            6
            :AFC               <Boolean>|ONCE                                                 1994       RS012
            :AUTO              <Boolean>|ONCE                                                             7
          :MANual              <numeric_value>                                                            8
          :MODE                CW|FIXed|SWEep|LIST|SOURce
          :MULTiplier          <numeric_value>                                                            9
          :OFFSet              <numeric_value>                                                           10
          :RANGe
           [:UPPer]            <numeric_value>                                                           11
            :LOWer             <numeric_value>                                                           12
            :AUTO              <Boolean>|ONCE
          :RESolution          <numeric_value>                                                           13
            :AUTO              <Boolean>|ONCE                                                            14
          :SPAN                <numeric_value>
            :HOLD              <Boolean>                                                                 15
            :LINK              CENTer|STARt|STOP                                                         16
            :FULL                                                            [no query]
          :STARt               <numeric_value>                                                           17
          :STOP                <numeric_value>                                                           18
18.12.1 :APERture <numeric_value>                                                                        19
        SENSe:FREQuency:APERture
        Specifies the acquisition/sampling/gate time for a single measurement point. The parameter       20
        has a unit of seconds.                                                                           21
        At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                         22
18.12.2 :CENTer <numeric_value>                                                                          23
        SENSe:FREQuency:CENTer
        Set the center frequency of the sweep or measurement.                                            24
        At *RST, this function will be set to (MINimum+MAX)/2.                                           25
                                                                                                         26


                                                                       SENSe:FREQuency 18-37
                                             1999 SCPI Command Reference

          18.12.3 [:CW|:FIXed] <numeric_value>
                      SENSe:FREQuency:CW
                      The Continuous Wave or FIXed node is used to select a frequency of a non-swept signal.
                      This node is optional. An optional node, such as [:CW|:FIXed], implies that the device shall
                      accept and process commands with or without the optional node and have the same result.
 1                    That is, the device is required to accept the optional node, if sent, without error. A device
 2                    must accept both :CW and :FIXed if it implements this node.
 3                    At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
 4        18.12.3.1     :AFC <Boolean>|ONCE                                                                           RS012
                      SENSe:FREQuency:CW:AFC
 5                    If AFC is ON the sensor is coupled to the frequency of the signal. The default frequency is
 6                    determined by SENSe:FREQuency[:CW].
 7                    The actual value of FREQuency[:CW] is adjusted to match the frequency of the signal. The
                      query FREQuency[:CW]? returns the adjusted value, not the value sent with the last
 8                    FREQuency[:CW] command.
 9                    At *RST, this value is set to OFF.
10        18.12.3.2     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
11                    SENSe:FREQuency:CW:AUTO
                      Couples the CW frequency to center frequency. Explicitly setting FREQuency:CW will set
12                    AUTO OFF.
13                    At *RST, this value is set to ON.
14        18.12.4 :MANual <numeric_value>
15                    SENSe:FREQuency:MANual
                      Same as CW except limited by STARt and STOP. This command only affects the frequency
16                    if SENSe:SWEep:MODE MANual and SENSe:FREQuency:MODE SWEep are selected. If
17                    the sweep limits are changed such that manual frequency would be outside the sweep limits,
                      then the manual frequency will be set to the nearest end point of the sweep.
     18
                      At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
19
          18.12.5 :MODE CW|FIXed|SWEep|LIST|SOURce
20                    SENSe:FREQuency:MODE
21                    Determines which set of commands control the frequency. If CW or FIXed is selected, the
                      frequency is determined by FREQuency:CW. CW and FIXed are aliases. Both must be
22                    implemented if either is implemented. If SWEep is selected, the sensor is in the swept mode
23                    and frequency is determined by FREQuency:STARt, STOP, CENT, SPAN, and MAN. If
                      LIST is selected, the frequencies are determined by LIST:FREQuency.
24
                      If SOURce is selected, the sensor is coupled to the source. All frequency controls are
25
                      determined by the SOURCe:FREQuency block, except for OFFSet and MULTiplier. These
26                    two commands remain active under SENSe to allow for offset and harmonic tracking.
                      At *RST, this value is set to CW.

          18-38   SENSe:FREQuency
                                   1999 SCPI Command Reference

18.12.6 :MULTiplier <numeric_value>
            SENSe:FREQuency:MULTiplier
            Sets a reference multiplier for all other frequency settings in the instrument. All entered and
            displayed frequencies are affected by this command. The coupling equation is:
                    Entered|Displayed frequency = (Hardware frequency * multiplier) + offset.
                                                                                                                 1
            This command affects the values of all functions which affect sensing of the signal. This
            includes such things as CW frequency and the sweep frequency controls. It does not affect
                                                                                                                 2
            things like input filter bandwidths. It does affect the settings of relative frequency parameters    3
            such as delta markers or FM deviation. Also note that this command does not affect the
            hardware settings of the instrument, but only the entered and displayed frequencies.
                                                                                                                 4
            At *RST, this value is set to 1.
                                                                                                                 5
18.12.7 :OFFSet <numeric_value>
                                                                                                                 6
            SENSe:FREQuency:OFFSet                                                                               7
            Sets a reference frequency for all other absolute frequency settings in the instrument. This
            command affects the values of all functions which affect sensing of the signal. This includes
                                                                                                                 8
            such things as CW frequency and the sweep frequency controls. It does not affect things like         9
            input filter bandwidths. It also does not affect the settings of relative frequency parameters
            such as delta markers or SPAN. Also note that this command does not affect the hardware
                                                                                                                10
            settings of the instrument, but only the entered and displayed frequencies. The coupling            11
            equation is:
                    Entered|Displayed frequency = (Hardware frequency * multiplier) + offset.
                                                                                                                12
            At *RST, this value is set to 0.
                                                                                                                13
18.12.8 :RANGe
                                                                                                                14
            SENSe:FREQuency:RANGe                                                                               15
            Sets the frequency range for the sensor function.
                                                                                                                16
18.12.8.1     [:UPPer] <numeric_value>
            SENSe:FREQuency:RANGe:UPPer                                                                         17
            Specifies the maximum value expected for the sensor input.                                          18
            At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                            19
18.12.8.2     :LOWer <numeric_value>                                                                            20
            SENSe:FREQuency:RANGe:LOWer
                                                                                                                21
            Specifies the lowest value expected for sensor input.This function is coupled to UPPer in a
            device-dependent manner.                                                                            22
            At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                            23
18.12.8.3     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE                                                                              24
            SENSe:FREQuency:RANGe:AUTO
                                                                                                                25
            Sets the RANGe to the value determined by the instrument.
                                                                                                                26
            At *RST, AUTO is set to ON.

          18.12.9 :RESolution <numeric_value>
                      SENSe:FREQuency:RESolution
                      Specifies the absolute resolution of the frequency measurement. For example, if a
                      measurement of 10 MHZ is made with a resolution of .01, the measurement is returned with
                      a resolution of .01 Hz (that is, 10000000.00Hz)
 1
                      At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
 2
          18.12.9.1     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
 3                    SENSe:FREQuency:RESolution:AUTO
 4                    Allows the system to determine the best resolution for the other measurement conditions.
 5                    Explicitly selecting a value for FREQuency:RESolution will set AUTO OFF.
 6                    At *RST, this value is set to ON.
 7        18.12.10 :SPAN <numeric_value>
                      SENSe:FREQuency:SPAN
 8                    Sets the frequency span.
 9                    At *RST, this function will be set to MAXimum.
10        18.12.10.1     :HOLD <Boolean>
11                    SENSe:FREQuency:SPAN:HOLD
                      Provides a mechanism to prevent the SPAN from being changed implicitly by the defined
12                    coupling between STARt, STOP, CENTer and SPAN. When HOLD is set to ON, SPAN
13                    shall only be changed by explicitly sending the SPAN command.
14                    At *RST, this value is set to OFF.
15        18.12.10.2     :LINK CENTer|STARt|STOP
                      SENSe:FREQuency:SPAN:LINK
16                    Allows the default couplings for SPAN to be overridden. LINK selects the parameter, either
17                    CENTer, STARt or STOP, that shall not be changed when SPAN’s value is changed. For
                      example, if LINK is set to STARt, then changing SPAN shall cause CENTer and STOP, not
     18               STARt, to change.
19                    At *RST, this value is set to CENTer, to be compatible with the default definition for the
20                    couplings.
21        18.12.10.3     :FULL
                      SENSe:FREQuency:SPAN:FULL
22                    When this command is received, start frequency is set to its minimum value, and stop
23                    frequency is set to its maximum value. Center frequency and span are set to their coupled
                      values.
24
                      This command is an event. Therefore it has no associated query, or meaning at *RST.

18.12.11 :STARt <numeric_value>
        SENSe:FREQuency:STARt
        Sets the starting frequency for a sweep or measurement. It also sets one limit of a manual
        frequency adjustment. If the instrument does not support negative frequency span, having the
        start frequency greater than the stop frequency will cause an error to be generated.
                                                                                                        1
        At *RST, the parameter will be set to MINimum.
                                                                                                        2
18.12.12 :STOP <numeric_value>
        SENSe:FREQuency:STOP                                                                            3
        Sets the stop frequency of a sweep or measurement. It also sets the other limit of a manual     4
        sweep adjustment. If the instrument does not support negative frequency span, having the
        stop frequency less than the start frequency will cause an error to be generated.
                                                                                                        5
        At *RST, this parameter will be set to MAXimum.
