          18.13       FUNCtion & DATA Subsystem
                      SENSe:FUNCtion & DATA
                      The FUNCtion subsystem selects the <sensor_function>(s) to be sensed by the instrument.
                      These functions differ from the signal-oriented MEASure instructions in that a
                      <sensor_function> is something that the sensor can be configured to directly detect.
 1
                      The DATA subsystem is used to query data from the SENSe block.
 2
                      KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                                  NOTES
 3                    :DATA?                  [<data_handle>]                                 [query only]      1991
 4                    :DATA                                                                                     1995       TK056
                        :PREamble?            [<data_handle>]                                 [query only]      1994      TK032a
 5                    :FUNCtion
 6                      :CONCurrent           <Boolean>                                                        1991
                        :OFF                  <sensor_function>{,<sensor_function>}                            1991
 7                        :ALL                                                                [no query]       1991
 8                        :COUNt?                                                             [query only]     1991
                       [:ON]                  <sensor_function>{,<sensor_function>}                            1991
 9                        :ALL                                                                [no query]       1991
10                        :COUNt?                                                             [query only]     1991
                        :STATe?               <sensor_function>                               [query only]     1991
11
          18.13.1 DATA? [<data_handle>]
12                    SENSe:DATA?

13                    Provides access to the result(s) of the SENSe block. This query retrieves the current SENSe
                      result(s).
14
                      The <data_handle> parameter to this query is optional. Instruments that implement this
15                    query are required to accept the the optional parameter <data_handle> if sent. If a sensor
16                    function is specified, and that function is currently being sensed the result is returned. If the
                      function is not being sensed an error -221 (Settings Conflict) shall be generated.
17
                      If a <data_handle> is not specified, then the result(s) of all functions being sensed are
     18               returned. If CONCurrent is OFF there will be only one FUNCtion result. If CONCurrent is
19                    ON there will be one or more results, depending on how many functions are currently on.
                      The order of the function results returned by the DATA? query is device-dependent,
20                    although the order of these results shall be the same as the order of the functions returned by
21                    the FUNCtion[:ON]? query. If no functions are currently being sensed an error -221
                      (Settings Conflict) shall be generated. The data returned by the DATA? query is affected by
22                    the FORMat subsystem.
23                    This command is query-only and therefore has no *RST condition.
24        18.13.1.1       SENSe <data_handle>s
25                    If the SENSor block only emits one data flow, then the <data_handle> is just the string
                      “SENSe<n>”, where <n> is a numeric suffix. However, for the case where the SENSe block
26                    outputs more than one result, each data result needs to be assigned a unique <data_handle>,
                      symbolic of the data flow. Since the SENSe:FUNCtion command is already defined to take a


          18-42   SENSe:FUNCtion & DATA
                                  1999 SCPI Command Reference

            well-defined string as a parameter, these <sensor_function> strings are used as part of the
            <data_handle>. If more than one SENSe block in the instrument outputs the same
            <sensor_function> the SENSe block must also be included in the data handle. The syntax for
            the SENSe block <data_handle> is:
                   <data_handle> := “[SENSe:]<sensor_function>” | “SENSe[:<sensor_function>]”
                                                                                                             1
18.13.1.2     :PREamble? [<data_handle>]                                                                    TK056
            SENSe:DATA:PREamble?                                                                             2
            PREamble? returns the preamble information supporting the DATA(CURVe(VALues)) but                3
                                                                                                            TK032a
            omits the following data:
                                                                                                             4
                      DIF blocks of waveform, measurement, and delta.
                                                                                                             5
                      DIF curve block keywords VALues and CSUM and their parameters.
                                                                                                             6
            The DIF difid block must contain the keyword SCOPe with the parameter of PREamble.              TK032a
                                                                                                             7
            While the PREamble? query is designed to efficiently transmit data relating directly to the     TK032a
            curve, the various notes and identification parameters may be sent if absolutely required.       8
            The optional <data_handle> parameter functions the same as it does in SENSe:DATA?.               9
                                                                                                            TK032a
18.13.2 :FUNCtion                                                                                           10
            SENSe:FUNCtion                                                                                  11
            The FUNCtion subsystem selects the <sensor_function>(s) to be sensed by the instrument.
            For compatibility, instruments that support CONCurrent ON are required to support               12
            CONCurrent OFF mode. This is so some level of compatibility can be maintained with              13
            non-concurrent instruments which expect data results for only one FUNCtion to be returned
            by the SENSe:DATA? query.
                                                                                                            14
18.13.2.1     :CONCurrent <Boolean>
                                                                                                            15
            SENSe:FUNCtion:CONCurrent                                                                       16
            The CONCurrent command indicates whether the SENSor block should be configured to
            SENSe one function at a time or SENSe more than one function at a time (concurrently).
                                                                                                            17
            If CONCurrent is OFF, the FUNCtion[:ON] command acts as a one-of-n switch selecting the
                                                                                                            18
            indicated function to be the only sensed function. If CONCurrent is ON, the function(s)         19
            specified as parameter(s) to the FUNCtion[:ON] command are turned on, while the state of
            other functions are not affected.
                                                                                                            20
            When CONCurrent is turned OFF, the instrument shall select one function to be turned on,
                                                                                                            21
            and turn off any other functions that were on. The function which is selected to be on shall    22
            always be the same one, even if that function is not currently ON.
                                                                                                            23
            When CONCurrent is turned ON, the states of individual functions shall not be changed.
                                                                                                            24
            At *RST the value of CONCurrent is device-dependent. However if an instrument
            implements CONCurrent ON, then it must implement CONCurrent OFF also for purposes of
                                                                                                            25
            instrument compatibility.                                                                       26


                                                                    SENSe:FUNCtion & DATA           18-43
                                             1999 SCPI Command Reference

          18.13.2.2     :OFF <sensor_function>{,<sensor_function>}
                      SENSe:FUNCtion:OFF
                      The FUNCtion:OFF command selects the <sensor_function>s to be turned off. This
                      command only needs to be implemented by instruments which allow users to turn OFF
                      individual functions while leaving others on. The state of any other functions are not affected
 1                    by turning the specified functions OFF.
 2                    The query response of FUNCtion:OFF? shall return a comma separated list of functions
 3                    which are currently OFF, each of which are <STRING RESPONSE DATA>. If no functions
                      are OFF, a null string is returned. The query shall return the short form mnemonics and shall
 4                    omit any default nodes in the <sensor_function>.
 5                    At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
 6        18.13.2.2.1     :ALL
 7                    SENSe:FUNCtion:OFF:ALL
                      This command turns OFF all of the <sensor_function>s which the instrument can
 8                    concurrently sense. There is no query for this command.
 9        18.13.2.2.2     :COUNt?
10                    SENSe:FUNCtion:OFF:COUNt?
                      This query returns the number of <sensor_function>s which are OFF. This command must
11                    be implemented if CONCurrent ON and FUNCtion:OFF are implemented.
12                    This command is query-only and therefore has no *RST condition.
13        18.13.2.3     [:ON] <sensor_function>{,<sensor_function>}
14                    SENSe:FUNCtion:ON
                      The FUNCtion[:ON] command selects the <sensor_function>(s) to be SENSed by the
15                    instrument. This command only needs to be implemented by instruments which allow users
16                    to select what functions will be SENSed. The <sensor_function> is specified as a quoted
                      string. For example:
17                        FUNCtion “VOLTage:AC”
     18               If CONCurrent is OFF, a single <sensor_function> is sent as the parameter. This selects this
19                    function to be sensed. If more than one function is sent an error -108 (Parameter not
                      allowed) shall be generated.
20
                      If CONCurrent is ON, a comma separated list of <sensor_function> may be sent as
21                    parameters. These functions are turned on, while the state of other functions are not affected.
22                    The query response of FUNCtion[:ON]? shall return a comma separated list of functions
23                    which are on, each of which are <STRING RESPONSE DATA>. If no functions are ON, a
                      null string is returned. The query shall return the short form mnemonics and shall omit any
24
                      default nodes in the <sensor_function>.
25
                      For example FUNCtion[:ON]? returns the quoted string “VOLT:AC”.
26
                      At *RST, this value is device-dependent.



          18-44   SENSe:FUNCtion & DATA
                                  1999 SCPI Command Reference

18.13.2.3.1     :ALL
            SENSe:FUNCtion:ON:ALL
            This command turns ON all of the <sensor_function>s which the instrument can
            concurrently sense. There is no query for this command.
18.13.2.3.2     :COUNt?                                                                                      1
            SENSe:FUNCtion:ON:COUNt?
            This query returns the number of <sensor_function>s which are ON. This command must be
                                                                                                             2
            implemented if CONCurrent ON and FUNCtion[:ON] are implemented.                                  3
            This command is query-only and therefore has no *RST condition.                                  4
18.13.2.4     :STATe? <sensor_function>                                                                      5
            SENSe:FUNCtion:STATe?
            Returns a Boolean indicating whether the specified <sensor_function> is currently ON or
                                                                                                             6
            OFF. This command is query only.                                                                 7
            At *RST, the state of each <sensor_function> is device- dependent.                               8
18.13.2.5     <sensor_function>                                                                              9
            SENSe:FUNCtion
            The FUNCtion subsystem uses the <sensor_function> to select the function on which the
                                                                                                            10
            FUNCtion commands operate on, <sensor_function> has the following syntax:                       11
                  <sensor_function> ::=“<presentation_layer><function_name>
                                  [<input block>{,<input block>}] [ON <subnode>{,<subnode>}]”
                                                                                                            12
            The <sensor_function> is STRING PROGRAM DATA.
                                                                                                            13
            The names inside angle brackets (<) and (>) are called productions and the commas (,) and
                                                                                                            14
                                                                                                            HP088
            ‘ON’ are literals. White space is defined in section 7.4.1.2 of IEEE 488.2 as one or more       15
            white space characters.
                                                                                                            16
            For a <sensor_function> sent to an instrument, white space is not allowed inside any            HP088
            production or literal. White space is not allowed between the <presentation_layer> and
                                                                                                            17
            <function_name> productions. At least one white space character is required before and          18
            after the literal ON. At least one white space character is required before the first
            <input_block>. White space is permitted, but not required, everywhere else in the
                                                                                                            19
            <sensor_function>. The FUNCtion commands shall accept the long and short forms of               20
            <sensor_function> mnemonics. Instruments shall accept both upper and lowercase
            characters without distinguishing between cases.
                                                                                                            21
            When a <sensor_function> is returned in response to a query, it shall contain no white space
                                                                                                            22
                                                                                                            HP088
            except for a single space before the first <input_block> and single spaces around the literal   23
            ON if either is present. The mnemonics in the query response shall use short form with
                                                                                                            24
            default nodes omitted. All alpha characters in the response shall be in uppercase.
            <input_block> elements are omitted in the query response only if all have been set to their     25
            default values. If any <input_block> element has been set to anything other than its default
                                                                                                            26
            value, then all <input_block> elements are returned in the query response.



                                                                   SENSe:FUNCtion & DATA            18-45
                                         1999 SCPI Command Reference

                   The <function_name> is a well-defined hiearchical sensor function indicating the type of
                   function the sensor will be configured to directly detect.
                   The optional <input_block> parameters are numeric values indicating which INPut blocks
                   shall be “fed” into the sensor function. The numeric value corresponds to the same-
 1                 numbered INPut block. Specifying an input block in a sensor function makes an implicit
                   internal routing connection such that the output of the designated INPut block will flow into
 2                 the sensor. If no <input_block> parameters are specified the instrument defined default data
 3                 flow is used.
 4                 For example, SENSe:FUNCtion “VOLTage:AC 2” would configure the sensor to sense the
                   AC Voltage of the data flowing out of INPut2. The SENSe:FUNCtion? query would then
 5                 return the quoted string “VOLT:AC 2”.
 6                 The optional <subnode> parameter is used when the SENSe block contains user
 7                 configurable selections of subnodes to be used in computation of the SENSe FUNCtion. For
                   example if a single SENSe block contained two SWEep subblocks and the sensor could use
 8                 either SWEep block to measure the AC Voltage of INPut1. Currently SWEep and AVERage
 9                 are the only subnodes which are allowed after the ON keyword.

          18.13.2.7     <function_name>
                      SENSe:FUNCtion
                      A SENSe:FUNCtion <function_name> is a well-defined hierarchical sensor function                  TK018
                      indicating the type of function the sensor will be configured to directly detect. The
                      <function_name> comprises the <function> and is optionally followed by a
 1                    :<function_suffix>.
 2                            <function_name> := <function>[:<function_suffix>]
 3                    Where: <function_suffix> is of type <CHARACTER PROGRAM DATA> with the
                      following values defined:
 4                           <function_suffix> := RATio | SUM
 5                    When the RATio suffix is included, then a ratio between two input blocks shall be selected.      TK018
 6                    When the SUM suffix is included, then the sum of two or more input blocks shall be selected.     TK018
 7                    Excluding the <function_suffix> shall cause the sensor function to be selected.                  TK018
 8                    For example:
 9                       :SENSe:FUNCtion “FREQuency”
10                    Selects frequency sensing.
11                       :SENSe:FUNCtion “FREQuency:RATio”
12                    Selects a ratio of two frequencies as a function. If the user specifies input blocks after the
13                    sensor function, then the first input block specified is the numerator and the second input
                      block is the denominator.
14
                         :SENSe:FUNCtion “VOLTage:DC:SUM 1,2"
15
                      Selects the sum of DC voltages on inputs 1 and 2 as a function.
16

          18.14       LIST Subsystem
                      SENSe:LIST
                      The list subsystem controls automatic sequencing through associated lists of frequency, and
                      dwell time values. The various values are specified in the LIST:FREQuency, LIST:DWELl
                      commands. Points in each list correspond to the associated point in all other lists.
 1
                      The LIST subsystem controls a characteristic of the instrument when that subsystem’s mode
 2                    is set to LIST (for example, FREQuency:MODE LIST).
 3                    When employing multiple lists, all lists must be of equal length. If they are not of the same
 4                    length, an error is generated at sequencing time. An exception is made for the case where the
                      shorter list is of length 1. In this case, the particular list is treated as though it were a list of
 5                    equal length, with all values being the same.
 6                    Lists are not affected by *RST.
 7                    KEYWORD                  PARAMETER FORM                                   NOTES
 8                    :LIST
                        :COUNt                 <numeric_value>
 9                      :DIRection             UP|DOWN
10                      :DWELl                 <numeric_value>{,<numeric_value>}
                          :POINts?                                                              [query only]
11                      :FREQuency             <numeric_value>{,<numeric_value>}
12                        :POINts?                                                              [query only]
                        :SEQuence              <numeric_value>{,<numeric_value>}
13                        :AUTO                <Boolean>|ONCE
14                        :POINts?                                                              [query only]

15        18.14.1 :COUNt <numeric_value>
                      SENSe:LIST:COUNt
16                    Controls the number of times the sequence list is scanned when a trigger is received.
17        18.14.2 :DIRection UP|DOWN
                      SENSe:LIST:DIRection
     18
                      Specifies the direction that the sequence list is scanned. If UP is selected, the list is scanned
19                    from the first to the last item in the sequence list. If DOWN is selected, the list is scanned
20                    from the last item to the first item in the sequence list.
21        18.14.3 :DWELl <numeric_value>{,<numeric_value>}
                      SENSe:LIST:DWELl
22                    Specifies the dwell time points of the lists. The units are in seconds.
23                    This specifies the amount of time spent at each point.
24        18.14.3.1     :POINts?
25                    SENSe:LIST:DWELl:POINts?
                      Returns the number of points currently in the DWELl list.
26


          18-58   SENSe:LIST
                                   1999 SCPI Command Reference

            Specifies the frequency points of the list set. The units are Hz.

            SENSe:LIST:FREQuency:POINts?                                                                    1
            This query returns the number of points currently in the FREQuency list.
                                                                                                            2

            SENSe:LIST:SEQuence                                                                             3
            Defines a sequence for stepping through the list. Individual points may be specified as many    4
            times as desired in a single sequence. The points specified are indexes into the lists. For
            example, if 3 was selected, the third point in the frequency and dwell lists would be
                                                                                                            5
            sequenced.                                                                                      6
18.14.5.1     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE                                                                          7
            SENSe:LIST:SEQuence:AUTO
            When on, the sequence list is set to 1 through N, where N is the longest list.
                                                                                                            8
18.14.5.2     :POINts?
                                                                                                            9
            SENSe:LIST:SEQuence:POINts?                                                                    10
            This query returns the number of points currently in the SEQuence list.

          18.15       MIXer Subsystem
                      SENSe:MIXer
                      This subsystem controls external mixers for tuned receivers. It also provides controls to
                      compensate for known fixed losses in external mixers.

 1                    KEYWORD                  PARAMETER FORM                              NOTES
                      :MIXer
 2                      :BIAS                  <numeric_value>
 3                        :AUTO                <Boolean>|ONCE
                          :LIMit               <numeric_value>
 4                      :HARMonic              <numeric_value>

 7        18.15.1 :BIAS <numeric_value>
                      SENSe:MIXer:BIAS
 8
                      Controls the mixer bias.
 9
                      At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
10
          18.15.1.1     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
11                    SENSe:MIXer:BIAS:AUTO

12                    Allows the mixer bias to be automatically set by other parameters in the system. Explicitly
                      setting a value for BIAS shall cause AUTO to be set to OFF.
13
                      At *RST, this value shall be set to ON.
14
          18.15.1.2     :LIMit <numeric_value>
15                    SENSe:MIXer:BIAS:LIMit

16                    Controls the maximum mixer bias level which can be set by the BIAS command or by other
                      parameters when AUTO is ON.
17
                      The limits and *RST conditions are instrument-dependent.
     18
          18.15.2 :HARMonic <numeric_value>
19                    SENSe:MIXer:HARMonic

20                    Selects which harmonic of the local oscillator will be used for mixing.
21                    At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
22        18.15.2.1     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
                      SENSe:MIXer:HARMonic:AUTO
23                    When AUTO is ON, the harmonic is chosen by the system or instrument, and may change
24                    during the sweep. When OFF, the harmonic is locked to the selected value. Setting a value
                      for MIXer:HARMonic sets AUTO to OFF.
25
                      At *RST, this value is set to ON.

18.20   SMOothing Subsystem
        SENSe:SMOothing
        This subsystem controls the point-to-point smoothing of the signal. Smoothing differs from
        averaging in that with smoothing, adjacent points of one set of data are averaged, while in
        averaging the average is taken over several acquisitions (that is, smoothing is a moving
        average). This subsystem controls smoothing done to compensate for measurement artifacts.      1
        Analytical post-acquisition smoothing is controlled with CALCulate:SMOothing.                  2   FL005




        KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                              NOTES                       3
        SMOothing
         [:STATe]              <Boolean>                                                               4
          :APERture            <numeric_value>                                                         5
          :POINts              <numeric_value>
                                                                                                       6
18.20.1 [:STATe] <Boolean>
        SENSe:SMOothing:STATe                                                                          7
        Determines whether the smoothing algorithm is enabled.                                         8
        At *RST, this function is set to OFF.                                                          9
18.20.2 :APERture <numeric_value>                                                                     10
        SENSe:SMOothing:APERture
        Specifies the size of the smoothing APERture as a ratio of smoothing window points/trace      11
        points. POINts is coupled to APERture by the equation:                                        12
                POINts = APERture * SWEep:POINts
                                                                                                      13
        For example, if an APERture of .01 were chosen for a 1000-point sweep, then the smoothing
        window would be 10 points wide.                                                               14
        At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                      15
18.20.3 :POINts <numeric_value>                                                                       16
        SENSe:SMOothing:POINts
                                                                                                      17
        Controls the number of points to be included in the running average. POINts is coupled to
        APERture by the equation:                                                                     18
              POINts = APERture * SWEep:POINts                                                        19
        At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                      20
                                                                                                      21
                                                                                                      22
                                                                                                      23
                                                                                                      24
                                                                                                      25

18.23   SWEep Subsystem
        SENSe:SWEep
        This subsystem controls the timebase and/or sweep generator in instruments that acquire data ACQ02b
        either directly or indirectly as a function of time.
        Examples of instruments that acquire data directly as a function of time (non-swept              ACQ02b
                                                                                                           1
        instruments) are digitizers and logic analyzers. The X axis has units of time. The
        <sensor_function> presentation layer is :XTIMe.                                                    2
        Examples of instruments that acquire data indirectly as a function of time (swept                  3
        instruments) are spectrum analyzers. In this case, the X axis has units of frequency, but the      4
        frequency is swept with relationship to time. The <sensor_function> presentation layer is
        :XFRequency. The parameter to be swept is specified by setting the :MODE node in the               5
        associated subsystem to SWEEP (FREQuency:MODE SWEep).                                              6
        Some commands in this subsystem are applicable to both swept and non-swept instruments.          ACQ02b
                                                                                                           7
        Others may apply to only one of these classes.
                                                                                                           8
        Commands in this subsystem may be coupled to those in implementor-defined trigger                ACQ02b
        sequences such as TRIGger:SAMPle. The TRIGger sequences can provide additional                     9
        flexibility by allowing the user more precise control over the acquisition.                       10
        The commands in the :SWEep subsystem specify the timing and spacing of the values                ACQ02b
                                                                                                          11
        returned in :DATA?, FETCh?, and other measurement queries. The commands in the
        TRIGger subsystem specify when actual measurements are acquired. The precise                      12
        relationship between the parameters in the two subsystems is device dependent. For                13
        example, the :SWEep:TINTerval command specifies the timing period between two
        successive samples of the SENSe:DATA? response. The TRIGger:SAMPle:TIMer                          14
        command specifies the timing period between two acquisition samples that are taken by the         15
        trigger subsystem.
                                                                                                          16
        The :SWEep subsystem contains several sets of commands which have complex couplings.             ACQ02b
                                                                                                         Minutes
        These include the commands :TIME, :POINts, :DWELl, and TINTerval. Sending any one of              17
        a set singly will affect others of the set. However, if two are sent in a single program          18
        message, then these two shall set the values specified and the other changed. This is an
        accordance with the style guidelines and IEEE 488.2. See Syntax and Style section 7.4 for         19
        additional rules.                                                                                 20
        Default units in this subsystem are seconds unless otherwise specified.                          ACQ02b
                                                                                                          21
        KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                                NOTES                       22
        :SWEep
          :COUNt                <numeric_value>                                                           23
          :DIRection            UP|DOWN                                                                   24
          :DWELl                <numeric_value>
            :AUTO               <Boolean>|ONCE                                                            25
          :GENeration           STEPped|ANALog                                                            26
          :MODE                 AUTO|MANual
          :OFFSet                                                                              1994      ACQ02b

18.23.9 :REALtime
                                                                                                             12
                                                                                                              PH072
         SENSe:SWEep:REALtime                                                                                13
         Instruments that acquire data directly as function of time, may use several data acquisition
         methods to sense the data points of the sweep.
                                                                                                             14
         There are techniques where the points in the requested sweep are collected from a number of
                                                                                                             15
         successive acquisitions. In this case the result is a reconstruction of the original signal out of  16
         several acquisitions; this is not real time.
                                                                                                             17
         An acquisition is known as real time if no reconstruction is done; that is, the points in the
                                                                                                             18
         resulting data set are in the order in which they were acquired.
                                                                                                             19
18.23.9.1 [:STATe] <Boolean>                                                                                  PH072
         SENSe:SWEep:REALtime:STATe                                                                          20
         When STATe is ON, the instrument is required to collect data in real time. When STATe is
                                                                                                             21
         OFF, the instrument is allowed to use reconstruction techniques.
                                                                                                             22
         At *RST this function is OFF

18.25       WINDow Subsystem
            SENSe:WINDow
            The window subsystem selects digital signal processing windowing parameters for use by              FL005




            FFT analyzers. Windows are time-domain weighting functions applied to input time records
            to condition the results of a time-domain to frequency-domain transformation. This
            subsystem controls windowing done to compensate for measurement artifacts. Analytical           1
            post-acquisition windowing is controlled with CALCulate:TRANsform.                              2
            KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                               NOTES                       3
            :WINDow
             [:TYPE]               RECTangular subsystem|UNIForm|FLATtop subsystem                          4
                                   |HAMMing|HANNing|KBESsel                                                 5
                                   |FORCe|EXPonential
               :KBESsel            <numeric_value>                                                          6
               :EXPonential        <numeric_value>                                                          7
               :FORCe              <numeric_value>
                                                                                                            8
18.25.1 [:TYPE] RECTangular|UNIForm|FLATtop|HAMMing|HANNing
                      |KBESsel|FORCe|EXPonential                                                            9
            SENSe:WINDow:TYPE
                                                                                                           10
            TYPE allows user selection from among several well-known or standard window types.
            Each window has characteristics that make it particularly suitable for certain kinds of        11
            measurements.                                                                                  12
            Individual windowing algorithms are defined in “On the Use of Windows for Harmonic             13
            Analysis with the Discrete Fourier Transform,” F. J. Harris, Proc of the IEEE, Vol. 66-1,
            January 1978, pp 51-83.                                                                        14
            AT *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                       15
18.25.1.1     :KBESsel <numeric_value>                                                                     16
            SENSe:WINDow:TYPE:KBESsel
                                                                                                           17
            Enters the exponential decay time constant which characterizes the KBESsel window. The
            parameter to this command has units of seconds.                                                18
            At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                       19
18.25.1.2     :EXPonential <numeric_value>                                                                 20
            SENSe:WINDow:TYPE:EXPonential
                                                                                                           21
            Enters the exponential decay time constant which characterizes the EXPonential window.
            The parameter to thids command has units of seconds.                                           22
            At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                       23
18.25.1.3     :FORCe <numeric_value>                                                                       24
            SENSe:WINDow:TYPE:FORCe                                                                        25
            Enters the time value parameter corresponding to the width of the gated portion of the input
            time record for FORCe windows. The parameter of this command has units of seconds.             26
            At *RST, this value is device-dependent.

19   SOURce Subsystem
     The SOURce setup commands are divided into several sections. Each section or subsystem
     deals with controls that directly affect device-specific settings of the device, and not those
     related to the signal-oriented characteristics. These commands are referenced through the
     SOURCe node.                                                                                         1
     The SOURce node may be optional in a particular device. The reason that the SOURce is                2
     optional is to allow devices which are primarily sources to accept shorter commands. The             3
     SOURce node cannot be optional if either SENSe or ROUTe is optional, since only one node
     at a given level may be optional. For example, a typical power supply may elect to make the          4
     SOURce node optional, since the most frequently used commands would be under the                     5
     SOURce subsystem. If the power supply also contained either source or routing
     functionality, these would be controlled through their respective nodes; however, the SENSe          6
     or ROUTe nodes would be required. An optional node, such as SOURce, implies that the                 7
     device shall accept and process commands with or without the optional node and have the
     same result. That is, the device is required to accept the optional node, if sent, without error.    8
     In some instances, a source may contain subservient source or sensor functions. In such              9
     cases, the additional subservient functionality shall be placed as SENSe or SOURce                  10
     subnodes under the SOURce subsystem. Further, no optional nodes (SENSe, SOURce or
     ROUTe) are permitted if such subservient functionality exists in a device. Otherwise                11
     conflicts in interpreting commands would occur, for example, between SOURce and                     12
     [SENSe:]SOURce if the SENSe were allowed to be optional.
                                                                                                         13
     CURRent, POWer, VOLTage, FREQuency, and RESistance contain several sets of
     commands which have complex couplings. This includes the sweep commands STARt,                      14
     STOP, CENTer, and SPAN as one set, and AMPLitude, OFFSet, HIGH, and LOW as                          15
     another. Sending any one of a set singly will affect two others of the set. However, if two are
     sent in a single message unit, then these two should be set to the values specified and the         16
     other two changed. This is in accordance with the style guidelines and IEEE 488.2. STARt,           17
     STOP, CENTer, and SPAN must be implemented as a set. That is, if any one is
     implemented, then all must be implemented.                                                          18
     If the requested setting is unachievable given the other instrument settings, then an error         19
     must be generated (-211 “settings conflict”). The device may resolve the conflict in a              20
     device-dependent manner (for example, change STARt, STOP, CENTer, and/or SPAN) to
     resolve the error. Note that when more than one of the four sweep settings are received in the      21
     same program message unit, the sweep will be determined by the last two received.                   22
     The coupled commands may define commands as subnodes which alter these couplings. The               23
     command description will define how the couplings are altered. However, any command
     which alters couplings must default to the couplings described in this section as the *RST          24
     couplings.                                                                                          25
     When CENTer or SPAN is changed the following couplings apply:                                       26
                      SPAN         = SPAN
                      CENTer       = CENTer

                                                                                   SOURce:       19-1
                                          1999 SCPI Command Reference

                                         STOP           = CENTer + (SPAN/2)
                                         STARt          = CENTer - (SPAN/2)
                   When STARt or STOP is changed the following couplings apply:
                                    STARt         = STARt
 1                                  STOP          = STOP
                                    CENTer        = (STARt + STOP)/2
 2                                  SPAN          = STOP - STARt
 3                 The couplings above assume linear units in the sweep specified.
 4                 HIGH, LOW, AMPLitude, and OFFSet have the same interactions described above for
 5                 STARt, STOP, CENTer, and SPAN.
 6                 When AMPLitude or OFFSet is changed the following couplings apply:
                                     OFFSet       = OFFSet
 7                                   AMPLitude = AMPLitude
 8                                   HIGH         = OFFSet + (AMPLitude/2)
                                     LOW          = OFFSet - (AMPLitude/2)
 9
                   When HIGH or LOW is changed the following couplings apply:
10                                 HIGH          = HIGH
11                                 LOW           = LOW
                                   OFFSet        = (HIGH + LOW)/2
12                                 AMPLitude = HIGH - LOW

                   attenuator to extend the dynamic range of the source’s level. Fig 19-1 illustrates this situation.

17                 dynamic range signal and the attenuator to supply the requested level.

Say the output of the amplifier can vary from -5dBm to 10dBm and the attenuator can range      HP094
from 0 to 50dB in steps of 10dB. The source’s level can thus vary from -55dBm to 10dBm.
                                                                                                5
After *RST, POWer:ATTenuation:AUTO is ON allowing POWer:ATTenuation to
                                                                                                6
                                                                                               HP094
automatically change depending on POWer[:LEVel]. The allowable range for                        7
POWer[:LEVel] is from -55dBm (MINimum) to 10dBm (MAXimum). If POWer[:LEVel] is
set to -48dBm, POWer:ATTenuation is set to 50dB and the power level at the amplifier’s
                                                                                                8
output is 2dBm. If POWer[:LEVel] is -43dBm, the instrument could be in one of two states:       9
POWer:ATTenuation is -40dB and amplifier’s level is -3dBm or                                   10
                                                                                               HP094
POWer:ATTenuation is -50dB and amplifier’s level is 7dBm
                                                                                               11
Which state is chosen may depend on the previous state of POWer[:LEVe]] and the                HP094
algorithm employed by the instrument.
                                                                                               12
The user now wants to prevent the attenuator from changing values. POWer:ATTenuation
                                                                                               13
                                                                                               HP094
-40 is sent. Receiving a value for POWer:ATTenuation has the side effect of turning            14
POWer:ATTenuation:AUTO OFF, see 7.4 in Syntax & Style. Because the attenuator cannot
automatically change, the allowable range for POWer[:LEVel] is limited to the range
                                                                                               15
-45dBm (MINimum) to -30dBm (MAXimum). Trying to program a value outside this range             16
causes an Execution Error. The permissable range for POWer[:LEVel] can be changed by
sending a new value for POWer:ATTenuation.

The actual algorithm employed in the instrument and the range of values depend on the          HP094
underlying hardware implementation. SCPI does require MAXimum/MINimum queries                  19
which a user could use to discover how the bounds of the LEVel command change.

13                   SOURce:AM:COUPling

14                   COUPling, at this level, is used to set the coupling between the modulator and the
                     modulating signal. The modulating signal may be the sum of several signals, either internal
15                   or external sources. If COUPling is set to DC, then both AC and DC components of the
16                   signal pass. AC coupling passes only the AC component of the signal. The GROund
                     parameter allows Amplitude Modulation to be turned ON without the modulating signal
17                   connected.
18                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
     19   19.2.2     [:DEPTh] <numeric_value>

21                   command is used where the DEPTh can be controlled independently from the modulating
22                   signal voltage level. Alternately, it is used to set a device capability that can indicate when
                     the desired DEPTh has been achieved.
23
                     At *RST, this value is device-dependent.

19.4     CORRection Subsystem
         SOURce:CORRection                                                                                        HP067




         The correction subsystem provides for known external losses or gains. In contrast to
         CALibration, these losses usually are dependent on individual setups.
         Correction data may be entered and stored in several ways. A mechanism is provided to                1
         automatically measure the signal and store the resulting “correction set”. This data can be
         selected at any time as the active “correction set”. The data could also be generated by an          2
         external device and transferred to the instrument over a computer interface. Commands are            3
         also provided to enter individual losses, gains, offsets, delays, etc. that the instrument should
         use in correcting its operation. An instrument is not required to implement all of the methods.      4
         KEYWORD             PARAMETER FORM                                    COMMENTS                       5

           This node defines a single value that is added to the signal supplied by the instrument. This

           additive (or subtractive) for linear units such as VOLT.

19.4.5     :LOSS|:GAIN|:SLOPe                                                                                 13PH075
           SOURce:CORRection:LOSS
                                                                                                              14
                                                                                                                    HP075




           These commands are used either to provide a mechanism to apply simple correction or to
           correct external factors that have not been accounted for in the correction set.                   15
           Loss, gain and slope affect the signal amplitude as a multiplier for linear units such as VOLT     16
           and as additive (or subtractive) for logarithmic units such as dB.
                                                                                                              17
           :LOSS      This command is used to set the anticipated loss in the system, excluding those
                                                                                                              18
                      factors covered by the active correction set. The device then adjusts the signal by
                      this factor to compensate for the loss. Loss is coupled to GAIN by the equation         19
                      LOSS = 1/GAIN when the default unit is linear and LOSS =- GAIN when the
                                                                                                              20
                      default unit is logarithmetic.
                                                                                                              21
           :GAIN      This command is used to set the anticipated gain in the system, excluding those
                      factors covered by the active correction set. The device then adjusts the signal by     22
                      this factor to compensate for the gain. Gain is coupled to LOSS by the equation
                                                                                                              23
                      GAIN = 1/LOSS when the default unit is linear and GAIN =- LOSS when the
                      default unit is logarithmetic.                                                          24
           :SLOPe     This node defines an increasing or decreasing value that is added to the signal.        25    HP075




                      This correction value is zero at a zero value of the x axis and increase or decreases
                                                                                                              26
                      from there.



                                                                          SOURce:CORRection 19-13
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

          19.4.5.1     :STATe <Boolean>
                     SOURce:CORRection:LOSS:STATe
                     This function is used to enable or disable the correction for LOSS or GAIN.
                     At *RST, this function is set to OFF.
 1        19.4.5.2     [:OUTPut]

19.5   CURRent Subsystem
       SOURce:CURRent
       This subsection controls the signal amplitude characteristics of the source.
       There is only one subsystem for each of the main amplitude characteristics of the signal.
       Thus, AC voltage and DC voltage are both placed under the VOLTage subsystem. A device           1
       which implemented both simultaneously would implement them as two separate sources, one
       AC and one DC.                                                                                  2

          19.5.4.1.1     [:AMPLitude] <numeric_value>
                   SOURce:CURRent:LEVel:IMMediate:AMPLitude
                   Sets the actual magnitude of the unswept output signal in terms of the current operating
                   units. The units are set to the default value, or alternately to a different value under the UNIT
                   subsystem. AMPLitude may be used to specify the level for either a time varying or
 1                 non-time varying signal.
 2                 Note the optional nodes exist to enable CURRent to be directly followed by a
 3                 <numeric_value>. This is useful for programming simple devices in a straightforward
                   manner.
 4
                   At *RST, the signal being sourced should be set to a “safe” condition. This is generally
 5                 achieved by setting the amplitude to its minimum value in conjunction with OUTPut:STATe
 6                 subsystem.
 7        19.5.4.1.1.1    :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
                   SOURce:CURRent:LEVel:IMMediate:AMPLitude:AUTO
 8
                                                                                                                       PH040




                   If AUTO ON is selected, the voltage setting will be adjusted automatically when a new
 9                 current setting (with the existing voltage setting) exceeds the maximum power limit. If
                   AUTO OFF is selected a new current setting will cause an execution error -221 (Settings
10                 conflict), and the instrument state is device dependent when the maximum power limit is
11                 exceeded.
12                 *RST condition: AUTO OFF

18                 achieved by setting the offset to its minimum value in conjunction with OUTPut:STATe
                   subsystem.

          19.6     DM Subsystem
                   SOURce:DM
                   The Digital Modulation subsystem is used to set the modulation controls and the parameters
                   associated with the modulating signal(s). This modulation embraces a number of digital
                   modulation techniques, which are described in the general terms of I and Q components. The
 1                 keywords to describe the carrier signal exist in other subsystems (such as, FREQuency and
 2                 PHASe).

 3                 KEYWORD               PARAMETER FORM                              COMMENTS
                   :DM
 4                   :FORMat             BPSK|PSK2|QPSK|PSK4|PSK8|QAM16|QAM64|

 6                   :SOURce             EXTernal|PRBS|CALibrate

                       [:SOURce]         INTernal|EXTernal

                     :IQRatio
10                      :STATe           <Boolean>
11                     [:MAGNitude]      <numeric_value>
                     :LEAKage
12                      :STATe           <Boolean>
13                     [:MAGNitude]      <numeric_value>
                        :ANGLe           <numeric_value>
14                   :QUADrature

          19.7      FM Subsystem
                    SOURce:FM
                    The Frequency Modulation subsystem is used to set the modulation controls and the
                    parameters associated with the modulating signal(s). The keywords to describe the carrier
                    signal exist in other subsystems (such as FREQuency and PHASe).
 1
                    KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                                 COMMENTS
 2                  :FM
 3                     :COUPling            AC|DC|GROund
                      [:DEViation]          <numeric_value>
 4                     :EXTernal
 5                        :COUPling         AC|DC|GROund
                          :IMPedance        <numeric_value>
 6                        :POLarity         NORMal|INVerted
 7                     :INTernal
                          :FREQuency        <numeric_value>
 8                     :MODE                LOCKed|UNLocked
 9                     :POLarity            NORMal|INVerted
                       :SENSitivity         <numeric_value>
10                     :SOURce              EXTernal|INTernal{,EXTernal|,INTernal}
11                     :STATe               <Boolean>

12        19.7.1    :COUPling AC|DC|GROund
                    SOURce:FM:COUPling
13                  COUPling at this level is used to set the coupling between the modulator and the modulating
14                  signal. The modulating signal may be the sum of several signals, either as internal or external
                    sources. If COUPling is set to DC, then both AC and DC components of the signal pass. AC
15                  coupling passes only the AC component of the signal. The GROund parameter allows the
16                  modulation to be turned ON without the modulating signal connected.

17                  At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
18        19.7.2    [:DEViation] <numeric_value>
                    SOURce:FM:DEViation
     19             Sets the modulation DEViation of an FM signal. The unit for DEViation is Hertz (Hz). This
20                  command is used where the DEViation can be controlled independently from the modulating
                    signal voltage level. Alternatively, it is used to set a device capability that can indicate when
21                  the desired DEViation has been achieved.
22                  At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
23        19.7.3    :EXTernal
24                  SOURce:FMwEXTernal
                    Controls the specified external signal source. Where multiple external modulation sources
25                  are available, the EXTernal keyword may have a numeric suffix signifying the particular
26                  external signal source. If no number is given, a 1 is assumed.



          19-32    SOURce:FM
                                  1999 SCPI Command Reference

19.7.3.1     :COUPling AC|DC|GROund
           SOURce:FM:EXTernal:COUPling
           COUPling at this level sets the coupling for only the specified external signal source. If
           COUPling is set to DC, then both AC and DC Modulation components of the signal pass.
           AC coupling passes only the AC component of the signal. The GROund parameter allows
           the specified external source to be turned ON without being connected.
                                                                                                               1

           SOURce:FM:EXTernal:POLarity                                                                         7
           POLarity at this level sets the POLarity for only the specified external signal source.             8
           POLarity sets the relationship between the polarity of the applied modulation voltage and the
           resulting “direction” of modulation. The definition of “normal” polarity for FM modulated
                                                                                                               9
           signal is a positive voltage which causes the instantaneous output frequency to increase.          10
           At *RST, this value must be set to NORMal on.                                                      11

10                  Selects the source for the modulating signal, and it may specify a single source or a number
                    of sources. The specified sources, in the SOURce command, are all selected and turned on.
11                  Any sources from a previous selection that are not in the current selection list are deselected

                    legal in the device. Otherwise, an execution error -221 is generated, and the instrument state

19.8.1   :CDOWn                                                                                        21
         :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn
                                                                                                       22
         Coast Down
                                                                                                       23
         This node contains the commands required to run a Dynamometer Coast Down procedure. A
         coast down measures the force, power, and elapsed time over multiple speed intervals as a     24
         vehicle or dynamometer roll coasts in road load simulation from a starting speed to a final   25
         speed. This procedure uses the values set in the :SOURce:FORCe:CONFigure node and the
         CDownSpeed table. The procedure results are stored in the CDownResult table. Measured         26
         coefficients are placed in the memory table CDownMCoeff and are determined after each


                                                                         SOURce:FORCe         19-35
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

                     coast down run. CDownDCoeff should be calculated after coast down run according to SAE
                     J2264, but do not adjust the dyno-setting coefficients.
          19.8.1.1     :INITiate
                     :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn:INITiate
 1                   This is an overlapped command. This command initiates the coast down using the current
                     parameters from the :CONFigure node and CDownSpeed Table. This command describes an
 2                   event and therefore has no associated *RST condition.
 3                   When this command is initiated for dynamometers, the dynamometer must:
 4                      Check critical ancillaries, if any, for proper conditions: Brakes Off, Motor Contactor On,
 5                      parameters within dynamometer safety limits. For conditions that prohibit operation of
                        this procedure, issue appropriate warning messages, and execute the Idle Procedure.
 6
                        Set the DYNO operation condition register Coast Down Procedure bit indicating that a
 7                      Coast down is executing. Note: The DYNO operation condition register will be further
 8                      defined in Volume 4.
 9                      Enter the theoretical data for the defined speed interval and configured parameters in
                        CDownResult table.
10
                        Accelerate dynamometer to :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn:SOFFset +(plus) the starting
11                      speed for the first coast down interval, at the rate in :SOURce:ACCeleration . If the
12                      dynamometer determines this speed is not appropriate for the defined coast down, set the
                        DYNO questionable condition register Coastdown Speed bit and issue an error message,
13                      but continue on with the procedure.
14                      Coast down over the speed intervals defined in the CDownSpeed table. The first interval
15                      that has 0 for start and stop speeds ends the measurement. For each interval defined in
                        CDownSpeed, place the measured force, power, and time CDownResult table for the
16                      coast down being executed. Remaining entries should be set to 0.
17                      Perform a curve fit on the CDownResult data and place the coefficients in the memory
18                      table CDownMCoeff.

     19                 Repeat the coast down sequence for :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn:NRUNs

20                      After the last measurement, issue the process complete message and wait for a command.

21                      When commanded out of this procedure, clear the DYNO operation condition register
                        Coastdown Procedure bit indicating that the Coast down is not executing.
22
          19.8.1.2     :SOFFset <numeric_value>
23                   :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn:SOFFset

24                   Speed Offset - m/s

25                   This command sets how much speed offset above the top speed in the CDownSpeed Table to
                     which the dynamometer should be accelerated before beginning the coast down. This offset
26                   allows the dynamometer response to settle before coasting into the first speed segment.
                     At *RST, this value is set to 5.

          19-36   SOURce:FORCe
                                  1999 SCPI Command Reference

19.8.1.3     :NRUNs <numeric_value>
           :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn:NRUNs
           This command sets the number of coast downs to run.
           At *RST, this value is set to 3.
19.8.1.4     :RLDerivation
                                                                                                            1
           :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn:RLDerivation                                                                 2
           Road Load Derivation
                                                                                                            3
           This node contains the commands required to run a Dynamometer Road Load Derivation.
           This procedure will run a series of coast downs with the vehicle on the dyno to determine a
                                                                                                            4
           dyno-setting that will match the results from the track. The coast down procedure is defined     5
           by the SAE publication J2264 (See Appendix A - References for information on this
           publication.). Additional input for this procedure comes from the
                                                                                                            6
           :SOURce:FORCe:CONFigure node, CDownSpeed table, CDownDCoeff, CDownMCoeff,                        7
           and CDownResult table. The initial dynamometer coefficients (“best guess”) will be in the
           first row of CDownDCoeff prior to starting this procedure.
                                                                                                            8
19.8.1.4.1    :FACCeptance <numeric_value>
                                                                                                            9
           :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn:RLDerivation:FACCeptance                                                    10
           Force Acceptance - N
                                                                                                           11
           This command sets the maximum acceptable force difference between the force vs. speed
           curve derived from the dynamometer target and measured coefficients. This is the maximum
                                                                                                           12
           difference found at any of the specified coast down speed points.                               13
           At *RST, this value is set to 10.                                                               14
19.8.1.4.2    :INITiate                                                                                    15
           :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn:RLDerivation:INITiate
           This is an overlapped command. This command initiates the coast down simulation using the
                                                                                                           16
           current parameters in the :CONFigure node and CDownSpeed Table. This command                    17
           describes an event and therefore has no associated *RST condition.
                                                                                                           18
           When this command is initiated for dynamometers, the dynamometer must:
                                                                                                           19
              Check critical ancillaries, if any, for proper conditions: Brakes Off, Motor Contactor On,
              parameters within dynamometer safety limits. For conditions that prohibit operation of
                                                                                                           20
              this procedure, issue appropriate warning messages, and execute the Idle Procedure.          21
              Set the DYNO operation condition register Road Load Simulation Procedure bit                 22
              indicating that a Road Load Derivation is executing. Note: The DYNO operation
              condition register will be further defined in Volume 4.
                                                                                                           23
              Enter the theoretical data for the defined speed interval and configured parameters in
                                                                                                           24
              CDownResult table based on the target values in                                              25
              :SOURce:FORCe:CONFigure:VEHicle:TCOefficient and :TINertia.
                                                                                                           26
              Accelerate dynamometer to :SOURce:FORCe:CDOWn:SOFFset +(plus) the starting
              speed for the first coast down interval, at the rate in :SOURce:ACCeleration . If the

                                                                             SOURce:FORCe          19-37

                       dynamometer determines this speed is not appropriate for the defined coast down, set the

           wheels.

                     command. If set to “EXTernal”, then the simulation will include the grade from an external
                     analog input (Full Scale volts = 100% = 45(). “EXTernal” is used when a dynamometer is

19.9       FREQuency Subsystem
           SOURce:FREQuency
           The FREQuency subsystem controls the frequency characteristics of the instrument. Two
           types of controls are included in this subsystem. The first is frequency sensor controls, such
           as RANGe. The second is frequency sweep controls such as STARt, or tuning controls such
           as CW.                                                                                            1
           KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                                COMMENTS                    2
           :FREQuency                                                                                        3
              :CENTer              <numeric_value>
             [:CW|:FIXed]          <numeric_value>                                                           4
                :AUTO              <Boolean>|ONCE                                                            5
              :MANual              <numeric_value>
              :MODE                CW|FIXed|SWEep|LIST|SENSe                                                 6
              :MULTiplier          <numeric_value>                                                           7
              :OFFSet              <numeric_value>
              :RESolution          <numeric_value>                                                1992       8   RS001




                :AUTO              <Boolean> | ONCE                                               1992       9   RS001




              :SPAN                <numeric_value>
                :FULL                                                           [no query]                  10
                :HOLD              <Boolean>                                                                11
                :LINK              CENTer|STARt|STOP
              :STARt               <numeric_value>                                                          12
              :STOP                <numeric_value>                                                          13
19.9.1     :CENTer <numeric_value>                                                                          14
           SOURce:FREQuency:CENTer
           Sets the CENTer frequency.                                                                       15
           At *RST, this function will be set to (MINimum+MAX)/2.                                           16
19.9.2     [:CW|:FIXed] <numeric_value>                                                                     17
           SOURce:FREQuency:CW
                                                                                                            18
           The Continuous Wave or FIXed node is used to select a frequency of a non-swept signal.
           This node is optional. An optional node, such as [:CW|:FIXed], implies that the device shall     19
           accept and process commands with or without the optional node and have the same result.          20
           That is, the device is required to accept the optional node, if sent, without error. A device
           must accept both :CW and :FIXed if it implements this node.                                      21
           At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                         22
19.9.2.1     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE                                                                           23
           SOURce:FREQuency:CW:AUTO                                                                         24
           Couples the CW frequency to center frequency. Explicitly setting a value for
           FREQuency:CW sets AUTO OFF.                                                                      25
           At *RST, this value is set to ON.                                                                26
