          19.9.3    :MANual <numeric_value>
                    SOURce:FREQuency:MANual
                    Same as CW except limited by STARt and STOP. Receipt of this command will only change               Ed change




                    the frequency if SWEep:MODE MANual subsystem and FREQuency:MODE SWEep is
                    selected. If the sweep limits are changed such that manual frequency would be outside the
 1                  sweep limits, then the manual frequency will be set to the nearest end point of the sweep.
 2                  At *RST, FREQuency:MAN is device-dependent.
 3        19.9.4    :MODE CW|FIXed|SWEep|LIST|SENSe
 4                  SOURce:FREQuency:MODE
                    Determines which set of commands control the frequency subsystem. The settings have the
 5                  following meanings:
 6                             CW|FIXed: The frequency is determined by FREQuency[:CW] or
 7                             FREQuency[:FIXed]. CW and FIXed are aliases. Both must be implemented, if
                               either is implemented.
 8
                               SWEep: The source is in the swept mode and frequency is determined by
 9                             FREQuency:STARt, STOP, CENT, SPAN, and MAN.
10                             LIST: The source is in LIST sequence mode and frequency is determined by
11                             LIST:FREQuency.
12                             SENSe: The source is coupled to the sensor. All frequency controls are
                               determined by the SENSe:FREQuency block, except for OFFSet and MULTiplier.
13                             These two commands remain active under SOURce to allow for offset and
14                             harmonic tracking.
15                  At *RST, this value is set to CW.
16        19.9.5    :MULTiplier <numeric_value>
17                  SOURce:FREQuency:MULTiplier
                    Sets a reference multiplier for all other frequency settings in the instrument. All entered and
18                  displayed frequencies are affected by this command. The coupling equation is:
     19                     Entered|Displayed frequency = ( Hardware frequency * multiplier ) + offset
20                  This command affects the values of all functions which affect generation of the signal. This
                    includes such things as CW frequency and the sweep frequency controls. It does not affect
21                  things like input filter bandwidths. It does affect the settings of relative frequency parameters
22                  such as delta markers or FM deviation. Also note that this command does not affect the
                    hardware settings of the instrument, but only the entered and displayed frequencies.
23
                    At *RST, this value is set to 1.
24
          19.9.6    :OFFSet <numeric_value>
25                  SOURce:FREQuency:OFFSet
26                  Sets a reference frequency for all other absolute frequency settings in the instrument. This
                    command affects the values of all functions which affect generation of the signal. This
                    includes such things as CW frequency and the sweep frequency controls. It does not affect

          19-44    SOURce:FREQuency
                                   1999 SCPI Command Reference

           things like input filter bandwidths. It also does not affect the settings of relative frequency
           parameters such as delta markers or FM deviation. Also note that this command does not
           affect the hardware settings of the instrument, but only the entered and displayed
           frequencies. The coupling equation is:
                   Entered|Displayed frequency = ( Hardware frequency * multiplier ) + offset
                                                                                                              1
           At *RST, this value is set to 0.
                                                                                                              2

19.10   FUNCtion Subsystem
        SOURce:FUNCtion
        The function subsystem controls the shape and attributes of the output signal. The switch
        settings provided by this function are not horizontally compatible and represent what the
        source can be configured to generate directly.

        KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                              COMMENTS

        SOURce:FUNCtion:SHAPe                                                                        5
        Selects the shape of the output signal.                                                      6
        At *RST, the value of FUNCtion is device-dependent.                                          7
        The following SOURce functions are available for instruments:                                8
                   DC — An unvarying signal with respect to time.                                    9
                   IMPulse — IMPulse is an approximation of a zero width pulse                      10   HP022




                   PCHirp — PeriodicCHirp supplies a sine sweep over the current frequency span     11
                   which periodically repeats.                                                           HP022




                                                                                                    12
                   PRNoise — PeriodicRandomNoise provides a randomly varying signal with
                   respect to time which periodically repeats.                                      13   HP022




                   PULSe — A pulse, or string of pulses is generated.                               14
                   RANDom — provides a randomly varying signal with respect to time.                15   HP022




                   SINusoid — A sinusoidal signal is generated.                                     16
                   SQUare — A square wave signal is generated.                                      17
                   TRIangle — A triangular wave signal is generated.                                18
                   USER — The USER function allows the user to specify a periodic or arbitrary      19
                   waveform definition.

          19.11    LIST Subsystem
                   SOURce:LIST
                   The list subsystem controls automatic sequencing through associated lists of specified signal
                   values. It is also used to specify concurrent or simultaneous operation of the specified signal
                   in the associated lists. The various values are specified in the LIST subsystem commands.
 1                 The individual points in each of the list configuration commands are combined to make one
 2                 signal configuration.

 3                 The LIST subsystem controls a characteristic of the instrument when that subsystem’s mode
                   is set to LIST (such as :FREQuency:MODE LIST). Note that is permissible to have one
 4                 characteristic controlled by the list subsystem, and the others controlled by a different
 5                 subsystem (such as :FREQuency:MODE LIST or :POWer:MODE SWEep).

 6                 When employing multiple lists, all lists must be of the same length. If they are not all of the
                   same length, an error is generated at sequencing time. An exception is made for the case
 7                 where the shorter list is of length 1. In this case, the particular list is treated as though it were
 8                 a list of equal length, with all values being the same.

 9                 Lists are not affected by *RST.

19.11.10 :GENeration DSEQuence|SEQuence|DCONcurrent|CONCurrent                                                   13
            SOURce:LIST:GENeration
            The GENeration command is used to select how the defined lists are applied in a particular
                                                                                                                 14
            instrument. An instrument may support one or more of the generation modes. Selecting                 15
            Default SEQuence (DSEQuence) causes the instrument to cycle sequentially through the
            complete list in order. When SEQuence is selected, the sequence in which the list is used is
                                                                                                                 16

            the device to simultaneously generate all items in the list. When CONCurrent is selected, the
                                                                                                                 18
            list specified by the CONCurrent command defines which elements in the list are active
            simultaneously.                                                                                      19
            At *RST, GENeration shall be set to DSEQuence.                                                       20

          19.12    MARKer Subsystem
                   SOURce:MARKer
                   Selects between different markers, and adjusts the marker settings. The suffix with MARKer
                   selects the marker with the same number associated with it. If the suffix is omitted, then
                   marker #1 is assumed.
 1
                   KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                               COMMENTS
 2                 :MARKer
 3                    :AMPLitude          ON|OFF
                      :AOFF                                                            [no query]
 4                    :FREQuency          <numeric_value>
 5                    :MODE               FREQuency|POSition|DELTa
                      :POINt              <numeric_value>
 6                    :REFerence          <numeric_value>
 7                   [:STATe]             <Boolean>
                      :TIME               <numeric_value>
 8
          19.12.1 :AMPLitude <Boolean>
 9                 SOURce:MARKer:AMPLitude

10                 Controls whether the marker affects the signal. If ON, the signal is modified when the
                   marker frequency equals the output frequency. If OFF, only the marker output port is
11                 affected.
12                 At *RST, this value is set to OFF.
13        19.12.2 :AOFF
                   SOURce:MARKer:AOFF
14
                   Turns OFF all markers. This command is an event, and therefore has no query form. All
15                 markers shall be turned OFF at *RST.
16        19.12.3 :FREQuency <numeric_value>
                   SOURce:MARKer:FREQuency
17
                   Controls the absolute frequency of the specified marker when MARKer:MODE is
18                 FREQuency. When MARKer:MODE is DELTa, this command controls relative frequency.
     19            At *RST, this value is set to MINimum.
20        19.12.4 :MODE FREQuency|POSition|DELTa
                   SOURce:MARKer:MODE
21
                   This command controls whether the marker is tied to a frequency, referenced to an absolute
22                 trace point (position), or referenced to another marker (delta). If delta is selected,
23                 MARKer:REFerence determines which marker the current marker is referenced to.
24                 At *RST, this value is FREQuency.
25        19.12.5 :POINt <numeric_value>
                   SOURce:MARKer:POINt
26                 Sets the marker to the specified sweep point.
                   At *RST, this value is set to MINimum.

19.14   PM Subsystem
        SOURce:PM
        The Phase Modulation subsystem is used to set the modulation controls and the parameters
        associated with the modulating signal(s). The keywords to describe the carrier signal exist in
        other subsystems (such as FREQuency and PHASe).
                                                                                                          1
        KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                               COMMENTS
        :PM                                                                                               2
          [:DEViation]          <numeric_value>                                                           3
           :SENSitivity         <numeric_value>
           :MODE                LOCKed|UNLocked                                                           4
           :STATe               <Boolean>                                                                 5
           :SOURce              EXTernal|INTernal{,EXTernal|,INTernal}
           :COUPling            AC|DC|GROund                                                              6
           :POLarity            NORMal|INVerted                                                           7
           :INTernal
              :FREQuency        <numeric_value>                                                           8
           :EXTernal                                                                                      9
              :IMPedance        <numeric_value>
              :COUPling         AC|DC|GROund                                                             10
              :POLarity         NORMal|INVerted                                                          11
19.14.1 [:DEViation] <numeric_value>                                                                     12
        SOURce:PM:DEViation
        Sets the modulation DEViation of a PM signal. The unit for DEViation is radians. Where           13
        PM:DEViation is implemented, degree units must also be accepted. Radians must always be          14
        returned on a query. This command is used where the DEViation can be controlled
        independently from the modulating signal voltage level. Alternatively, it is used to set a       15
        device capability that can indicate when the desired DEViation has been achieved.                16
        At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                         17
19.14.2 :SENSitivity <numeric_value>                                                                     18
        SOURce:PM:SENSitivity
        Controls the modulation deviation by setting a sensitivity Modulation to the modulation          19
        signal voltage level. The unit for SENSitivity is radians/Volt (radians/V). Where                20
        PM:SENSitivity is implemented, degree/Volt (degree/V) units must also be accepted.
        Radians/Volt must always be returned on a query.                                                 21
        At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                         22
19.14.3 :MODE LOCKed|UNLocked                                                                            23
        SOURce:PM:MODE                                                                                   24
        Sets the synthesis mode employed in generating the PM signal. If MODE is set to LOCKed
        then a PLL is used in synthesizing the PM signal, to prevent frequency drift. If UNLocked        25
        the phase locked loop is inactive.                                                               26
        At *RST, this value is device-dependent.


                                                                               SOURce:PM         19-57
                                          1999 SCPI Command Reference

          19.14.4 :STATe <Boolean>
                   SOURce:PM:STATe
                   Turns phase modulation ON or OFF. Turning PM ON will not automatically turn OFF any
                   other types of modulation. Turning any or all modulations types ON or OFF must be done
                   explicitly. Where a type of modulation is active, turning ON another type of modulation will
 1                 add to the set of active modulations if that combination of capabilities are legal in the device.
 2                 Otherwise, an execution error -221 is generated and the instrument state is left undefined.
 3                 At *RST, this value must be set to OFF.
 4        19.14.5 :SOURce EXTernal|INTernal{,EXTernal|,INTernal}
                   SOURce:PM:SOURce
 5                 Selects the source for the modulating signal, and it may specify a single source or a number
 6                 of sources. The specified sources in the SOURce command are all selected and turned on.
                   Any sources from a previous selection that are not part of the current selection list are
 7                 deselected and turned off. If multiple sources are selected and the device does not support the
 8                 combination requested in the SOURce command, an execution error -221 must be generated.
 9                 Where multiple internal modulation sources are available, individual INTernal sources must
                   be distinguished by a unique number suffix. If no number suffix is provided in a command, a
10                 1 must be assumed.
11                 Where multiple external modulation sources are available, individual EXTernal sources must
12                 be distinguished by a unique number suffix. If no number suffix is provided in a command, a
                   1 must be assumed.
13
                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
14
          19.14.6 :COUPling AC|DC|GROund
15                 SOURce:PM:COUPling
16                 COUPling at this level is used to set the coupling between the modulator and the modulating
                   signal. The modulating signal may be the sum of several signals, either internal or external
17                 sources. If COUPling is set to DC, then both AC and DC components of the signal pass. AC
18                 coupling passes only the AC component of the signal. The GROund parameter allows the
                   modulation to be turned ON without the modulating signal connected.
     19
                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
20
          19.14.7 :POLarity NORMal|INVerted
21                 SOURce:PM:POLarity
22                 POLarity, at this level, is used to set the polarity between the modulator and the modulating
                   signal. The modulating signal may be the sum of several signals, either internal or external
23
                   sources. POLarity sets the relationship between the polarity of the applied modulation
24                 voltage and the resulting “direction” of modulation. The definition of “normal” polarity for
                   PM modulated signal is that a positive voltage causes the instantaneous output phase to
25
                   increase.
26
                   At *RST, this value must be set to NORMal.



          19-58   SOURce:PM
                                   1999 SCPI Command Reference

19.14.8 :INTernal
            SOURce:PM:INTernal

            numeric suffix signifying the particular internal signal source. If no number is given, a 1 is
            assumed.

            the internal signal source(s) to be controlled as a subsystem(s). The unit of FREQuency is
                                                                                                                4
            Hertz (Hz).                                                                                         5
            At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                            6
19.14.9 :EXTernal                                                                                               7
            SOURce:PM:EXTernal
            The EXTernal subsystem is used to control the specified external signal source. Where
                                                                                                                8
            multiple external modulation sources are available, the EXTernal keyword may have a                 9

            assumed.

            SOURce:PM:EXTernal:IMPedance                                                                       12

                                                                                                               14
19.14.9.2     :COUPling AC|DC|GROund
            SOURce:PM:EXTernal:COUPling                                                                        15
            COUPling, at this level, sets the coupling for only the specified external signal source. If       16
            COUPling is set to DC, then both AC and DC components of the signal pass. AC coupling
            passes only the AC component of the signal. The GROund parameter allows the specified
                                                                                                               17
            external source to be turned ON without being connected.                                           18
            At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                           19
19.14.9.3     :POLarity NORMal|INVerted                                                                        20
            SOURce:PM:EXTernal:POLarity
                                                                                                               21
            POLarity, at this level, sets the POLarity for only the specified external signal source.
            POLarity sets the relationship between the polarity of the applied modulation voltage and the      22
            resulting “direction” of modulation. The definition of “normal” polarity for PM modulated
                                                                                                               23
            signal is a positive voltage that causes the instantaneous output phase to increase.
                                                                                                               24
            At *RST, this value must be set to NORMal.

                      SOURce:PULM
                      The PULse Modulation subsystem is used to set the modulation controls and the parameters
                      associated with the modulating signal(s). The keywords to describe the carrier signal exist in
                      other subsystems (such as, FREQuency and PHASe).
 1
                      KEYWORD                 PARAMETER FORM                                COMMENTS
 2                    :PULM
 3                      :EXTernal
                           :HYSTeresis        <numeric_value>
 4                         :IMPedance         <numeric_value>

                           :POLarity          NORMal|INVerted
 6                      :INTernal
 7                         :FREQuency         <numeric_value>
                        :MODE                 FIXed|LIST                                                      1993        EM004

          19.16.1 :EXTernal
11                    SOURce:PULM:EXTernal

12                    The EXTernal subsystem is used to control the specified external signal source. Where
                      multiple external modulation sources are available, the EXTernal keyword may have a
13                    numeric suffix signifying the particular external signal source. If no number is given, a 1 is
14                    assumed.

15        19.16.1.1     :HYSTeresis <numeric_value>
                      SOURce:PULM:EXTernal:HYSTeresis
16                    Sets, for the specified signal source, how far the signal voltage must rise above (alternatively,
17                    fall below) the threshold LEVel before the carrier is turned ON from the OFF state (or turned
                      OFF from the ON state). The unit for HYSTeresis is Volts.
18
                      At *RST, this defaults to the TTL preset value.
     19
          19.16.1.2     :IMPedance <numeric_value>
20                    SOURce:PULM:EXTernal:IMPedance

21                    Sets the impedance of the specified external signal source. The unit for IMPedance is Ohms.
22                    At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
23        19.16.1.3     :LEVel <numeric_value>
                      SOURce:PULM:EXTernal:LEVel
24                    For the specified signal source, this sets the threshold voltage level used to turn ON the
25                    carrier. The unit for LEVel is Volts.
26                    At *RST, this defaults to the TTL preset value.



          19-68   SOURce:PULse Modulation
                                   1999 SCPI Command Reference

19.16.1.4     :POLarity NORMal|INVerted
            SOURce:PULM:EXTernal:POLarity
            POLarity, at this level, sets the POLarity for only the specified external signal source.
            POLarity sets the relationship between the polarity of the applied modulation voltage and the
            resulting “direction” of modulation. The definition of “normal” polarity for PULSe
            modulated signal is, a voltage more positive than some threshold (after applying hysteresis
                                                                                                                1
            effects) and causes the carrier to turn on.                                                         2
            At *RST, this value must be set to NORMal.                                                          3

            SOURce:PULM:INTernal
            The INTernal subsystem is used to control the specified internal signal source. Where
                                                                                                                5

            numeric suffix signifying the particular internal signal source. If no number is given, a 1 is
            assumed.

                                                                                                               10

19.16.4 :POLarity NORMal|INVerted                                                                              19
            SOURce:PULM:POLarity
                                                                                                               20
            POLarity, at this level, is used to set the polarity between the modulator and the modulating

          19.16.5 :SOURce EXTernal|INTernal{,EXTernal|,INTernal}
                   SOURce:PULM:SOURce
                   Selects the source for the modulating signal, and it may specify a single source or a number
                   of sources. The specified sources in the SOURce command are all selected and turned on.
                   Any sources from a previous selection are ignored. If multiple sources are selected and the
 1                 device does not support the combination requested in the SOURce command, an execution
 2                 error -221 must be generated.
 3                 Where multiple internal modulation sources are available, individual INTernal sources may
                   be distinguished by a unique numeric suffix. If no numeric suffix is provided in a command,
 4                 a 1 is assumed.
 5                 Where multiple external modulation sources are available, individual EXTernal sources must
 6                 be distinguished by a unique number suffix. If no number suffix is provided in a command, a
                   1 must be assumed.
 7
                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
 8
          19.16.6 :STATe <Boolean>
 9                 SOURce:PULM:STATe
10                 Turns Pulse Modulation ON or off. Turning ON PULse Modulation Modulation will not
                   automatically turn OFF any other types of modulation. Turning any or all modulations types
11                 ON or OFF must be done explicitly. Where a type of modulation is active, turning ON
12                 another type of modulation will add to the set of active modulations if that combination of
                   capabilities are legal in the device. Otherwise, an execution error -221 is generated and the
13                 instrument state is left undefined.
14                 At *RST, this value must be set to OFF.

          19.17.5 :DELay <numeric_value>
                      SOURce:PULSe:DELay
                      Sets the time from the start of the period to the first edge of the pulse. The fundamental units
                      for DELay is seconds.
 1                    At *RST, the value of this parameter is set to either 0 seconds or the nearest specified value.
 2        19.17.6 :DOUBle
                      SOURce:PULSe:DOUBle
 3                    This subsystem contains the commands necessary to control the parameters associated with
 4                    double pulse. When a double pulse is enabled, a second pulse which is identical to the
                      primary pulse is generated at some point during the period of the pulse. This second pulse
 5                    has the same characteristics as the first pulse, including width. A side effect is that since a
 6                    second pulse has been added, the actual duty cycle of the signal is twice that specified in
                      PULSe:DCYCle. Attempting to enable double pulse mode when the pulse width is greater
 7                    than:
 8                           (PULSE:PERiod-PULSe:DOUBle:DELay)/2
 9                    will cause an error -221, “Settings Conflict,” to be generated.
10        19.17.6.1     [:STATE] <Boolean>
                      SOURce:PULSe:DOUBle:STATE
11                    This command sets the double pulse mode to ON or OFF.
12                    At *RST, this parameter is set to OFF.
13        19.17.6.2     :DELay <numeric_value>
14                    SOURce:PULSe:DOUBle:DELay
                      Sets the time from the start of the period to the first edge of the second pulse. The
15                    fundamental units for DELay is seconds.
16                    At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
17        19.17.7 :TRANsition
18                    SOURce:PULSe:TRANsition
                      Collects together the commands to control the parameters associated with characteristics of
     19               the leading and trailing edges of the pulse.
20        19.17.7.1     :STATe <Boolean>
21                    SOURce:PULSe:TRANsition:STATe
                      Sets the transition mode to ON or OFF. If STATe is OFF, then the LEADing and TRAiling
22                    edges must be set to the minimum transition times available in the device. If STATe is ON,
23                    then the pulse transition times are specified by values for LEADing and TRAiling.

          19.20    SPEed Subsystem
                   SOURce:SPEed
                   This node controls the speed of the device.
                   KEYWORD                  PARAMETER FORM                              COMMENTS
 1                 :SPEed                                                                               1999
                      :INITiate                                                         [event; no query]1999
 2                   [:LEVel]               <numeric_value>                                             1999
 3                    :SSDLoss                                                                          1999
                         :INITiate                                                      [event; no query]1999

 6        19.20.1 :INITiate
                   :SOURce:SPEed:INITiate
 7                 This command initiates speed. This is an overlapped command. This command describes an
 8                 event and therefore has no associated *RST condition.

 9                 When this command is initiated for chassis dynamometers, the dynamometer must:

10                    Check critical ancillaries, if any, for proper conditions: Brakes Off, Motor Contactor On,
                      parameters within dynamometer safety limits. For conditions that prohibit operation of
11                    this procedure, issue appropriate warning messages, and execute the Idle Procedure.
12                    Set the DYNO operation condition register Go To Speed Procedure bit indicating Go To
13                    Speed Procedure is executing. Note: The DYNO operation condition register will be
                      further defined in Volume 4.
14
                      Accelerate dynamometer to the :SOURce:SPEed:LEVel speed point at the rate in
15                    :SOURce:ACCeleration. The dynamometer determines when the speed point has
16                    stabilized.

17                    Maintain speed and wait for a command.

18                    When commanded out of this procedure, clear the DYNO operation condition register Go
                      To Speed Procedure bit indicating the Go To Speed Procedure is not executing.
     19
                      Issue the process complete message.
20
          19.20.2 [:LEVel] <numeric_value>
21                 :SOURce:SPEed:LEVel

22                 Set the desired speed set-point in m/s.

23                 At *RST, this value is device dependent.

24        19.20.3 :SSDLoss
                   SOURce:SPEed:SSDLoss
25                 Steady State Driveline Loss
26                 This node describes the procedure to measure the driveline loss forces as a function of speed.
                   The Steady State Driveline Procedure measures the vehicle losses due to vehicle drive train


          19-82   SOURce:SPEed
                                   1999 SCPI Command Reference

            components. The vehicle losses are measured by operating the dynamometer at various
            selected speeds and measuring the force required to maintain the constant speed over a
            specified time interval. The results are stored in the DrvLLoss pre-defined table. This table
            has two columns, SPEed, the speeds at which the losses are to be measured (input) and
            LOSS, the measured losses at each speed (result). Coefficients for vehicle driveline losses
            are determined at the end of the procedure and reside in DrvLCoeff.
                                                                                                               1
19.20.3.1     :INITiate
                                                                                                               2
            :SOURce:SPEed:SSDLoss:INITiate                                                                     3
            This is an overlapped command. The command uses the speed points defined in the
            :MEMory:TABLe:SELect DrvLLoss. This command describes an event and therefore has no
                                                                                                               4
            associated *RST condition.                                                                         5
            When this procedure is initiated for dynamometers, the dynamometer must:                           6
               Check critical ancillaries, if any, for proper conditions: Brakes Off, Motor Contactor On,      7
               parameters within dynamometer safety limits. For conditions that prohibit operation of
               this command, issue appropriate warning messages, and execute the Idle Procedure.               8
               Set the DYNO operation condition register Driveline Loss Procedure bit indicating the           9
               driveline loss is executing. Note: The DYNO operation condition register will be further       10
               defined in Volume 4.
                                                                                                              11
               Accelerate dynamometer to the first speed point defined in the DrvLLoss memory table
               at the rate in :SOURce:ACCeleration.                                                           12
               Stabilize at this speed for :SOURce:SPEed:SSDLoss:STIMe. If the speed does not                 13
               stabilize, set Failed to Stabilize bit of the DYNO questionable condition register and         14
               continue with the procedure.
                                                                                                              15
               Average the force at the roll surface required to maintain the speed set point over the loss
               average time :SOURce:SPEed:SSDLoss:LATime. The average force value is placed in                16
               the DrvLLoss memory table for the specified speed point. Repeat steps 3 to 5 for each          17
               point in the DrvLLoss table. The first zero speed in the DrvLLoss table ends the
               procedure.                                                                                     18
               Perform a curve fit on the DrvLLoss data and place the coefficients in the memory table        19
               DrvLCoeff.                                                                                     20
               Clear the DYNO operation condition register bit 7 indicating the driveline loss is not         21
               executing.
                                                                                                              22
               Issue the process complete message.
                                                                                                              23
               Execute the Idle Procedure.
                                                                                                              24
19.20.3.2     :LATime <numeric_value>
            :SOURce:SPEed:SSDLoss:LATime                                                                      25
            Loss Averaging Time - sec                                                                         26

                                             1999 SCPI Command Reference

                      This command sets the time after stabilization that the losses are to be averaged before
                      moving to the next speed point.
                      At *RST, this value is set to 5.

            SOURce:SWEep:TIME:AUTO

          19.21.2.1     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
                      SOURce:SWEep:DWELl:AUTO
                      When AUTO ON is selected, the dwell time is coupled to the sweep time and number of
                      points. The coupling equation is:
                              DWELl=(TIME/POINts)-(device-dependent stepping time)
 1
                      Setting a value for dwell turns AUTO OFF.
 2
                      At *RST, AUTO is set to ON.
 3
          19.21.3 :DIRection UP|DOWN
 4                    SOURce:SWEep:DIRection
 5                    Controls the direction of the sweep. If UP is selected, the sweep is carried out in ascending
                      order, from STARt to STOP. If DOWN is selected, the sweep is carried out in descending
 6                    order, from STOP to STARt.
 7                    At *RST, the value of this function is UP.
 8        19.21.4 :MODE AUTO|MANual
 9                    SOURce:SWEep:MODE
                      Selects the sweep conditions for the sweep. The various conditions are:
10

12                              command, such as, FREQuency:MANual. This setting is valid only if the
13                              :MANual capability has been implemented.
                      At *RST, this function is set to AUTO.

          19.21.5 :SPACing LINear|LOGarithmic
15                    SOURce:SWEep:SPACing
16                    Determines the swept entity versus time characteristics of the sweep. The various settings
                      have the following meanings:
17
                                LINear: For stepped sweeps, the swept entity is incremented (decremented) by the
18                              step size until the sweep limit is reached. For analog sweeps, a linear ramp is
     19                         generated.
20                              LOGarithmic: For non-linear sweeps, step size is determined by a logarithmic
                                curve fitted between the start and stop frequency. Stepping is determined by the
21                              SWEep:POINts. For analog sweeps, a logarithmic ramp is generated.
22                    At *RST, this value is set to LINear.
23        19.21.6 :GENeration STEPped|ANALog
                      SOURce:SWEep:GENeration
24                    Selects between an analog or stepped sweep.
25                              STEPped: A stepped sweep is selected, and the points are controlled by the
26                              SWEep:POINts and SWEep:STEP settings.
                                ANALog: The sweep is controlled by an analog signal.


          19-86   SOURce:SWEep

        At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
19.21.7 :STEP <numeric_value>

        GENeration is ANALog or if SPACing is LOGarithmic.                                                1

               STEP=SPAN/(POINts-1)                                                            1991

              STEP = SPAN/(POINts-1)                                                       1991           9   HP045




        If POINts are changed, STEP will also be changed, but not SPAN. In a logarithmic sweep,          10

               POINts/DECADE = (POINts-1)/SPAN (in decades)                               1991

19.22.3 :LCONstants
            SOURce:TEMPerature:LCONstants
            A temperature chamber is a closed loop thermal system. The Loop CONstants of such a
            system determine its performance. These loop constants are popularly known as pid.
            The p is the proportional or GAIN control and can be imagined as a coarse control. The i is      1
            the integral (lead) compensator and d is the derivative (lag) compensator. These two
            compensators are additional controls to fine tune the system. The INTegral value improves
                                                                                                             2
            the steady-state error and the DERivative value improves the transient response of a             3
            feedback control system.
                                                                                                             4
            For further information on feedback control systems please refer to Vol 1: Syntax and Style -
            Chapter 2, Tuning a Control Loop Performance
                                                                                                             5
19.22.3.1     :DERivative <numeric_value>
                                                                                                             6
            SOURce:TEMPerature:LCONstants:DERivative                                                         7
            The DERivative, which is also called a lead compensator, is used to improve the transient
            response of the system. The unit for DERivative is (currently selected units) degrees per
                                                                                                             8
            second.                                                                                          9
            With both GAIN and DERivative are specified, the output (heat/cold) is proportional to the      10
            input signal plus its derivative. This is shown in the figure below using Laplace transform
            notation.
                                                                                                            11

            At *RST the value is device dependent.                                                          18
19.22.3.2     [:GAIN] <numeric_value>                                                                       19
            SOURce:TEMPerature:LCONstants:GAIN
                                                                                                            20
            The value of :GAIN determines the time required to reach the target temperature. The higher
            the value of gain, the sooner the target temperature is achieved. The GAIN is a unitless        21
            quantity.                                                                                       22
            At *RST the value is device dependent.                                                          23
19.22.3.3     :INTegral <numeric_value>                                                                     24
            SOURce:TEMPerature:LCONstants:INTegral
            The INTegral, which is also called a lag compensator, is used to minimize the steady-state      25
            error.                                                                                          26


                                                                       SOURce:TEMPerature 19-89
                                             1999 SCPI Command Reference

                      When the steady-state error is too large, it is possible to minimize this value by adjusting the
                      value of INTegral. The units for INTegral are degree*seconds.
                      With both GAIN and INTegral are specified, the output (heat/cold) is proportional to the
                      input signal plus its integral. This is shown in the figure below using Laplace transform

19.23   VOLTage Subsystem

        There is only one subsystem for each of the main amplitude characteristics of the signal.
        Thus, AC voltage and DC voltage are both placed under the VOLTage subsystem. A device        1

20   STATus Subsystem                                                                                    TK012
     This subsystem controls the SCPI-defined status-reporting structures. SCPI defines, in
     addition to those in IEEE 488.2, QUEStionable, OPERation, Instrument SUMmary and
     INSTrument registers. These registers conform to the IEEE 488.2 specification and each
     may be comprised of a condition register, an event register, an enable register, and negative       1
     and positive transition filters. The purpose and definition of the SCPI-defined registers is        2
     described in “Volume 1: Syntax and Style”.
                                                                                                         3
     SCPI also defines an IEEE 488.2 queue for status. The queue provides a human readable
     record of instrument events. The application programmer may individually enable events              4
     into the queue. STATus:PRESet enables errors and disables all other events. If the summary          5
     of the queue is reported, it shall be reported in bit 2 of the status byte register. A subset of
     error/event numbers is defined by SCPI. Additional error/event numbers will be defined at a         6
     later date.                                                                                         7

24                 The status reporting commands are orthogonal. Status register bits are classified as either
                   terminal (reporting a single class of events) or summary (reporting several classes of events).
25
                   Summary bits have the same register structure behind them. This is called register fan-out.
26                 The commands to access each register are always the same and are described below. The
                   name of each subsystem follows the name of the associated bit in the next higher status


          20-2   STATus Subsystem
                                 1999 SCPI Command Reference

         structure. Therefore, the event register associated with the frequency error bit of the
         questionable signal/data register set would be accessed by the command:
             STATus:QUEStionable:FREQuency:EVENt?
         Certain commands in this subsystem are required to be implemented by all SCPI
         instruments. These commands are described in section 4.2.1 of “Volume 1: Syntax and                    1
         Style.”
                                                                                                                2
         The parameters to the commands are described as <NRf> as defined in IEEE 488.2 and not
         as SCPI’s <numeric_value>. This means that UP, DOWN, MINimum, and MAXimum are
                                                                                                                3
         not accepted for these commands. When a STATus command is queried, the return form                     4
         shall always be an <NR1> value.
                                                                                                                5
         The following commands can be applied to all SCPI registers by prefixing the command
         with the node(s) that represent the particular register to be controlled.
                                                                                                                6
20.1     :OPERation                                                                                             7
         STATus:OPERation
                                                                                                                8
         The OPERation status register contains conditions which are part of the instrument’s normal
         operation.                                                                                             9
         See Volume 1 Section 9.3 for more detailed information.                                               10
20.1.1   :BIT<n>                                                                                               11
         STATus:OPERation:BIT<n>
                                                                                                               12
         This command accesses the user-definable bits in the OPERation register set. The value of
         <n> is restricted from 8 to 12 and represents bits 8 through 12 in the :STATus:OPERation              13
         status register. This allows standardized access to user-definable terminal and summary bits.         14
20.1.2   :CONDition?                                                                                           15
         STATus:OPERation:CONDition?
         Returns the contents of the condition register associated with the status structure defined in        16
         the command. Reading the condition register is nondestructive.                                        17
         The response is (NR1 NUMERIC RESPONSE DATA) (range: 0 through 32767) unless                           18
         changed by the :FORMat:SREGister command.
                                                                                                               19
20.1.3   :ENABle <NRf> | <non-decimal numeric>
         STATus:OPERation:ENABle                                                                               20
         Sets the enable mask which allows true conditions in the event register to be reported in the         21
         summary bit. If a bit is 1 in the enable register and its associated event bit transitions to true,
         a positive transition will occur in the associated summary bit.                                       22
         The command accepts parameter values of either format in the range 0 through 65535                    23
                                                                                                               TK046
         (decimal) without error.                                                                              24
         The query response format is <NR1> unless changed by the :FORMat:SREGister command.                   25

25        20.2       :PRESet
                     STATus:PRESet
26                   The PRESet command is an event that configures the SCPI and device-dependent status data
                     structures such that device-dependent events are reported at a higher level through the


          20-4     STATus Subsystem
                       1999 SCPI Command Reference

mandatory part of the status-reporting mechanism. Device-dependent events are summarized
in the mandatory structures. The mandatory structure is defined in part by IEEE 488.2;
SCPI-required structures compose the rest. The mandatory part of the status-reporting
mechanism provides a device-independent interface for determining the gross status of a
device.
                                                                                                   1
The PRESet command affects only the enable register, the transition filter registers, and          TK012
queue enabling for the SCPI-mandated and device-dependent status data structures. PRESet
                                                                                                   2
does not affect either the “status byte” or the “standard event status” as defined by IEEE         3
488.2. PRESet does not clear any of the event registers or any item from the error/event
queue. The *CLS command is used to clear all event registers and queues in the device
                                                                                                   4
status-reporting mechanism.                                                                        5
For the device-dependent status data structures, the PRESet commands shall set the enable          6
                                                                                                   TK012
register to all 1’s and the transition filter register to a device-dependent value. The
device-dependent value shall be either PTR, NTR, or both, such that the device-dependent
                                                                                                   7
event shall be propagated to the structure that summarizes that event. For the SCPI                8
mandatory status data structures, the PRESet command shall set the transition filter registers
to recognize only positive transitions and set the enable register to 0’s. The PREset
                                                                                                   9
command shall also set error/event queue enabling to report only errors.                          10
An application may select the events that shall cause a service request at the mandatory SCPI     11
status data structure level, rather than excluding those that are of no interest to the
application. Further, there is no requirement on the application to set up the
                                                                                                  12
device-dependent structures for normal device operation.                                          13
For this concept to be extended to encompass the IEEE 488.2-mandated status data                  14
structures, the following sequence of commands is required when initializing the device:
                                                                                                  15
          *CLS – Clears all event status registers and queues                                      TK012
                                                                                                  16
          *SRE 0 – Clears the IEEE 488.2-mandated service request enable register
                                                                                                  17
          *ESE 0 – Clears the IEEE 488.2-mandated standard event status enable register
                                                                                                  18
          STATus:PRESet – Presets all other registers and queues                                   TK012
                                                                                                  19

20.3     :QUEStionable
         STATus:QUEStionable?
         The QUEStionable status register set contains bits which give an indication of the quality of
         various aspects of the signal.
         A bit set in the condition register indicates that the data currently being acquired or             1
         generated is of questionable quality due to some condition affecting the parameter associated
         with that bit. For example, if the FREQ bit were set, this would mean that the frequency            2
         accuracy of the signal was of questionable quality.                                                 3
         See Volume 1 Section 9.4 for more detailed information.                                             4
20.3.1   :BIT<n>                                                                                             5
         :STATus:QUEStionable:BIT<n>
         This command accesses the user-definable bits in the QUEStionable register set. The value           6
         of <n> is restricted from 9 to 12 and represents bits 9 through 12 in the                           7
         :STATus:QUEStionable status register. This allows standardized access to user-definable
         terminal and summary bits.                                                                          8
         Note that this definition is different from that of :STATus:OPERation:BIT in that the bit           9
         number is restricted to the range of 9 through 12, while the range for                             10
         :STATus:OPERation:BIT is restricted to 8 through 12.
                                                                                                            11

         STATus:QUEStionable:CONDition?                                                                     12
         Defined the same as STATus:OPERation:CONDition. See Section 20.1.2 for details.                    13

         Defined the same as STATus:OPERation:ENABle. See Section 20.1.3 for details.                       15

21   SYSTem Subsystem
     The SYSTem subsystem collects the functions that are not related to instrument
     performance. Examples include functions for performing general housekeeping and
     functions related to setting global configurations, such as TIME or SECurity.

21.1     :ALTernate <numeric_value>
         SYSTem:ALTernate                                                                               11
         Selects an alternate instrument state, which is swapped with the current state at the end of   12
         some specified action. The <numeric_value> selects which of the states will be used. The
         states are created with the *SAV command. The action is generally sweep, list sequencing or    13
         some programmable delay, depending on the device configuration.                                14
         At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                       15
21.1.1   :STATe <Boolean>                                                                               16
         SYSTem:ALTernate:STATe
         Controls whether the alternate state mode is enabled. While it is ON, the device shall swap    17
         the active state with the one stored in the register specified in ALTernate.                   18
         At *RST, this parameter is set to OFF.                                                         19
21.2     :BEEPer                                                                                        20
         SYSTem:BEEPer
                                                                                                        21
         This subsystem controls the audible beeper of the instrument.
                                                                                                        22
21.2.1   :FREQuency <numeric_value>
         SYSTem:BEEPer:FREQuency                                                                        23
         Programs the frequency of audible tones. It also sets the default frequency for the            24
         [:IMMediate] command. The parameter is specified in Hz. The range of valid parameters is
         instrument-dependent.                                                                          25
         At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                       26


                                                                         SYSTem:ALTernate 21-3
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

          21.2.2     [:IMMediate][<frequency>[,<time>[,<volume>]]]
                     SYSTem:BEEPer:IMMediate
                     The receipt of this command causes an audible tone to be generated by the instrument. Note
                     that this command generates an event and therefore it has no associated *RST state or query
                     form.
 1
                     The allowable values of the parameters <frequency>, <time> and <volume> are
 2                   instrument-dependent. The frequency parameter is specified in Hz. The duration time
 3                   parameter is specified in seconds. The volume parameter range is from 0 to 1, with 1
                     indicating the maximum volume that the instrument can produce and 0 indicating minimum
 4                   volume.
 5        21.2.3     :STATe <Boolean>
 6                   SYSTem:BEEPer:STATe
                     Enables/disables the beeper. When STATe OFF is selected, no instrument condition, except
 7                   the :SYSTem:BEEPer:IMMediate command, shall cause an audible beep to be emitted.
 8                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
 9        21.2.4     :TIME <numeric_value>
10                   SYSTem:BEEPer:TIME
                     Programs the duration of audible tones. It also sets the default duration for the [:IMMediate]
11                   command. The parameter is specified in seconds. The range of valid parameters is
12                   instrument-dependent.
13                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
14        21.2.5     :VOLume <numeric_value>
                     SYSTem:BEEPer:VOLume
15                   Programs the volume of audible tones. It also sets the default volume for the [:IMMediate]
16                   command. The parameter range is from 0 to 1, with 1 indicating the maximum volume that
                     the instrument can produce and 0 indicating minimum volume. Actual sound pressure levels
17                   generated by any particular volume setting are instrument-dependent.
18                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
19        21.3       :CAPability?                                                                                     TWV41C
20                   SYSTem:CAPability?
                     This query returns an <instrument_specifier>. See the Compliance section in the                  TWV41C
     21              introduction to Instrument Class Applications.

21.4.1.1     :FEED <data_handle>                                                                           HP063e
           SYSTem:COMMunicate:CENTronics:FEED
           Sets or queries what data is used to FEED the remote device. Data may be streamed to an
           external device without sending it through the HCOPy subsystem, for example by directly
           feeding SENSe or CALCulate data, where no page formatting commands are needed. That
           is, the SYSTem:COMMunicate subsystem shall not add any page formatting to the output
                                                                                                            1
           stream, where this is required HCOPy should be used.                                             2
           At *RST, FEED is device dependent.                                                               3
21.4.2     :GPIB                                                                                            4
           SYSTem:COMMunicate:GPIB
           The GPIB subsystem controls the physical configuration of a GPIB (IEEE 488) port.
                                                                                                            5
21.4.2.1     :RDEVice
                                                                                                            6
                                                                                                           HP063e
           SYSTem:COMMunicate:GPIB:RDEVice                                                                  7
           The Remote DEVice subsystem configures how the instrument uses a peripheral device,
           such as a printer or plotter, connected to a GPIB port.
                                                                                                            8
21.4.2.1.1    :ADDRess <numeric_value>[,<numeric_value>]
                                                                                                            9
                                                                                                           HP063e
           SYSTem:COMMunicate:GPIB:RDEVice:ADDRess                                                         10
           Sets or queries the bus address of the peripheral device. The first parameter is the primary
           address and the optional second parameter is the secondary address. Changing the address
                                                                                                           11
           with this does not affect the address of the peripheral device. It does affect the address to   12
           which data is sent by the instrument.
                                                                                                           13
           At *RST, the value of this parameter is device dependent.
                                                                                                           14
21.4.2.1.2    :FEED <data_handle>                                                                          HP063e
           SYSTem:COMMunicate:GPIB:RDEVice:FEED                                                            15
           Sets or queries what data is used to FEED the peripheral device. Data may be streamed to an     16
           external device without sending it through the HCOPy subsystem, for example by directly
           feeding SENSe or CALCulate data, where no page formatting commands are needed. That
                                                                                                           17
           is, the SYSTem:COMMunicate subsystem shall not add any page formatting to the output            18
           stream. Where page formatting is required, HCOPy should be used.
                                                                                                           19
           At *RST, FEED is device dependent.
                                                                                                           20
21.4.2.2     [:SELF]                                                                                       HP063e
           SYSTem:COMMunicate:GPIB[:SELF]
                                                                                                           21
           The SELF subsystem sets the configuration relating to the GPIB port on the instrument itself.   22
21.4.2.2.1    :ADDRess <numeric_value>[,<numeric_value>]                                                   23
                                                                                                           HP063e
           SYSTem:COMMunicate:GPIB[:SELF]:ADDRess
                                                                                                           24
           Sets the GPIB address of the instrument. The first parameter is the primary address and the
           optional second parameter is the secondary address.                                             25
           *RST has no effect on the value of these parameters.                                            26

          21.4.3     :SERial
                     SYSTem:COMMunicate:SERial
                     Controls the physical configuration of a serial port, such as RS-232-D, RS-422, or
                     EIA/TIA-562. Any command that changes the configuration of the port takes effect
                     immediately upon receipt of the Program Message Terminator.
 1                                                                                                                   TK014
                     *RST has no effect on the value of these parameters.
 2
          21.4.3.1     :CONTrol
 3                   SYSTem:COMMunicate:SERial:CONTrol                                                                   HP047




 4                   Add command which independently sets the mode in which DTR and RTS pacing operate.
                     Since hardware handshaking can be configured to pertain to either transmit, receive, or both,
 5                   a CONTrol branch separate from the transmit and receive branches was added.
 6        21.4.3.1.1   :DTR ON|OFF|STANdard|IBFull                                                                   TK014
 7                   SYSTem:COMMunicate:SERial:CONTrol:DTR
                     Sets the hardware pacing scheme.
 8                                                                                                                   TK014
                     The ON parameter indicates that the DTR line should always be asserted (held in the ON
 9                   condition).
                                                                                                                     TK014
10                   The OFF parameter indicates that the DTR line should always be unasserted (held in the
11                   OFF condition).
                                                                                                                     TK014
12                   When the STANdard option is set for DTR, the DTR line behaves as specified in the EIA
                     standard RS-232-D section 4.4. As stated in the standard:
13
                        “Signals on this circuit are used to control the switching of the DCE to the
14                      communication channel. The ON condition prepares the DCE to be connected to the
15                      communication channel and maintains the connection established by external means.”
                                                                                                                     TK014
16                   A common use of the DTR line that has evolved is that of pacing. The IBFull parameter sets
                     the DTR line to indicate when the device is ready to receive. When the number of received
17                   bytes in the input buffer of the device reaches the STOP threshold the device will de-assert
18                   the DTR line. When the number of bytes has been reduced to the STARt threshold, the
                     device will assert DTR indicating that it can receive input again. The device will also
19                   monitor the state of DSR and CTS and will stop transmission if either of those lines becomes
20                   de-asserted.
                                                                                                                     TK014
     21              *RST has no effect on the value of this parameter.
22        21.4.3.1.2   :RTS ON|OFF|STANdard|IBFull|RFR
                     SYSTem:COMMunicate:SERial:CONTrol:RTS
23
                     Sets the hardware pacing (hand-shaking) scheme.
                                                                                                                     TK014
24
                     The ON parameter indicates that the RTS line should always be asserted.
                                                                                                                     TK014
25
                     The OFF parameter indicates that the RTS line should always be unasserted.
                                                                                                                     TK014
26
                     When the STANdard option is set for RTS, the RTS line behaves as specified in the EIA
                     standard RS-232-D section 4.4. As stated in the standard:

          21-6     SYSTem:COMMunicate
                                  1999 SCPI Command Reference

              “This circuit is used to condition the local DCE for data transmission and on a
              half-duplex channel, to control the direction of data transmission of the local DCE.”
                                                                                                            TK014
           A common use of the RTS line that has evolved is that of pacing. Many high speed
           asynchronous modems use this line (paired with CTS) as receive/transmit pacing. The IBFull
           or its alias RFR (Ready For Receiving) parameter sets the RTS line to indicate when the          1
           device is ready to receive. When the number of received bytes in the input buffer of the
           device reaches the STOP threshold the device will de-assert the RTS line. When the number
                                                                                                            2
           of bytes has been reduced to the STARt threshold, the device will assert RTS, indicating that    3
           it can receive input again. The device will also monitor the state of CTS and will stop
           transmission if that line becomes de-asserted.
                                                                                                            4
                                                                                                            TK014
           The IBFull (RFR) mode follows the CCITT Recommendations V.42, Section 7.3.1, “Flow
                                                                                                            5
           Control across the DTE/DCE interface, Option a) Using Circuit 133 and 106.”                      6
                                                                                                            TK014
           *RST has no effect on the value of this parameter.                                               7

          21.4.4     :SOCKet <n>
                     :SYSTem:COMMunicate:SOCKet<n>
                     This command identifies the socket to be opened. The syntax of the numeric suffix is as
 1                   specified in 6.2.5.2 in Volume 1, Syntax and Style.
 2        21.4.4.1     :ADDRess <string>
                     :SYSTem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:ADDRess
 3                   This command allows the user to enter the IP address or host name of the remote device. If it
 4                   is an IP address, it is specified using IP dot notation (e.g. 123.45.67.89). If it is a host name,
                     it is specified by using the host name string (e.g., my_host).
 5
          21.4.4.2     :CONNect
 6                   :SYSTem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:CONNect
 7                   This command implements the socket connection.
 8        21.4.4.3     :DISConnect
                     :SYSTem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:DISConnect
 9                   The Disconnect command breaks the socket connection.
10        21.4.4.4     :FEED <n> <data_handle>{,<data_handle>}

                     Sets or queries what data is used to FEED the communications socket.
12
                     Note: There can be multiple FEEDs for the same socket.

          21.4.4.4.1    :OCONdition <event_handle>
14                   :SYSTem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:FEED:OCONdition
15                   The On Condition command, :OCONditon, defines the rate at which data will be collected
                     and sent to the socket FEED.
16
          21.4.4.4.2    :SCONdition <event_handle>
17                   :SYSTem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:FEED:SCONdition
18                   The Send Condition, SCONdition, defines the rate at which the data will be transmitted on
                     the socket.
19
          21.4.4.5     :LISTen
20                   :SYSTem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:LISTen
     21              The LISTen command instructs the device (instrument) to listen for a connection on the
                     specified socket. This will allow data channels from one instrument to another instrument to
22                   be opened.

21.4.4.7     :TYPE TCP|UDP
           :SYSTem:COMMunicate:SOCKet :TYPE
           This command allows the user to select the type of Ethernet port to be opened, either TCP or
           UPD. The query form will return either TCP or UDP.

                                                                                                            2

           either be a module number or a user-defined card name. If the parameter is ALL, then all         3

           Any instrument which has an internal calendar shall implement the following command to
           set the calendar:
                                                                                                           11

                                                                                                           12
                     by the capability of the instrument. The year shall be entered as a four-digit        13
                     number, including century and millennium information.
                                                                                                           14
           <month>: Must be <numeric_value>. It is rounded to the nearest integer. Its range is 1 to 12
                    inclusive. The number 1 corresponds to the month January, 2 to February, and so
                                                                                                           15
                    on.                                                                                    16
           <day>:    Must be <numeric_value>. It is rounded to the nearest integer. Its range is 1 to      17
                     number of days in the month from the previous parameter. A device
                                                                                                           18
                     implementing this command shall keep track of the number of days in each
                     month, accounting for leap years through the range of years that it accepts.          19
           The response message shall consist of three fields separated by commas:                         20
                  <year>,<month>,<day>
                                                                                                           21
           <year>:   NR1 format. Range is device-dependent.
                                                                                                           22
           <month>: NR1 format. Range is 1 to 12.
                                                                                                           23
           <day>:    NR1 format. Range is 1 to 31.
                                                                                                           24
           This shall not be affected by a *RST command.
