          24.5       ABORt
11                   ABORt

12                   The ABORt command resets the trigger system and places all trigger sequences in the IDLE
                     state. Any actions related to the trigger system that are in progress, such as a sweep or
13                   acquiring a measurement, shall also be aborted as quickly as possible. The ABORt command
14                   shall not be considered complete until all trigger sequences are in the IDLE state. The
                     execution of an ABORt command shall set false the pending operation flags that were set by
15
                     the initiation of the trigger system.
16
                     This command is an event and has no associated *RST condition or query form.
17
          24.6       ARM
18                   ARM

19                   The purpose of the ARM subsystem is to qualify a single event or a sequence of events
                     before enabling the TRIGger. The ARM subsystem for a given sequence may be omitted if
20
                     TRIGger does not require additional qualification by other events.
21
          24.6.1     [:SEQuence]
22                   ARM:SEQuence

23                   SEQuence is used in the expanded capability model to identify a particular sequence of       ACQ01B
                     layers in the trigger system. A <sequence_name>, see 24.4.2, may also be used here.
     24
          24.6.1.1     :DEFine <sequence_name>
25                   ARM:SEQuence:DEFine

26                   Sets or queries the SEQuence alias. This command is required where aliases are employed      ACQ01B
                     and they do not correspond to the standard mapping. The numeric suffix on SEQuence
                     corresponds to the sequence number to which the alias is to be applied.

          24-12    TRIGger Subsystem ABORt
                               1999 SCPI Command Reference

         This command is an alias to TRIGger:SEQuence:DEFine. Changing the value of                   ACQ01B
         ARM:SEQuence:DEFine changes the value of TRIGger:SEQuence:DEFine to the same
         value.
         The <sequence_name> is character data.                                                       TK028A
         The effect of <sequence_name> is modified by DEFine:MGRules as follows:
                                                                                                           1
                                                                                                      TK028A
                    Regardless of the state or presence of DEFine:MGRules, there is no difference
                                                                                                           2
                                                                                                         TK028A
                    between uppercase and lowercase letters used in <sequence_name>.                       3
                    If the command DEFine:MGRules is absent or set to OFF, the                             4
                                                                                                         TK028A
                    full<sequence_name> as written is the only form allowed.
                                                                                                           5
                    For example, if the <sequence_name> were SAMPLE1, then SAMPLE1 is the                  6
                    only alias accepted.
                                                                                                           7
                    If the command DEFine:MGRules is present and set to ON, the                          TK028A
                    <sequence_name> is interpreted as <program_mnemonic>[<numeric_suffix>]
                                                                                                           8
                    where all the contiguous trailing digits form the <numeric_suffix>. Mnemonic           9
                    generation rules as described in Syntax and Style, Section 6.2.1. shall apply to the
                    <program_mnemonic> and the <numeric suffix>.
                                                                                                          10
                                                                                                          11
                    For example, if the <sequence_name> were defined as VECTOR or VECTOR1,
                    then VECT, VECT1, VECTOR, and VECTOR1 would all be acceptable aliases.
                                                                                                          12
         If the <sequence_name> is identical to a keyword under ARM or TRIGger subsystem, the
                                                                                                          13
                                                                                                         ACQ01B
         device shall report execution error -224. For example ARM:SEQuence2:DEFine FILTER                14
         will cause an error. This command shall accept any other valid character program data for
         <sequence_name>.
                                                                                                          15
         The query returns a string which contains the <sequence_name>, so that a null string can
                                                                                                          16
                                                                                                         ACQ01B
         indicate that nothing is defined.                                                                17
         If the command DEFine:MGRules is present and set to ON, the returned <sequence_name>             18
                                                                                                         TK028A

                                                                                                          19
         Interpreting Command Tables. An omitted <numeric_suffix> or a <numeric_suffix> of 1
         will be represented as [1].                                                                      20
         For example, if <sequence_name> is VECTOR1 then the response is “VECTor[1]”; if it is            21
                                                                                                         TK028A
         DELAYED2, the response is “DELayed2”; if it is SAMPLE, the response is “SAMPle[1]”.
                                                                                                          22
         By executing this command the previously defined name is overwritten.                           ACQ01B

          24.6.1.2       [:LAYer]
                     ARM:SEQuence:LAYer

                     LAYer is used in the expanded capability model to identify a particular ARM LAYer in the
                     trigger system.
                                                                                                                        FL003




 1
          24.6.1.2.1     :COUNt <numeric_value>
 2                   ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:COUNt

 3                   COUNt controls the path of the trigger system in the upward traverse of the event detection
                     layer, shown in figure 24-4, “Event Detection Layer.” The trigger system is directed either to
 4                   the next layer up or to loop back through the downward traverse. Moving to the next layer up
 5                   occurs when the number of times that the trigger system has passed through the downward
                     traverse (given by the value of loop_ctr) is equal to the specified COUNt. In the simple case,
 6                   COUNt has the value 1, a single downward traverse through the layer occurs, followed by
 7                   the actions dictated by subservient layers, and finally a single upward traverse to next layer
                     up. COUnt shall be set to a value of 1 or greater.
 8
                     At *RST, this value is set to 1.
 9
          24.6.1.2.2     :COUPling AC|DC
10                   ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:COUPling

11                   COUPling only has effect if the source for the event detector is an analog electrical signal,
                     such as INTernal, LINE, or EXTernal. It selects AC or DC coupling for the SOURced signal.
12
                     DC coupling allows the signal’s AC and DC components to pass. AC coupling passes only
13                   the signal’s AC component.
14                   At *RST, this value is device-dependent.
15        24.6.1.2.3     :DELay <numeric_value>
                     ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:DELay
16
                     DELay sets the time duration between the recognition of an event(s) and the downward exit
17                   of the specified layer. DELay must be either zero or a positive value. An attempt to set it to a
18                   negative value shall cause an error -222 to be generated.

19                   At *RST, this value is set to 0 or the smallest available positive value. The units for DELay
                     are seconds.
20
          24.6.1.2.3.1     :AUTO <Boolean>|ONCE
21                   ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:DELay:AUTO

22                   This command is used for sensor devices with internal settling delays. If ON, the delay is set
                     to the minimum necessary to ensure that a valid measurement can be acquired. This value
23
                     may be coupled to other instrument settings such as function, range, resolution, and input
     24              bandwidth.

25                   At *RST, AUTO is set ON.

26

                                 1999 SCPI Command Reference

          24.6.1.2.7     :HYSTeresis <numeric_value>
                   ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:HYSTeresis

                   HYSTeresis is a qualifier of LEVel. It sets how far a signal must fall below LEVel before a
                   rising edge can again be detected, and how far a signal must rise above LEVel before a
 1                 falling edge can again be detected. Its function is to eliminate false events caused by signal
                   noise. Units for the parameter default to the current amplitude units.
 2
                   In instruments that have only two discrete values for hysteresis (such as Noise Rejection On
 3                 and Noise Rejection Off), the device designer should pick two numeric values that
 4                 approximate the actual hystereis settings. The :HYSTeresis command has no :STATe
                   function because confusion would occur when turning hysteresis off. This might imply to a
 5                 user that the actual hysteresis had been set to 0. This is rarely the case in instruments that
 6                 have only two states.
                                                                                                                         TWOS03




 7                 At *RST, this value is device-dependent.

 8        24.6.1.2.8     [:IMMediate]
                   ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:IMMediate
 9                 This command provides a onetime override of the normal process of the downward traverse
10                 of the event detection layer. This command shall cause the immediate exit of the specified
                   event detection layer if the trigger system is in the specified layer when the IMMediate is
11                 received. Otherwise, the IMMediate command shall be ignored and an error -212 shall be
12                 generated.
13                 The actual event detection and delay shall be skipped; however, normal processing of the
                   loop_ctr as shown in figure 24-4, “Event Detection Layer” shall occur. This command has no
14                 effect on any other settings in this subsystem.
15                 This command is an event and has no *RST condition and cannot be queried.
16        24.6.1.2.9     :LEVel <numeric_value>
17                 ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:LEVel

18                 LEVel qualifies the characteristic of the selected SOURce signal that generates an event.
                   LEVel only has effect if the source for the event detector is an analog electrical signal, such
19                 as INTernal, LINE, or EXTernal. Units for the parameter default to the current amplitude
20                 unit.

21                 At *RST, this value is instrument-dependent.

22        24.6.1.2.9.1     :AUTO <Boolean> | ONCE                                                                    TK036
                   ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:LEVel:AUTO
23                 When AUTO is ON, the device dynamically selects the best arm level based on a                     TK036
     24            device-dependent algorithm applied to the arm signal.
                   When AUTO is OFF, the arm LEVel sets the arm level.                                               TK036
25
                   Setting AUTO to ONCE turns AUTO ON, adjusts the arm level once and then resets AUTO               TK036
26                 to OFF.


          24-16   TRIGger Subsystem ARM

         Setting the arm LEVel turns AUTO OFF.                                                            TK036
         At *RST, the value of this parameter is OFF.                                                     TK036

                   ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:SLOPe
 1                 SLOPe qualifies whether the event occurs on the rising edge, falling edge, or either edge of
 2                 the signal.

 3                 At *RST, this value is set to POS.

 4        24.6.1.2.14   :SOURce <parameter>
                   ARM:SEQuence:LAYer:SOURce
 5                 This command selects the source for the event detector. Only one source may be specified at
 6                 a time for a given event detector. The various sources are:
 7                           AINTernal — The triggering source is selected automatically by the instrument         TK040
                             from internal algorithms to best match the current operating mode. An Automatic
 8                           INTernal event is derived from measurement functions and/or sensor capabilities
 9                           in the signal conditioning block.
10                           BUS — The source is signal specific to the control interface. For IEEE 488.1, the    TWV41C
                             group execute trigger, GET, would satisfy this condition. In VXI the word serial
11                           command TRIGger performs this function. The event detector is also satisfied,
12                           independent of the interface, when a *TRG command is received. Note that
                             neither GET nor *TRG can be sent without having an effect on the message
13                           exchange protocol described in IEEE 488.2.
14                           ECLTrg — The signal source is the specified VXI P2 or P3 backplane ECLTrg
15                           TRIGGER line. Valid lines are ECLTrg0 and ECLTrg1 on P2, and ECLTrg2
                             through ECLTrg5 on P3.
16
                             EXTernal — An external signal jack is selected as the source. If no suffix is
17                           specified, EXTernal1 is assumed.
18                           HOLD — The event detection is disabled. However, the IMMediate command
19                           shall override HOLD.

20                           IMMediate — No waiting for an event occurs.

21                           INTernal — An internal channel is selected as the source. An INTernal event is
                             derived from a measurement function and/or sensor capability in the signal
22                           conditioning block. If no suffix is specified, INTernal1 is assumed.
23                           LINE — The source signal is determined from the AC line voltage.
     24                      LINK — The source for the event detector is specified by the LINK command.

25                           MANual — The signal is user-generated, such as by pressing a front panel key.

26                           OUTPut — The signal source is taken from an output channel. If no channel is
                             specified, OUTPut1 is assumed.


          24-18   TRIGger Subsystem ARM
                                  1999 SCPI Command Reference

                       TIMer — The source signal comes from a periodic timer. The period of the timer
                       is specified by the TIMer command.
                       TTLTrg — The signal source is the specified VXI P2 backplane TTLTrg
                       TRIGGER line. Valid lines are TTLTrg0 through TTLTrg7.
         At *RST, IMMediate shall be selected as the SOURce. This value was chosen so that                  1
         devices that do not implement any ARM layers (and hence the controls for the ARM layer)            2
         behave at *RST in the same manner as devices that do.
                                                                                                            3

         TIMer sets the period of an internal periodic signal source. Its value affects the trigger         5
         system only when it is selected as the SOURce for the event detector. TIMer must be a              6
         positive value. An attempt to set it differently shall cause an error -222 to be generated. The
         synchronization of the timer’s period is device-dependent.                                         7
         At *RST, this value is device-dependent value. The default units for this value is seconds.        8

24.7     INITiate
         INITiate                                                                                           2
         The INITiate subsystem is used to control the initiation of the trigger subsystem. It initiates    3
                                                                                                          ACQ01B
         all trigger sequences as a group except those sequences that are defined otherwise by either       4
         the standard or in the instrument documentation.
                                                                                                            5
         Instruments which implement the INITiate command as overlapped can continue parsing and            KI005
         executing subsequent commands and queries while initiated. Instruments which implement             6
         the INITiate commands as sequential cannot execute subsequent commands and queries until           7
         the trigger model has returned to the IDLE state.
                                                                                                            8
         For this reason, devices which implement the INITiate commands as sequential shall enter           KI005
         IDLE when the IEEE 488.2 dcas message is received. They shall also execute the next                9
         message unit received after the dcas before leaving IDLE (if INITiate:CONTinuous is ON).          10
         dcas followed by *RST or dcas followed by INIT:CONT OFF shall always stop the trigger
         model in the IDLE state.                                                                          11
         There are advantages to implementing the INITiate commands as overlapped.                         12
                                                                                                            KI005
                     The instrument designer decides whether or not a device clear aborts the trigger      13
                                                                                                            KI005
                     model.                                                                                14
                     The instrument can continue parsing and executing commands and queries while           KI005
                                                                                                           15
                     the trigger model is initiated (for example, FETCh? to get the readings which are
                     being triggered in a meter).                                                          16
         The disadvantage to implementing any commands as overlapped, including the INITiate               17
                                                                                                            KI005
         commands, is that it adds complexity to the implementation of the IEEE 488.2 common               18
         commands *OPC, *WAI and *OPC?
                                                                                                           19
24.7.1   :CONTinuous <Boolean>                                                                             TK038
         INITiate:CONTinuous                                                                               20
         The CONTinuous command is used to select whether the trigger system is continuously               21
         initiated or not. With CONTinuous set to OFF, the trigger system shall remain in the IDLE
         state until CONTinuous is set to ON or INITiate:IMMediate is received. Once CONTinuous
                                                                                                           22
         is set to ON, the trigger system shall be initiated and shall exit the IDLE state. On completion  23
         of each trigger cycle, with CONTinuous ON, the trigger system shall immediately
         commence another trigger cycle without entering the IDLE state.                                   24
         When INITiate:CONTinuous is set to OFF, the current trigger cycle shall be completed              25
                                                                                                            KI005
         before entering the IDLE state. The return to IDLE shall also occur as the result of an           26
         ABORt or *RST command.


                                                              TRIGger Subsystem INITiate           24-21
                                              1999 SCPI Command Reference

                     With the trigger system set to cycle continuously, the ABORt command shall force the
                     trigger system to the IDLE state; however, the value of INITiate:CONTinuous is unaffected.
                     If CONTinuous was set to ON prior to receiving ABORt, it shall remain ON and the trigger
                     system shall immediately exit the IDLE state.
 1                   This subsystem does not apply to sequences that are initiated by the INITiate:ALL command. ACQ01B
 2        24.7.1.1     [:ALL] <Boolean>
                     INITiate:CONTinuous:ALL

          24.8.1.1.1    [:STATe] <Boolean>                                                                             TK027
                     TRIGger:SEQuence:ATRigger:STATe

                     STATe sets and queries the state of the auto trigger function. STATe ON enables the               TK027
                     function and STATe OFF disables it.
 1                   At *RST, the value of this parameter is OFF.                                                      TK027
 2        24.8.1.2     :COUNt <numeric_value>
                     TRIGger:SEQuence:COUNt
 3
                     COUNt controls the path of the trigger system in the upward traverse of the event detection
 4                   layer, shown in figure 24-4, “Event Detection Layer.” The trigger system is directed either to
 5                   the next layer up or to loop back through the downward traverse. Moving to the next layer up
                     occurs when the number of times that the trigger system has passed through the downward
 6                   traverse (given by the value of loop_ctr) is equal to the specified COUNt. In the simple case,
 7                   COUNt has the value 1, a single downward traverse through the layer occurs, followed by
                     the actions dictated by subservient layers and finally a single upward traverse to next layer
 8                   up. COUnt shall be set to a value of 1 or greater.
 9                   At *RST, this value is set to 1.
10        24.8.1.3     :COUPling AC|DC
                     TRIGger:SEQuence:COUPling
11
                     COUPling only has effect if the source for the event detector is an analog electrical signal,
12
                     such as INTernal, LINE, or EXTernal. It selects AC or DC coupling for the SOURced signal.
13                   DC coupling allows the signal’s AC and DC components to pass. AC coupling passes only
                     the signal’s AC component.
14
                     At *RST, this value is device-dependent.

24.8.1.10      :HYSTeresis <numeric_value>                                                                    12
            TRIGger:SEQuence:HYSTeresis
                                                                                                              13
            HYSTeresis is a qualifier of LEVel. It sets how far a signal must fall below LEVel before a
            rising edge can again be detected, and how far a signal must rise above LEVel before a            14
            falling edge can again be detected. Its function is to eliminate false events caused by signal    15
            noise. Units for the parameter default to the current amplitude units.
                                                                                                              16
            In instruments that have only two discrete values for hysteresis (such as Noise Rejection On
            and Noise Rejection Off), the device designer should pick two numeric values that                 17
            approximate the actual hystereis settings. The :HYSTeresis command has no :STATe                  18
            function because confusion would occur when turning hysteresis off. This might imply to a
            user that the actual hysteresis had been set to 0. This is rarely the case in instruments that    19
            have only two states.                                                                             20   TWOS03




            At *RST, this value is device-dependent.                                                          21

24.8.1.17     :SOURce <parameter>                                                                             19
            TRIGger:SEQuence:SOURce
                                                                                                              20
            This command selects the source for the event detector. Only one source may be specified in
            the parameter at a time for a given event detector. The various sources are:                      21
                      AINTernal — The triggering source is selected automatically by the instrument           22
                                                                                                              TK040
                      from internal algorithms to best match the current operating mode. An Automatic         23
                      INTernal event is derived from measurement functions and/or sensor capabilities
                      in the signal conditioning block.                                                       24
                      BUS — The source is signal specific to the control interface. For IEEE 488.1 the        25
                                                                                                             TWV41C
                      group execute trigger, GET, would satisfy this condition. In VXI the word serial
                      command TRIGger performs this function. The event detector is also satisfied,
                                                                                                              26
                      independent of the interface, when a *TRG command is received. Note that

                                                                 TRIGger Subsystem TRIGger          24-29
                                             1999 SCPI Command Reference

                                 neither GET nor *TRG can be sent without having an effect on the message
                                 exchange protocol described in IEEE 488.2.
                                 ECLTrg — The signal source is the specified VXI P2 or P3 backplane ECLTrg
                                 TRIGGER line. Valid lines are ECLTrg0 and ECLTrg1 on P2, and ECLTrg2
 1                               through ECLTrg5 on P3.
 2                               EXTernal — An external signal jack is selected as the source. If no suffix is
                                 specified, EXTernal1 is assumed.
 3
                                 HOLD — The event detection is disabled. However, the IMMediate command
 4                               shall override HOLD.
 5                               IMMediate — No waiting for an event occurs.
 6                               INTernal — An internal channel is selected as the source. An INTernal event is
 7                               derived from a measurement function and/or sensor capability in the signal
                                 conditioning block. If no suffix is specified, INTernal1 is assumed.
 8
                                 LINE — The source signal is determined from the AC line voltage.
 9
                                 LINK — The source for the event detector is specified by the LINK command.
10
                                 MANual — The signal is user-generated, such as by pressing a front panel key.
11
                                 OUTPut — The signal source is taken from an output channel. If no channel is
12                               specified, OUTPut1 is assumed.
13                               TIMer — The source signal comes from a periodic timer. The period of the timer
14                               is specified by the TIMer command.

15                               TTLTrg — The signal source is the specified VXI P2 backplane TTLTrg
                                 TRIGGER line. Valid lines are TTLTrg0 through TTLTrg7.
16
                      At *RST, IMMediate shall be selected as the SOURce.

25     UNIT Subsystem
       Default units are defined, where applicable, for each SCPI command. The UNIT subsystem
       provides a mechanism to change the default values. The units selected apply to the
       designated command parameters for both command and response.
                                                                                                        1
       The UNIT command at the root level has a global effect on the selected units. The UNIT
       command may also be applied to lower levels in the SCPI command hierarchy to have a              2
       localized effect. When the UNIT command is applied to a node, then all the nodes below the       3
       node to which the unit command was applied shall be affected by the localized UNIT
       command. There is no restriction on the number of levels to which UNIT may be applied. In        4
       this way the more global units are overridden by the more local units. Units may also be         5
       overridden temporarily by attaching the desired unit as a suffix to the appropriate parameter
       in the command, if the instrument supports that unit.                                            6
       For example, to program a source with units of Volts, the command UNIT:VOLTage VOLT              7
       would be used. To program only the modulator of that same source in dBuVs, the additional        8
       command [SOURce:]MODulation:UNIT DBUV would be required.
                                                                                                        9
       The UNIT command cannot be applied to either SENSe, SOURce or ROUTe nodes, since
       the UNIT command at these nodes and at the root cannot be unambiguously recognized.             10
       This condition arises from the ability to have one of SENSe, SOURce or ROUTe nodes              11
       optional.
                                                                                                       12
                                                                                                       13
       KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                               NOTES
                                                                                                       14
                                                                                                            Bode




       :UNIT
         :ANGLe               DEG|RAD                                                                  15
         :CURRent             <amplitude unit>
         :POWer               <amplitude unit>                                                         16
         :TEMPerature         C|CEL|F|FAR|K                                                            17
         :TIME                HOUR|MINute|SECond                                            1993       XSS01c
         :VOLTage             <amplitude unit>                                                         18

25.1   :ANGLe DEG|RAD                                                                                  20

       Specifies the fundamental unit of angle.
                                                                                                       22
       At *RST, the default unit is RAD.
                                                                                                       23
25.2   :CURRent, :POWer, and :VOLTage
       UNIT:CURRent
                                                                                                       24
       Selects a default unit for commands which program absolute amplitude. The default unit          25
       may be overridden when programming a function by explicitly sending a suffix. The default
                                                                                                       26
       unit may also be overridden if a unit command exists at a lower tree level. Query values of
       commands which program in amplitude units shall be returned in the current amplitude unit

                                                                              UNIT:ANGLe        25-1
                                         1999 SCPI Command Reference

                   unless overridden by a unit command at a tree level closer to the command itself (such as
                   POWer:UNIT).
                   The possible values are:
                               Linear power: W (Watt)
 1
                               Linear voltage: V (Volt)
 2
                               Linear current: A (Ampere)
 3
                               Logarithmic power: DBM, DB[IEEE suffix multiplier]W (such as DBUW)
 4
                               Logarithmic voltage: DB[IEEE suffix multiplier]V (such as DBUV)
 5
                               Logarithmic current: DB[IEEE suffix multiplier]A (such as DBA)
 6
                   An instrument must accept all values in any class if it accepts any value in that class.
 7                 However, the decision to accept a class is device-dependent. A device which accepts
 8                 logarithmic units must also accept the comparable linear unit. This means that
                   UNIT:VOLTage WATT is permissible if it makes sense for the instrument. It is also implied
 9                 that an impedance is specified for the signal when converting between different fundamental
10                 quantities.

11                 At *RST, this value is device-dependent. However, the following restrictions apply. The
                   UNIT subsystem must be implemented if a device chooses any value other than the
12                 fundamental unit for either the VOLTage, POWer, or CURRent subsystem , or if it
13                 implements logarithmic units.

14        25.3     :TEMPerature C|CEL|F|FAR|K
                   UNIT:TEMPerature

16                 form FAR and CEL, defined by IEEE 488.2, shall be accepted for Fahrenheit and Celsius
17                 respectively, and these shall be the preferred forms that are returned for a query.

18                 At *RST, this value is device-dependent.

26   VXI Subsystem
     The VXI subsystem contains commands that control the administration functions associated
     with operating a VXI-based system. This section will track the work of the VXI consortium.
     This section describes ASCII commands which are issued to the system from an external           1
     host. The exact internal destination device and routing methods to that device are system
     specific. These commands are used for access to system configuration information, and for       2
     common capabilities. The terminology used in this section is patterned after IEEE 488.2.        3
     The following commands are the standard set of VXIbus system commands which are                 4
     ASCII encoded. If a device implements one or more of these commands, the syntax of this
     section shall be used. The response syntax shall also follow this section.                      5
     The COMMON ASCII SYSTEM COMMANDS are organized into subsystems. If a device                     6
     implements a required command in a subsystem then it shall implement all the required           7
     commands in the subsystem. If a device implements an optional command in a subsystem
     then it shall implement all the required commands in the subsystem. If a device implements a    8
     command from any subsystem then it shall also implement the VXI:SELect command.                 9
     KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                            NOTES                         10

26.1     :CONFigure                                                                                         5
         VXI:CONFigure
         Provides the necessary commands to query the configuration of a VXI system.                        6
26.1.1   :DNUMber?                                                                                          7
         VXI:CONFigure:DNUMber?
                                                                                                            8
         This query returns the number of devices in the system, in <NR1 numeric value> format.
         The range of this integer numeric value is 1 to 256 inclusive.                                     9
26.1.2   :HIERarchy?                                                                                       10
         VXI:CONFigure:HIERarchy?
                                                                                                           11
         This command returns current hierarchy configuration information about the selected logical
         address. The individual fields of the response are comma separated. If the information about      12
         the selected logical address is not available from the destination device, (that is, the          13
         requested device is not in the servant area of the destination device), then error -224,
         “Parameter error” will be set and no response data will be sent. This is a required               14
         configuration command. The output fields are defined as follows:                                  15
                   Logical address: a <NR1>, between -1 and 255 inclusive. A -1 indicates that the         16
                   device has no logical address.
                                                                                                           17
                   commander’s logical address: a <NR1>, between -1 and 255 inclusive. -1
                   indicates that this device has no commander or the commander is unknown.                18
                   Interrupt Handlers: a comma separated list of 7 <NR1>, between 0 and 7                  19
                   inclusive. Interrupt lines 1-7 are mapped to the individual return values. 0 is used    20
                   to indicate that the particular interrupt handler is not configured. A set of return
                   values of 0,0,0,5,2,0,6 would indicate that the device is configured as follows:        21
                      handler 4 is configured to handle interrupts on line 5                               22
                      handler 5 is configured to handle interrupts on line 2
                      handler 7 is configured to handle interrupts on line 6                               23
                      handlers 1,2,3,6 are not configured                                                  24
                   Interrupters: a comma separated list of 7 <NR1>, between 0 and 7 inclusive.             25
                   Interrupt lines 1-7 are mapped to the individual return values. 0 is used to indicate
                   that the particular interrupter is not configured. A set of return values of            26
                   0,0,0,5,2,0,6 would indicate that the device is configured as follows:


                                                                                             VXI    26-3
                                             1999 SCPI Command Reference

                                   interrupter 4 is configured to interrupt on line 5
                                   interrupter 5 is configured to interrupt on line 2
                                   interrupter 7 is configured to interrupt on line 6
                                   interrupters 1,2,3,6 are not configured
 1                               Pass/Failed: a <NR1> which contains the pass/fail status of the specified device
                                 encoded as follows:
 2                                   FAIL=0 IFAIL=1 PASS=2 READY=3
 3                               manufacturer specific comment: This up to 80 character quoted string contains
 4                               manufacturer specific data. It is sent with a 488.2 string response data format.
 5        26.1.2.1       :ALL?
                     VXI:CONFigure:HIERarchy?:ALL?

                     returns the current hierarchy configuration information about the destination device followed

                     semi-colon separated and follow the IEEE 488.2 response message format). The individual
10                   fields of the output are comma separated. This is an optional configuration command.

device has no logical address.

         manager, then the response to the command will contain the number of devices which are
                                                                                                              2
         immediate servants to the destination device including the destination device. For example, a        3
         commander with 3 servants would return a value of 4, or a resource manager for a system of
         4 devices would return a value of 5. The range of this <NR1> is 1 to 256 inclusive. This is a
                                                                                                              4
         required configuration command.                                                                      5
26.2     REGister                                                                                             6
         VXI:REGister
         The node collects together the commands that interact with the VXI registers.                        7
26.2.1   :READ? <register>                                                                                    8
         VXI:REGister:READ?
                                                                                                              9
         This command returns the contents of the specified 16 bit register at the selected logical
         address as a <NR1>. This is a required register access command. The register is specified as        10
         the byte address of the desired register or as optionally the register name. It has values of all   11
         even numbers from 0 to 62 inclusive (as a <numeric_value>) or the following (optional)
         words:                                                                                              12
         A24Low: A24 Pointer Low register (18)                                                               13
         A24High: A24 Pointer High register (16)                                                             14
         A32Low: A32 Pointer Low register (22)                                                               15
         A32High: A32 Pointer High register (20)                                                             16
         ATTRibute: Attribute register (8)                                                                   17
         DHIGh: Data High register (12)                                                                      18
         DLOW: Data Low register (14)                                                                        19
         DTYPe: Device Type register (2)                                                                     20
         ICONtrol: Interrupt Control register (28)                                                           21
         ID: ID register (0)                                                                                 22
         ISTatus: Interrupt Status register (26)                                                             23
         MODid: MODID register (8)                                                                           24
         OFFSet: Offset register (6)                                                                         25
         PROTocol: PROTocol register (8)                                                                     26
         RESPonse: RESPonse register (10)

                                                                                               VXI    26-7
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

                     SNLow: Serial Number Low register (12)
                     SNHigh: Serial Number High register (10)
                     STATus: Status register (4)
 1                   SUBClass: Subclass register (30)
 2                   VNUMber: Version Number register (14)
 3        26.2.1.1       :VERBose? <register>
                     VXI:REGister:READ?:VERBose?
 4                   This command has the same functionality as VXI:REGister:READ?. However it returns a
 5                   quoted string indicating the register contents for the selected device. The format of this string
                     is manufacturer specific. This command is intended to allow for a human readable form of
 6                   the response to VXI:REG:READ? which could include additional decoding of bits in
 7                   specific registers. This is an optional register access command.
 8        26.2.2     :WRITe (<numeric_value> | <register>), <data>
                     VXI:REGister:WRITe
 9                   This command writes data to the specified register on the selected logical address. This is a
10                   required register access command. The Data is a 16 bit value specified as a <numeric_value>
                     in the range of -32768 to 32767. The register is specified as the byte address of the desired
11                   register or as optionally the register name. It has values of all even numbers from 0 to 62
12                   inclusive (expressed as a <numeric_value>) or the following (optional) words:
13                   CONTrol: Control register (4)
14                   DEXTended: Data Extended register (10)
15                   DHIGh: Data High register (12)
16                   DLOW: Data Low register (14)
17                   ICONtrol: Interrupt Control register (28)
18                   MODid: MODID register (8)
19                   LADDress: Logical Address register (0)
20                   OFFSet: Offset register (6)
21                   SIGNal: Signal register (8)
22        26.3       :RESet?
                     VXI:RESet?
23                   This command resets the selected logical address. SYSFAIL generation is inhibited while
24                   the device is in the self test state. The command waits for five seconds or until the selected
                     device has indicated passed (whichever occurs first). If the device passes its self test, then
25                   SYSFAIL generation will be re-enabled. If the device fails its self test, then SYSFAIL
     26              generation will remain inhibited. The return value from this command is the state of the
                     selected device after it has been reset. The command returns an <NR1> which is encoded as


          26-8     VXI
                                  1999 SCPI Command Reference

           follows: FAIL=0, PASS=2, READY=3. The state of the A24/A32 enable bit is not altered by
           this command. This is a required register access command.
26.3.1     :VERBose?
           VXI:RESet?:VERBose?
           This command has the same functionality as VXI:RESet?. However it returns a quoted string            1
           indicating the state of the specified device. The format of this string is manufacturer specific.
           This is an optional register access command.
                                                                                                                2
26.4       :SELect <logical_address>                                                                            3
           VXI:SELect
                                                                                                                4
           This command specifies the logical address which is to be used by all subsequent commands
           in the VXI subsystem. Logical_address is specified as a <numeric_value> in the range of 0            5
           to 255. The query form returns the logical address as a <NR1> the value of -1 is reserved to         6
           indicate that no logical address has been selected. The *RST default value for
           logical_address is that no logical address is selected. All other commands which require a           7
           logical_address to be selected will respond with an error -221, “Settings conflict” if no            8
           logical address is selected.

26.5       :WSPRotocol
           VXI:WSPRotocol                                                                                      10
           This node collects together all the commands associated with the word serial protocol.              11
26.5.1     :COMMand                                                                                            12
26.5.1.1    [:ANY] <data>                                                                                      13
           VXI:WSPRotocol:COMMand:ANY
           This command sends the specified word serial command to the selected logical address. The           14
           data field is a <numeric_value> or a non-decimal value which specifies the command to be            15
           sent. The response of a word serial query which is sent with this command can be read with
           the VXI:WSPRotocol:RESPonse? command. This is a required Word Serial Support                        16
           command.                                                                                            17
26.5.1.2    :AHLine <hand_id>,<line_number>                                                                    18
           VXI:WSPRotocol:COMMand:AHLine
           This command sends an Assign Handler Line command to the selected logical address. The              19
           hand_id field has a value in the range of 1 to 7 inclusive, and line_number field has a value       20
           in the range of 0 to 7 inclusive. They are both specified with <numeric_value>s or as
           non-decimal values. The response to this command can be read with the                               21
           VXI:WSPRotocol:RESPonse? command. This is an optional Word Serial Support command.                  22
26.5.1.3    :AILine <int_id>,<line_number>                                                                     23
           VXI:WSPRotocol:COMMand:AILine
           This command sends an Assign Interrupter Line command to the selected logical address.              24
           The int_id field has a value in the range of 1 to 7 inclusive, and line_number field has a          25
           value in the range of 0 to 7 inclusive. They are both specified with numeric_ values or as
           non-decimal values. The response to this command can be read with the                               26
           VXI:WSPRotocol:RESPonse? command. This is an optional Word Serial Support command.

           This node collects together all the messages (as defined by VXI) of the word serial protocol.   19
26.5.2.1    :RECeive? <count>|<terminator>                                                                 20
           VXI:WSPRotocol:MESSage:RECeive?
                                                                                                           21
           This command receives a message from the selected logical address using both the word
           serial protocol and the byte transfer protocol. The command will always terminate on the        22
           End bit being set. Additional termination options are on a specified number of bytes (count),
                                                                                                           23
           or on a match to a particular terminator, (that is, LF, CRLF, END). The response is returned
           as a string. This is a required Word Serial Support command.                                    24
26.5.2.2    :SEND <message_string> [,(END|NEND)]                                                           25
           VXI:WSPRotocol:MESSage:SEND
                                                                                                           26
           This command sends the specified message string to the selected logical address. The string
           is sent using the word serial protocol with the byte transfer protocol. The last byte of the

                                                                                            VXI    26-13
                                            1999 SCPI Command Reference

                     string is sent with the End bit set unless NEND is specified. This is a required Word Serial
                     Support command.

         non-decimal value. The returned value is the response to the command and is a <NR1>. This
                                                                                                           6
         is an optional Word Serial Support command.                                                       7
26.5.4   :RESPonse?                                                                                        8
         VXI:WSPRotocol:RESPonse?
         This command returns one word of data from the data low register on the selected logical
                                                                                                           9
         address. This command obeys the Byte transfer protocol. The data is returned as a <NR1>.         10
         This is a required Word Serial Support command.

Chapter 7 Data Format Example

               viii
                             1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format


1     Introduction
      The data interchange format described in this section lets software packages and instruments
      share waveform and other data. It is designed to be flexible and extensible, and can
      accommodate a wide range of data structures and formats. In addition to describing the data
      itself, the data interchange format provides information regarding the data environment,             1
      structure, and other related specifications. Only a minimum of information about the data is
      actually required but a wide range of information can be associated with the data. Complex           2
      data dimensioned sets and simpler data are equally representable using the block structure of
      this data format.
                                                                                                           3
      Because this data format is hierarchically structured, it can be subordinate to other structures.    4
      It is suitable as a file format and its encoding formats allow it to be easily transmitted across
      IEEE 488.1/488.2, RS-232, SCSI, IEEE 802, and various other transmission media and                   5
      protocols.
                                                                                                           6
      The syntax of the data interchange format is compatible with IEEE 488.2 syntax. With minor
      modifications, an IEEE 488.2 parser, or at least its lexical analyzer, can also analyze the          7
      syntax of this format. While the format imposes its own rules within IEEE 488.2
      expressions, these rules conform to the IEEE 488.2 restrictions for expressions.                     8
1.1   Overview                                                                                             9
      The data interchange format is block-structured. A data set generally consists of several
      description blocks and a data block. A block contains keywords and subordinate blocks.              10
      Within a block or sub-block are keywords with values that define characteristics of the data
      or the environment in which it was acquired. Many blocks accept a modifier label value and          11
      it is required for some blocks. A block modifier allows multiples of the same block type to
      be distinguished from one another.
                                                                                                          12
      Each block addresses a different aspect of data description. The DATA block contains the            13
      data. The IDENtify block describes the manner and environment in which the data was
      obtained. The DIMension and ENCode blocks describe how the data is physically                       14
      represented and logically organized. The TRACe and VIEW blocks provide semantic
      information about the data. A REMark block contains textual comments regarding the data.            15
      Finally, the DIF block identifies the block as a <dif_expression> and describes the version of
                                                                                                          16
      SCPI used.
                                                                                                           DIF01
      This data interchange format focuses on data as an abstraction of instrument- or                    17
      algorithm-generated data. The method of data acquisition or creation is handled as
      descriptive information that is not required for proper interpretation of the data. Information     18
      about the encoding, structure, scaling, range, etc., of the data is independent of the source of
      the data.                                                                                           19
      For example, instrument-dependent settings and characteristics such as sample rate are              20
      translated into acquisition independent parameters such as RESolution.
                                                                                                          21
                                                                                                          22
                                                                                   Introduction     1-1
                                      1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

         1.2       Defined Blocks
                   The Data Interchange Format consists of the following major blocks:
                                                                                                                     DIF01
                              DIF identifies the expression as a <dif_expression> and contains the version of
                              the standard used to create the data set.                                              DIF01
     1
                              REMark contains general comments in human-readable text regarding the data.
 2
                              IDENtify names the data set and describes the environment in which it was
 3                            generated. Environment description includes project name, test number and series,
                              date and time, and source.
 4                            ENCode specifies the encoding format for data in the DATA and ENCode
                              blocks. Also covered are signal values for underflow, overflow and no value, as
 5                            well as the range and resolution of the data.
 6                            DIMension specifies the structure and format of data in the DATA block.
                              Provision is made for data scaling, offset, naming, and units specification.
 7
                              ORDer specifies ordering of the data elements in the DATA(CURVe) block for
 8                            each dimension.
                              TRACe logically groups dimensions as functions, surfaces, sets, etc. TRACe
 9                            blocks provide semantic information about the data and are used to build VIEW
                              blocks. They also provide a convenient and powerful mechanism for subsetting
10                            data.
11                            VIEW provides a second level of semantic information about the data. VIEW
                              describes logical relationships among traces defined in the TRACe block such as
12                            envelope traces.

13                            DATA contains the actual data. Different subordinate blocks describe
                              dimensioned data, waveform parameter measurements, and point values.
14
         1.3       Implicit and Explicit Dimensions
15                 There are many ways to describe the structure and order of dimensioned data, and not all
                   terms are well defined or understood. The data interchange format treats all CURVe data as
16                 coordinates in n-dimensional space. If a coordinate is actually present in the data, its
                   dimension is said to be explicit. If the coordinate value of a dimension is not present as a
17                 data value, but is instead derived from the location of other coordinate values, the dimension
                   is said to be implicit.
18
                   Suppose you mark off an evenly spaced grid on the floor of a room, and then make
19                 measurements of temperature and humidity at some (varying) height above the floor. As you
                   make these measurements, you write down the temperature and humidity measurements and
20                 the location (X, Y, and Z positions relative to one corner of the room). The result is 5-tuple.
                   You must write each set of measurements in a consistent order (such as X, Y, Z,
21                 temperature, and humidity), but you may write the sets of measurements in any order.

22

         1-2   Introduction
                      1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

A 5-tuple may be viewed, as this format does, as a point in a 5-dimensional space. All five
dimensions are explicit, meaning that for each dimension, you have explicitly written down
its coordinate.
Now suppose you make the measurements according to some consistent pattern. You start
with the first grid line and make the measurements sequentially at each Y point along the X             1
grid line. You then make the measurements along the second X grid line, and so on, until the
last grid line is completed.                                                                            2
If you keep track of the order in which the measurements were made, you only need to write
                                                                                                        3
down two measurements: temperature and humidity. The other three measurements (X
location, Y location, and height) are derivable from the order of the data. The data is still           4
5-dimensional, but three of the dimensions are implicit and two are explicit.
Simple waveforms acquired from instruments like oscilloscopes (when clocked internally)                 5
commonly consist of a time series of voltage (vertical axis) measurements. For the
time-voltage space, only the voltage value or coordinate is provided by the oscilloscope; the
                                                                                                        6
time (horizontal axis) is derived from the order of the data, an initial starting time, and a           7
scale factor. The voltage dimension is explicit and the time dimension is implicit.
This format classifies all dimensions as implicit or explicit. The order of the data, which is          8
essential to the correct derivation of implicit dimension coordinates or values, is strictly
defined by the ORDer block or its default values.                                                       9

2   Style
    The data interchange format uses, for the most part, standard IEEE 488.2 syntactic elements
    along with the nested parentheses which together comprise an Expression type parameter
    (“Volume 1: Syntax and Style,” Section 8).
                                                                                                        1
    The format also uses the concept of “friendly” listening and “precise” talking followed by
    IEEE 488.2. There are some differences, which are clarified in 3 of this section.                   2
    Keywords may take single or multiple values. If a keyword takes multiple values, all values
    shall be of the same type.
                                                                                                        3
    A few keywords have default values. If the keyword is omitted, the default value prevails.          4
    These values are specified in the block descriptions in 6 of this section.
                                                                                                        5
    An invalid set reports either a Command Error or an Execution Error as described in                TK053a
    “Volume 2: Command Reference,” 21.8.9 and 21.8.10. While uppercase characters are                   6
    specified, lowercase characters may be accepted without error if interpretation of the data set
    is unambiguous.                                                                                     7
    It is not required that a data format parser accept all values of an enumerated set (3.4.10 of     TK053a
                                                                                                        8
    this volume). An error may be generated on receipt of an unimplemented value.
                                                                                                        9

         2-2   Style
