3     Syntax
      The data format is block-structured. Each hierarchical level is introduced by a block name,
      with its subordinate elements enclosed in parentheses. A block may have a modifier and may
      contain subordinate blocks and keyword units, or both. Keyword units consist of a keyword
      followed by one or more values. If a keyword has more than one value, the values are             1
      separated by commas.
                                                                                                       2
      The following example shows a simple data set. It is formatted so that all blocks and
      keywords are indented to show their hierarchical relationship.                                   3
                                                                                                       4
                    (DIF (VERSion 1993.0)                                                             TK053a
                    IDENtify (                                                                         5
                           NAME “Data Format Example”
                           TEST (                                                                      6
                                  NUMBer “7D4", ”2.4"))
                    ENCode (                                                                           7
                           HRANge 75
                           LRANge 25)                                                                  8
                    DIMension=X (
                           TYPE IMPLicit                                                               9
                           SCALe 0.01
                           SIZE 7
                                                                                                      10
                           UNITs “S”)
                    DIMension=Y (
                                                                                                      11
                           TYPE EXPLicit
                                                                                                      12
                           SCALe 0.02
                           OFFSet 0.1                                                                 13
                           UNITs “V”)
                    DATA (                                                                            14
                           CURVe (
                                  VALues 49.0, 48.0, 50.2, 61.3, 68.5, 38.6, 48.0)))                  15DIF01
      The data interchange format overall is formatted as an IEEE 488.2 <EXPRESSION                   16
      PROGRAM DATA> element. Within this element, the various blocks, modifiers, keywords,
      and value types are composed of syntactic elements that, for the most part, are identical to    17
      the corresponding types specified in IEEE 488.2 or a subset of them.
                                                                                                      18
3.1   Character Set
      All syntactic elements except <Block> contain only 7-bit ASCII-formatted (ANSI                  19
      X3.4-1977) data with the high-order eighth bit always set to zero.
                                                                                                      20
3.2   White Space
      White space consists of the ASCII space character, 32 decimal. A space is used along with       21
      the parentheses, comma, and equal sign to separate syntactic elements.
                                                                                                      22DIF01
                                                                                       Syntax   3-1
                                         1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

                    When an instrument accepts data, redundant white space may appear without semantic effect
                    anywhere except within: block names, block modifiers, keywords, and all value types.
                    Note that the characters constituting white space may be a part of the semantic content of
                    <String> and <Block> value types.
 1                  When an instrument sends data, redundant white space is not allowed.
 2       3.3        Blocks, Block Modifiers, and Keywords
     3              When an instrument accepts data, block names, block modifiers, and keywords conform to
                    the IEEE 488.2 <CHARACTER PROGRAM DATA> syntax. Abbreviated short forms and
 4                  any specified aliases shall be accepted.
                    When an instrument sends data, the IEEE 488.2 <CHARACTER RESPONSE DATA>
 5
                    syntax is used. If a long and short form element is specified, the short form shall be sent.
                                                                                                                   DIF05
 6                  As the data format is hierarchically organized, mnemonic generation rules for compound
                    headers apply. See “Syntax and Style’” 2.2.1. Specific syntactic restrictions on the use of
 7                  blocks, block modifiers, and keywords are covered in 4 of this section.
 8       3.4        Value Types
                    The grammar employs the following value types.
 9
         3.4.1      <Numeric>
10                  The <Numeric> value type is used to specify zero, positive and negative numeric values.

11                  When an instrument accepts data, <Numeric> follows one of the following two IEEE 488.2
                    program data formats:
12                                          <DECIMAL NUMERIC PROGRAM DATA>, or
                                            <NON-DECIMAL NUMERIC PROGRAM DATA>
13
                    Contrary to IEEE 488.2, <Numeric> values with embedded white spaces do not have to be
14
                    accepted.
15                  When an instrument sends data, <Numeric> follows one of the following six response data
                    formats:
16
                                            <NR1 NUMERIC RESPONSE DATA>,
17                                          <NR2 NUMERIC RESPONSE DATA>,
                                            <NR3 NUMERIC RESPONSE DATA>,
18                                          <OCTAL NUMERIC RESPONSE DATA>,
                                            <BINARY NUMERIC RESPONSE DATA>, or
19                                          <HEXADECIMAL NUMERIC RESPONSE DATA>
20       3.4.2      <+Numeric>
                    The <+Numeric> value type is used to specify positive numeric values greater than zero.
21                  Other than this restriction, the value type is identical to <Numeric>.

22

         3-2     Syntax
                             1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

3.4.3   <0+Numeric>
        The <0+Numeric> value type is used to specify positive numeric values equal to or greater
        than zero. Other than this restriction, the value type is identical to <Numeric>.
3.4.4   <NR1>                                                                                                 DIF06
        The <NR1> value type is used to specify zero, positive and negative integer numeric values.           1
        An instrument shall accept any <Numeric> value, rounding as necessary to obtain an integer
        value. When an instrument sends data, <NR1> follows the IEEE 488.2 <NR1 DECIMAL
                                                                                                              2
        NUMERIC RESPONSE DATA> format.
                                                                                                              3
        Note that rounding may result in an invalid integer value.
                                                                                                              4
3.4.5   <+NR1>                                                                                                DIF06
        The <+NR1> value type is used to specify positive integer numeric values greater than zero.           5
        Other than this restriction, the value type is identical to <NR1>.
3.4.6   <0+NR1>
                                                                                                              6DIF06
        The <0+NR1> value type is used to specify positive numeric values equal to or greater than            7
        zero. Other than this restriction, the value type is identical to <NR1>.
3.4.7   <Block>                                                                                               8
        The <Block> value type is used to specify 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, or 64-bit significant data.
        <Block> is only allowed for use with the DATA(CURVe(VALues)) keyword.                                 9
        The FORMat keyword from the applicable ENCode block determines the interpretation of                 10
        the data values. Bytes are grouped according to the number of bits required. For example,
        bytes are grouped by four’s and interpreted as a 32-bit integer for INT32.                           11
        When an instrument accepts data, <Block> values shall follow the format of IEEE 488.2                12
        <ARBITRARY BLOCK PROGRAM DATA> format with the restriction that only definite
        length blocks are accepted.                                                                          13
        When an instrument sends data, <Block> values shall follow the format of IEEE 488.2
                                                                                                             14
        <DEFINITE LENGTH ARBITRARY BLOCK RESPONSE DATA> format.
3.4.8   <String>                                                                                             15DIF04
        The <String> is used to represent quoted strings.
                                                                                                             16
        When an instrument accepts data, <String> data conforms to IEEE 488.2 <STRING
        PROGRAM DATA> syntax.                                                                                17
        When an instrument sends data, <String> data conforms to IEEE 488.2 <STRING
                                                                                                             18
        RESPONSE DATA> syntax.
3.4.9   <Label>                                                                                              19
        The <Label> value type is used to represent short, unquoted string labels for block modifier
        and keyword values.                                                                                  20
        When an instrument accepts data, <Label> follows the IEEE 488.2 <CHARACTER                           21
        PROGRAM DATA> syntax.
                                                                                                             22
                                                                                           Syntax      3-3
                                       1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

                  When an instrument sends data, <Label> follows the IEEE 488.2 <CHARACTER
                  RESPONSE DATA> syntax. A <Label> has no short form.
                                                                                                                  DIF05
         3.4.10   Enumerated Set
                  Some keywords specify a value from an completely enumerated set of values.
 1
                  When an instrument accepts data, an enumerated set member follows the IEEE 488.2
 2                <CHARACTER PROGRAM DATA> syntax. If specified, acceptance of long and short
                  form as well as aliases is required.
     3
                  When an instrument sends data, an enumerated set member follows the IEEE 488.2
 4                <CHARACTER RESPONSE DATA> syntax. If both a long and short form element are
                  specified, only the short form shall be sent.
 5
                  It is not required that a data format parser accept all values of an enumerated set. An error
 6                may be generated on receipt of an unimplemented value. See 2 of this section.
                  Mnemonic generation rules for character data apply. See “Syntax and Style,” 2.2.1.

4       Grammar
        This chapter specifies the grammar of the data format. This grammar describes the contents          DIF01
        of a <dif_expression> that represents a Data Interchange Format.

4.1     Grammar Notation                                                                                    1
        The grammar notation consists of the non-terminal symbols, pseudo-terminal symbols,
        meta-symbols, and terminal symbols defined below.                                                   2
4.1.1   Non-terminals                                                                                       3
        Non-terminals are represented as all lowercase words.
4.1.2   Pseudo-terminals                                                                                    4
        Pseudo-terminals stand for any from a set of terminal symbols (value types) as described in
                                                                                                            5
        3.4 of this section and are represented as words bracketed between < and >.
4.1.3   Meta-symbols                                                                                        6
        In the following table, “.” represents an arbitrary string of terminals and non-terminals. The
        meta-symbols for the grammar are ->, {, }, *, +, [, ], and |.                                       7
        They have the following meanings:                                                                   8
              ->             Separates the left and right hand sides of a production
                                                                                                            9
               { . }*         The enclosed item occurs zero or more times.
                                                                                                          10
               { . }+         The enclosed item occurs one or more times.
                                                                                                          11
               [.]            The enclosed item occurs zero or one times.
                                                                                                          12
               {.|.|.}        One and only one of the two or more enclosed items separated by | occurs.
                                                                                                          13
4.1.4   Terminal Symbols                                                                                  14
        Terminal symbols are represented in mixed uppercase and lowercase to indicate long and
        short form (“Syntax and Style,” 1).                                                               15

         4.3      Required Blocks
 6                Note that a data set shall contain a DIF block and at least one DIMension and one DATA
                  block.
                                                                                                                     DIF01
 7                All TRACe blocks referenced by keywords in the VIEW and DATA blocks shall be present.
                  All DIMension blocks referenced by LABel keywords in the TRACe block shall be present.
 8
                  If the DIF(SCOPe) keyword is not present or is set to FULL, any CURVe block shall contain         TK032a
 9                a VALues keyword and parameters. If DIF(SCOPe) is present and set to PREamble,
                  VALues keywords and parameters shall be omitted from all CURVe blocks.
10
         4.4      Required Order
11                When an instrument accepts data, certain blocks shall be sent in the following order:

12                                      DIF                                                                          DIF01
                                        ENCode
13                                      DIMension
                                        TRACe
14                                      VIEW
                                        DATA
15
                  In addition, the ORDer must appear before the DATA block. The REMark and IDENtify
16                blocks may appear anywhere after the DIF block.
                                                                                                                     DIF01
17                Within the DATA block, the DELTa sub-block shall precede all other sub-blocks.
                  Within a block, individual keywords may also be accepted in any order with the exception
18                that the CTYPe keyword must come before the VALues keyword.
19                When an instrument sends data, the block and keyword order specified in the grammar is
                  required.
20
         4.5      Unrecognized Keywords and Blocks                                                                   DIF03
21                A listener is not required to interpret all keywords and blocks present in a data set, but only
                  those required for the type of data of interest. For example, all listeners must interpret most
22                keywords and sub-blocks in the DIF, DIMension, ENCode, and ORDer blocks since

         4-6   Grammar
                     1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

information contained in these blocks is required for the correct interpretation of data in the
DATA block. Exceptions are keywords such as NOTE, RESolution, HRANge, etc. Other
keywords and blocks may or may not be of interest to a listener. For example, a listener that
seeks only WAVeform data will ignore CURVe data, and vice versa.
This is consistent with the philosophy that different listeners may accept the same data set        1
but use it for different purposes. In addition, the data format provides an extension
mechanism that is designed to allow older listeners to accept newer data sets that may              2
contain new keywords and sub-blocks. See 5 of this section for further details on extension
mechanisms.                                                                                         3
Therefore, listeners must be able to ignore unrecognized (but syntactically correct) keywords       4
and blocks. The extent, if any, to which a listener notifies a user that an unrecognized
keyword or block was encountered; and, the extent, if any, of required user action is               5
implementation dependent.
Note that a block name is always followed by an open parenthesis; or, an equal sign,
                                                                                                    6
modifier, and open parenthesis sequence. This following structure may be ignored by                 7
searching forward to the matching closing parenthesis. A keyword is always followed by one
or more comma separated values.                                                                     8

5     Data Format Extensions
      This format may be extended and enhanced with one of the following two methods.

5.1   Extensions
      Keywords, blocks (sub-blocks) may be created to accomodate information that is not                1
      otherwise provided for by existing keywords or blocks. This method of extension can be
      done without conflict because parsers ignore unknown keywords and blocks. Name aliases            2
      may be specifed for the new keywords or blocks. However, the use of aliases is strongly
      discouraged and should only be provided if there is widespread industry usage of more than        3
      one name.
                                                                                                        4
5.2   Enhancements
      A second method of extension involves replacing an existing keyword with a sub-block of           5
      the same name. This method is used when the semantic information represented by an
                                                                                                        6
      existing keyword is insufficient. The replacement sub-block shall include a keyword that
      represents the exact same semantic information (including the same value type and range) of       7
      the original keyword. This keyword is distinguished from all other keywords in the new
      sub-block by appending an underscore to it. No alias names may be added for the new               8
      sub-block.
      A parser which was implemented before the extension was made recognizes this special              9
      keyword by the presence of the underscore and then takes the value associated with this
                                                                                                       10
      flagged keyword and assigns it to the old keyword. The remainder of the sub-block is
      discarded.                                                                                       11   HP072




5.3   Extension Example                                                                                12
      Suppose sometime in the future a need for a sub-block under RANGe is recognized. In this
      version the syntax for RANGe is:                                                                 13
             RANGe          <+Numeric>
                                                                                                       14
      The extended syntax might appear as:
             RANGe (                                                                                   15
                   HIGH_         <+Numeric>
                   [LOW          <+Numeric>]
                                                                                                       16
                   [OVER         <+Numeric>]
                                                                                                       17
             )
                                                                                                       18
      A newer implementation would understand the meaning for all three values under RANGe.
      An older parser takes the values associated with the flagged keyword in the sub-block, in this   19
      case, HIGH_, and uses its value as the value for RANGe. Since the older parser has no need
      for the LOW and OVER values, they are discarded.                                                 20
                                                                                                       21
                                                                                                       22
                                                                   Data Format Extensions        5-1
                                      1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

                  This extension can be continued. At some even later date, more sub-blocks are needed. The
                  syntax might now become:
                         RANGe (
                                HIGH_ (
                                       EXPected_ <+Numeric>
 1                                     [ALLowed <+Numeric>]
                                )
 2                              LOW (
                                       EXPected_ <+Numeric>
 3                                     [ALLowed <+Numeric>]
                                )
 4                              OVER (
                                       EXPected_ <+Numeric>
     5
                                       [ALLowed <+Numeric>]
 6                              )
                         )
 7
                  The original parser could still successfully determine which value to associate with the old
 8                keyword RANGe and safely discard the rest. Both the intermediate and newest parsers can
                  handle this syntax without conflict.

6     Block Descriptions
      This chapter details all of the block descriptions for the data interface format.

6.1   Top Level Block Organization                                                                     DIF01
      The entire data set is composed of the following sequence of mandatory and optional blocks.      1
         dif ->                difid                                                                  TK053a
                                                                                                       2
                               [remark]
                               [identify]                                                              3
                               [encode]
                               {dimension}+                                                            4
                               [order]
                               {trace}*                                                                5
                               {view}*
                               {data}+                                                                 6
      A data set is built from the blocks described in 6.2 through 6.10 of this section.               7
                                                                                                      TK053a

6.2   DATA                                                                                             8DIF03
      A DATA block contains the data of primary interest. It may contain dimensioned data such
      as DATA(CURVe), or specific sets of data (WAVeform, etc.). At least one DATA block is            9
      required, and multiple DATA blocks are allowed. A DATA block is defined as:
                                                                                                      10DIF03
         data ->           DATA [=    <Label>](
                              [NOTE   <String>]                                                       11
                              [delta]
                              [curve]                                                                 12
                              {waveform}*
                              {measurement}*                                                          13
                           )
                                                                                                      14
      <Label> is optional and allows for the unique identification of the DATA block; no two
      DATA blocks may have the same <Label> value within a data set.                                  15
      The subordinate blocks within a particular DATA block are assumed to be related. That is, if    16
      CURVe and WAVeform measurements are present in the same DATA block, the
      WAVeform measurements are assumed to have been derived from the CURVe data. If that             17
      is not the case, different DATA blocks should be used for the CURVe and WAVeform
      measurements.                                                                                   18
                                                                                                      19
                                                                                                      20
                                                                                                      21
                                                                                                      22
                                                                           Block Descriptions   6-1
                                           1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

         6.2.1       NOTE                                                                                             DIF03
                     This is arbitrary text.
                     Value type is <String>. Text should be human-readable. Only one occurrence of the NOTE
                     keyword is allowed and only one value is allowed.
 1                   Example: NOTE “Humidity was 45%”
 2       6.2.2       DELTa                                                                                            DIF03
                     A DELta sub-block provides for sequences of closely related data. When a data set contains
 3                   multiple occurrences of DATA blocks, the DELta block differentiates the characteristics of
                     each of the DATA blocks. Note that the DELta block is limited to redefining descriptive
 4                   information, encoding information, and dimension size, such as SCALe, DATE, and
                     OFFSet. A DELta block cannot change the organization of the data, such as the number of
 5                   dimensions or the data ordering.
     6               The values specified in a DELta block override those specified at a higher hierarchical level.
                     For example, the value for SCALe in the DATA(DELta(DIMension)) block overrides the
 7                   value for SCALe in the higher level DIMension block, but only for data within the DATA
 8                   block that contains the DELta block. If there are multiple DATA blocks with subordinate
                     DELta blocks, the DELta blocks have no effect on each other; that is, they each individually
 9                   specify a modification of the same (higher level) IDENtify, DIMension, or ENCode block.
                     The DELta sub-block may occur only once and, if present, shall be the first block in the
10                   DATA block. The DELta sub-block is defined as:
                                                                                                                      DIF03
11                      delta ->           DELTa(
                                              [NOTE               <String>]
12                                            {DIMension =        <Label> (
                                                 [SCALe           <Numeric>]
13                                               [OFFSet          <Numeric>]
                                                 [SIZE            <+NR1>]
14                                            )}+
                                              [DATE               <NR1>,<+NR1>,<+NR1>
15                                                                [,<NR1>,<+NR1>,<+NR1>]]                             DIF06
                                               [TIME              <0+NR1>,<0+NR1>,<0+Numeric>
16                                                                [,<0+NR1>,<0+NR1>,<0+Numeric>]]                     DIF06
                                           )
17

                     one and only one of the following enumerated set values:

         6-4     Block Descriptions

                 CRC16                 16-bit cyclic redundancy check code. x16 + x15 +x2 + 1. (default)
                 CCITT                 16-bit cyclic redundancy check code. x16 + x12 +x5 + 1.
                 SUM8                  8-bit longitudinal redundancy check code (8 bit sum). x8 + 1.
                                       (SUM8 is provided for compatibility and its use is discouraged).
                 SUM16                 16-bit longitudinal redundancy check code (16 bit sum). x16 + 1.

          The checksum is computed according to the rules specified by CTYPe. If data is formatted in
          <Numeric> value type, the checksum is computed using the 8-bit ASCII decimal equivalent          14

          characters but not white space.                                                                  15

         6-6   Block Descriptions
                    1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

In the absence of a TRACe block, the following rules are used to determine the independent
and dependent dimensions:
       1. The independent dimension is the first implicit dimension or, if no implicit
       dimensions are present, then the first explicit dimension
                                                                                                    1
       2. The dependent dimension is the first explicit dimension if there is at least one
       implicit dimension. Otherwise it is the second explicit dimension.                           2
The block modifier <Label> value is optional and allows for the unique identification of the        3
WAVeform block. No two WAVeform blocks may have the same <Label> within the same
DATA block.                                                                                         4
If WAVeform measurements are found together with a CURVe block in a DATA block,
                                                                                                    5
they are considered to be derived from or related to the CURVe data (or a subset of it).
However, the exact relationship of waveform measurements to the data can be determined              6
only if the TRACe keyword is present.
It is permissible for a data set to contain waveform measurements without a DATA(CURVe)             7
block, but DIMension blocks for the independent and dependent dimensions shall still be
specified.
                                                                                                    8
Waveform measurements derived from DATA block data are considered to have been                      9
derived from the data after SCALe and OFFSet (specified in the DIMension block) have
been applied. WAVeform measurements are derived from DIMension block units.                        10
Note that this standard requires the syntax for WAVeform data to be correct, but makes no          11
claim for the correctness or consistency of the data values. Keywords in the WAVeform
block are representative of terms generally used in the industry. Keyword descriptions are         12
general and, except where specifically provided (such as for HLMethod), no requirement for
specific calculation methods are claimed.                                                          13
The definitions for functions and settings within the waveform block are illustrated with the      14
following figure:

                   This is arbitrary text. Text should be human-readable.

 1                 Example: NOTE “500 ps Reference Waveform”

                   This is an arbitrary name of the waveform measurement. Typically, NAME is more

                   This notes the method used to determine the HIGH and LOW magnitudes.
13

                   defined by IEEE 194, sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.2.
15
                   Value type is <String>. It is recommended that the string length be 32 characters or less. The
16                 following values are predefined:
                        UNKNOWN                     Unknown or Unspecified. Default.
17                      MEAN                        Mean of Density Algorithm (IEEE 181, section 4.3.1.1)
                        MODE                        Mode of Density Algorithm (IEEE 181, section 4.3.1.2)
18                      PEAK                        Peak Magnitude (IEEE 181, section 4.3.1.4)
                        ABSOLUTE                    Absolute, user-specified levels

6.3     DIMension                                                                                       16
        Each DIMension block describes one dimension of DATA(CURVe) data. A dimension may
        be either explicit, in which case values are present in the DATA(CURVe) block, or implicit,     17
        in which case the values are not present, but are instead generated by a function. See 1.3 in
        this section. The order in which dimensions appear determines the data ordering in the          18
        DATA block.
                                                                                                        19
        The DIMension and ORDer blocks describe the logical structure and organization of data in
        the DATA(CURVe) block. The ENCode block describes the physical representation or                20
        encoding of the data. The ORDer block describes the ordering of the dimensional data
        elements in the DATA(CURVe) block. Together they provide the sufficient and necessary           21
        information for correct extraction of the data.
                                                                                                        22
                                                                          Block Descriptions     6-17
                                         1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

                   Whether a dimension is to be considered an independent or dependent dimension is
                   determined by the TRACe block. In the absence of a TRACe block, the following simple
                   rule is applied: if one or more implicit dimensions are present, they are considered to be
                   independent, and all explicit dimensions are considered to be dependent.

 1                 A DIMension block is required for each dimension of the data (implicit and explicit). The
                   DIMension block is defined as:
                                                                                                                 DIF03
 2                     dimension -> DIMension = <Label>(
                                      [NOTE    <String>]
 3                                    [NAME    <String>]
                                      TYPE     {IMPLicit | EXPLicit}

                                      [OFFSet <Numeric>]
 5
                                      [SIZE    <+NR1>]
     6                                UNITs    <String>
                                      [encode]
 7                                  )

 8                 Each dimension is uniquely distinguished by its required block modifier <Label> value. No
                   two DIMension blocks may have the same <Label> value. Dimension labels should be kept
 9                 short, yet meaningful.
10       6.3.1     NOTE                                                                                          DIF03
                   This is arbitrary text.

                   Example: NOTE “DS1C at test point 12”

6.3.4   SCALe                                                                                               DIF03
        Scaling factor to be applied to the dimension’s values in DATA(CURVe(VALues)).
        Value type is <Numeric>. Default value is 1.0. Only one occurrence of SCALe is allowed
        and only one value is allowed. The SCALe value may be overridden by
        DATA(DELTa(DIMension(SCALe))).                                                                      1
        SCALe is always applied to DATA(CURVe) data, but not to any other data, such as
        DATA(WAVeform).
                                                                                                            2
        For implicit dimensions:                                                                            3
             X’ = (SCALe * i) + OFFSet i = 1 to SIZE
                                                                                                            4
        For explicit dimensions:
             X’ = (SCALe * X) + OFFSet                                                                      5
        where X is a value from DATA(CURVe(VALues)). Also see Section 5.6, ORDer.
                                                                                                            6
        Example: SCALe 0.5E-2
                                                                                                            7
6.3.5   OFFSet                                                                                              DIF03
        Offset factor to be applied to the dimension’s values in DATA(CURVe(VALues)).                       8
        Value type is <Numeric>. Default value is zero. Only one occurrence of OFFSet is allowed
        and only one value is allowed. The OFFSet value may be overridden by                                9
        DATA(DELTa(DIMension(OFFSet))).
                                                                                                           10
        OFFSet is always applied to DATA(CURVe) data, but not to any other data, such as
        DATA(WAVeform).                                                                                    11
        For implicit dimensions:                                                                           12
             X’ = (SCALe * i) + OFFSet i = 1 to SIZE
        For explicit dimensions:                                                                           13
             X’ = (SCALe * X) + OFFSet
                                                                                                           14
        X is a value from DATA(CURVe(VALues)).
                                                                                                           15
        Example: OFFSet -1.0E-2
6.3.6   SIZE                                                                                               16DIF03
        This is the number of points or values in the dimension.
                                                                                                           17
        Value is type <+NR1>. Only one occurrence of SIZE is allowed and only one value is
        allowed. The SIZE value may be overridden by DATA(DELTa(DIMension(SIZE))).                         18
        The following two invariants hold:                                                                 19
               1.        All explicit dimensions must have the same SIZE value.
               2.        The product of the SIZE values of the implicit dimensions                         20
                         must equal the SIZE value of any explicit dimension.
        If SIZE is not specified for a dimension, it is assumed to be consistent with the above            21
        invariants. It is an error if there is insufficient information to determine a dimension’s SIZE.
        For example, SIZE cannot be determined if two or more implicit dimensions do not specify a         22
                                                                           Block Descriptions      6-19

                   SIZE, nor can it be determined if two or more explicit dimensions specify different SIZE

6.4     ENCode
        The ENCode block addresses data resolution, special range values, and encoding format             2
        <Block> value type data.
                                                                                                          3
        The scope of an ENCode block is determined by its hierarchical level in the data format
        structure. If the ENCode block is at the same level as DIMension blocks, it applies globally      4
        to all data in the DATA blocks. A global encoding specification can, however, be overridden
        on a dimension-by-dimension basis with an ENCode block that is subordinate to the                 5
        particular dimension. A keyword specification at the higher level rules unless explicitly
        superceded by the same keyword at the subordinate level.                                          6
        Only one ENCode block can be specified at the same hierarchical level as DIMension                7
        blocks, and only one ENCode block can be specified subordinate to a DIMension block.
        The ENCode block is not required at any hierarchical level. However, the specification of         8
        HRANge and LRANge for all explicit dimensions is strongly recommended. The ENCode
        block is defined as:
                                                                                                          9
           encode ->        ENCode (                                                                     10

         6.4.2     FORMat
                   This is the data encoding format for CURVe(VALue) data. <Block> value type is introduced
                   by a pound sign followed by one or more decimal digit characters. See section 3.4.5. ASCII
 1                 representation uses comma separated <Numeric> data.
                   Specifying a block FORMat does not require that the values in DATA block be formatted as
 2                 <Block> value type. Values may always be specified as <Numeric>.
 3                 If the ENCode block is subordinate to a DIMension block, then FORMat applies only to
                   values in DATA(CURVe(VALues)) for the particular dimension.
 4
                   FORMat takes a specified enumerated set of values. Only one occurrence of FORMat is
 5                 allowed and only one of the following enumerated set values is allowed:

     6                    ASCii         Comma-separated <Numeric> data
                          IFP32         IEEE floating point, 32 bits.
 7                        IFP64         IEEE floating point, 64 bits.
                          INT8          IEEE 8-bit signed integer (default).
 8                        INT16         IEEE 16-bit signed integer.
                          INT32         IEEE 32-bit signed integer.
 9                        INT64         IEEE 64-bit signed integer.
                          SFP32         IEEE swapped floating point, 32 bits.
10                        SFP64         IEEE swapped floating point, 64 bits.
                          SINT16        Swapped IEEE 16-bit signed integer.                                       TK055
11                        SINT32        Swapped IEEE 32-bit signed integer.                                       TK055
                          SINT64        Swapped IEEE 64-bit signed integer.                                       TK055
12                        SUINT16       Swapped IEEE 16-bit unsigned integer.                                     TK055
                          SUINT32       Swapped IEEE 32-bit unsigned integer.                                     TK055
13                        SUINT64       Swapped IEEE 64-bit unsigned integer.                                     TK055
                          UINT8         IEEE 8-bit unsigned integer.                                              TK055
14
                          UINT16        IEEE 16-bit unsigned integerUINT16.                                       TK055
15                        UINT32        IEEE 32-bit unsigned integerUINT32.                                       TK055
                          UINT64        IEEE 64-bit unsigned integerUINT64.                                       TK055
16
                   All signed integers are two’s complement. IEEE formats are defined by IEEE 488.2 Binary        TK055
17                 Integer and Binary Unsigned Integer codes. “Swapped” means that the byte order (from low
                   to high address) is from least significant to most significant byte.
18
                   For example, to transfer #H1234 as an INT16 (16-bit integer) across a byte oriented
19                 transmission medium, transfer the first byte as 12 (hex) and the second byte as 34 (hex). To
                   transfer #H1234 as an SINT16 (swapped 16-bit integer), transfer the first byte as 34 (hex)
20                 and the second byte as 12 (hex).
                   Similarly, to transfer #H12345678 as an INT32 (32-bit integer), transfer the bytes in the
21                 order: 12 (hex), 34 (hex), 56 (hex), and 78 (hex). To transfer #H12345678 as an SINT32
22

         6-22    Block Descriptions
                             1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

        (32-bit swapped integer), transfer the bytes in the order: 78 (hex), 56 (hex), 34 (hex), and
        12 (hex).
        Example: FORMat INT16
6.4.3   NVALue
        This is the numeric value (before application of SCALe and OFFSet) that is to be treated as          1
        implying “not a number” or “no value recorded” for values in the DATA block.
                                                                                                             2
        Value type is <Numeric>. Only one occurrence of NVALue is allowed and only one value is
        allowed. If NVALue is not present, no not-a-number value is defined for integer formats. For         3
        IEEE floating point formats, no NVALue is ever specified. In this case, NVALue is as
        defined by IEEE 754 for not-a-number. For ASCII, the default value is 9.91E+37.                      4
        Example: NVALue 9999                                                                                 5
6.4.4   ORANge
        This indicates the numeric value (before application of SCALe and OFFSet) that is to be
                                                                                                             6

        Value type is <Numeric>. Only one occurrence of ORANge is allowed and only one value is
        allowed. If ORANge is not present, no over range value is defined for integer formats. For           8
        IEEE floating point formats, no ORANge is ever specified. In this case, ORANGe is as
        defined by IEEE 754 for plus infinity. For ASCII, the default value is 9.9E+37.                      9
        Example: ORANge #H7FFF                                                                              10
6.4.5   URANge                                                                                              11
        This is the numeric value (before application of SCALe and OFFSet) that is to be treated as
        under range for values in the DATA block.                                                           12
        Value type is <Numeric>. Only one occurrence of URANge is allowed and only one value is
        allowed. If URANge is not present, no under range value is defined for integer formats. For         13
        IEEE floating point formats, no URANge is ever specified. In this case, URANGe is as
                                                                                                            14
        defined by IEEE 754 for negative infinity. For ASCII, the default value is -9.9E+37.

                                                                                                            18
        allowed. The value specified shall be at least as great as the greatest value present in the data

14                 data and 0 to 59.999... for instruments sending data.
15                 If two sets of values are specified, they define an inclusive range of time.                     DIF06

16                 Example: TIME 23,59,59 indicates one second before midnight.                                     DIF06

 9       6.6        ORDer
                    The ORDer block defines the physical layout of data within the DATA(CURVe) block. Data         TK052
10                  may be ordered as n-tuples, in which the data for each explicit dimension is “inter-mixed”.
11                  This is also called row order. Data may also be ordered by dimension. When ordered by
                    dimension, all data for each dimension is grouped consecutively, with all data for one
12                  dimension followed by all data for the next dimension. This is also called column order.
                    When more than one implicit dimension exists, the first implicit dimension index always
13                  increments the slowest and the last implicit dimension index always increments the fastest.
14                  The ORDer block may occur only once, but is not required. If omitted, the default values for
                    its keywords prevail. The ORDer block is defined as:
15                                                                                                                  DIF03
                        order ->          ORDer (
16                                           [NOTE      <String>]
                                             [BY        {TUPLe | DIMension}]
17                                        )

18       6.6.1      NOTE                                                                                            DIF03
                    This is arbitrary text.
19
                    Value type is <String>. Text should be human-readable. Only one occurrence of the NOTE
20                  keyword is allowed and only one value is allowed.

21                  Example: NOTE “Most important first”
         6.6.2      BY
22                  This indicates if the ordering is by tuple or dimension.

         6-28     Block Descriptions
                            1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format
                                                                                                           DIF03
        BY takes a specified enumerated set of values. BY may occur only once, and takes one of
        the two following enumerated set values:
             TUPLe                    Data values are organized by n-tuple (default).
             DIMension                Data values are organized by dimension.

         6.8       DIF
 5                 The DIF block is the first block in a dif data set. It uniquely defines the expression data as       TK053a
                   being a dif data set with the beginning DIF character sequence. The DIF block provides
     6             version information to assist the parser in determining compatibility. It further defines the
 7                 scope of the data set.

 8

                   This is arbitrary text.

                   keyword is allowed and only one value is allowed.
14
                   Example: NOTE “First Version”

         6.8.2     VERSion
16                 The DIF(VERSion) number exactly tracks the SCPI SYSTem:VERSion number (Command                       TK053a
                   Reference, 21.20) and correlates changes and extensions in the DIF volume with the rest of
17                 SCPI.
                   Note: The DIF(VERSion) keyword was new in 1994.0 and was created as a part of a
18
                   one-time major restructuring and simplification of DIF. DIF parsers designed prior to 1994
19                 will not be compatible with 1994.0 and following versions.
                   Value type is <+Numeric>. Only one value is allowed. Only one occurrence of VERSion is
20                 allowed.
21                 Note that while version numbers increase in value in time sequence, lesser version numbers
                   will not necessarily be guaranteed to be fully compatible.

6.9     TRACe                                                                                            10DIF03
        TRACe blocks describe logical relationships among all or some of the dimensions. They
        may define functions, curves, surfaces, or arbitrary sets or data groupings. They also provide   11
        a convenient means of describing subsets of the data. The windowing effect of the TRACe
        blocks may, for example, be used to make two-dimensional “cuts” through                          12
        three-dimensional data. Other blocks, such as the VIEW block, build on TRACe blocks.
        TRACe block information is built from DIMension blocks; VIEW blocks are built from               13
        TRACe block information.
                                                                                                         14
        If no TRACe block is present, the independence or dependence of a dimension is determined
        by rules described in 6.3 in this section.                                                       15
                                                                                                         16DIF03
        The TRACe block is optional and multiple TRACe blocks are allowed. The TRACe block is
        defined as:
           trace ->          TRACe = <Label>(                                                            17
                                [NOTE                <String>]
                                [NAME                <String>]                                           18
                                [SYMMetry            <String>]
                                {INDependent(                                                            19
                                   LABel             <Label>
                                   [STARt            <+NR1>]                                             20
                                   [STOP             <+NR1>]
                                )}*                                                                      21
                                {DEPendent(
                                                                                                         22
                                                                          Block Descriptions      6-33
                                         1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

                                                LABel            <Label>
                                             )}*
                                         )

                   The TRACe block modifier <Label> value is required. It provides for the unique
 1                 identification of the TRACe block. As <Label> for the entire data set are unique, no two
                   TRACe blocks may have the same <Label>.
 2
                   Explicit and implicit, as applied to dimensions, are distinguished from independent and
 3                 dependent as follows. Implicit and explicit are concerned with how the data is physically
                   represented and structured. Independent and dependent relate to how a dimension is
 4                 interpreted.

                   following values are predefined:

         6.10      VIEW                                                                                         DIF03
10                 VIEW blocks provide semantic information about the data in DATA(CURVe). With a
                   VIEW block, one can show relationships between and among subsets of the data as defined
11                 by TRACe blocks. For example, a complex waveform or surface can be easily defined, as
                   can a waveform and its upper and lower envelopes.
12
                   The VIEW block builds on traces described in a TRACe block. A trace commonly defines a
13                 simple function, but the data format allows for the definition of sets, surfaces and other
                   complex functions.
14                 For example, a time varying envelope might be described by three DIMension blocks. The
                   two explicit dimensions define the two Y-axis values for the upper and lower components of
15
                   the envelope. The implicit dimension defines the common X-axis. While the organizational
16                 structure of the data is defined by the DIMension and ORDer blocks, its meaning is
                   determined by a VIEW block. It is the view block that identifies which dimension is the
17                 upper envelope and which is the lower.
                   Alternatively, the same data could be viewed as a complex waveform. The DIMension
18                 blocks would be the same, but a VIEW block would identify which dimension is the real
19                 component and which is the complex component.
                   The VIEW block is optional and multiple VIEW blocks are allowed. The VIEW block is
20                 defined as:
21
22                                                                                                              DIF03

         6-36    Block Descriptions
                               1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

            view ->            VIEW = <Label> (                                                              HP091
                                  [NOTE               <String>]
                                  [NAME               <String>]
                                  {ENVelope(
                                     UPPer            <Label>
                                     LOWer            <Label>                                                 1
                                     [FUNCtion        <Label>]
                                  )}*                                                                         2
                                  {RCOMplex(
                                     REAL             <Label>                                                 3
                                     IMAGinary        <Label>
                                  )}                                                                          4
                                  {PCOMplex(
                                     MAGNitude        <Label>                                                 5
                                     PHASe            <Label>
                                  )}                                                                          6
                               )
                                                                                                              7
         The modifier label is required. It provides for the unique identification of the VIEW block.
                                                                                                              8
         As all <Label> elements are unique, no two VIEW blocks may have the same label.
         A VIEW block takes the following sub-blocks. Except for NAME and NOTE, only one type                 9
         of the other sub-blocks may be present:
                                                                                                             10
6.10.1   NOTE                                                                                                 DIF03
         This is arbitrary text.                                                                             11
         Value type is <String>. Text should be human-readable. Only one occurrence of the NOTE
                                                                                                             12
         keyword is allowed and only one value is allowed.
         Example: NOTE “Template defines the max and min values for calibrating mil spec                     13
         97654-D”
                                                                                                             14
6.10.2   NAME                                                                                                 DIF03
         This is the name of the view. NAME is typically more descriptive than the VIEW block                15
         label and does not need to be unique.
                                                                                                             16
         Value type is <String>. It is recommended that the string length be 32 characters or less.
         Only one occurrence of NAME is allowed and only one value is allowed.                               17
         Example: NAME “97654-D”

7   Data Format Example
    The following data set exemplifies the use of several related blocks in the data interchange
    format. The example below is shown encapsulated in parentheses; that is, as a
    <dif_expression>.
                                                                                                      1DIF01
                  ( DIF (
                        VERsion 1993.0)                                                               2
                  IDENtify (
                        DATE 1993,4,23                                                                3DIF06
                        TIME 16,4,14.23)                                                              DIF06
                  ENCode (                                                                            4
                        FORMat INT8
                        HRANge 127                                                                    5
                        LRANge -128)
                  DIMension=YH (                                                                      6
                        TYPE EXPLicit
                        SCALe 2.000000E-002                                                           7
                        OFFSet -3.500000E-001
                        SIZE 512                                                                      8
                        UNITs “V”)
                  DIMension=YL (                                                                      9
                        TYPE EXPLicit
                        SCALe 2.000000E-002                                                          10
                        OFFSet -3.500000E-001
                        SIZE 512                                                                     11
                        UNITs “V”)
                  DIMension=X (                                                                      12
                        TYPE IMPLicit
                        SCALe 2.000000E-005                                                          13
                        OFFSet -1.024000E-002
                        SIZE 512                                                                     14
                        UNITs “s”)
                  TRACe=H (                                                                          15
                        INDependent(
                              LABel X)
                                                                                                     16
                        DEPendent(
                              LABel YH))
                                                                                                     17
                  TRACe=L (
                                                                                                     18
                        INDependent(
                              LABel X)                                                               19
                        DEPendent (
                              LABel YL))                                                             20
                  VIEW=ENV1 (
                        ENVelope (                                                                   21
                              UPPer H
                              LOWer L))                                                              22
                                                                    Data Format Example        7-1
                                      1999 SCPI Data Interchange Format

                                DATA (
                                    CURVe (
                                        VALue #41024{1024 8-bit significant bytes of data goes here}
                                        CSUM 139))
                                    WAVeform (
 1                                      TRACe H
                                        RISE (
 2                                             TIME 1.04E-003)
                                        FALL (
 3                                             TIME 0.86E-003)))

 4                In this example, we have a data set that follows the 1993.0 version of SCPI and is dated at     DIF01,06
                                                                                                                         HP072




                  about 4 PM on April 23rd, 1993. The data is encoded as 8-bit signed integers ranging from
 5                -128 to 127 and is presented as a sequence of 512 byte pairs representing two voltage signal
                  levels (YH and YL). The raw bit values must be multiplied by .02 with .35 subtracted to
 6                yield the measured value in Volts. The first data pair occurred at a measured time (X) of (20
     7            - 10,240 microseconds) or -10.22 milliseconds. Subsequent data pairs were recorded at 20
                  microsecond intervals.
 8
                  Two traces (H and L) are specified with YH and YL voltage levels as the dependent
 9                variables and time as the independent variable. The traces can be viewed as envelope-type
                  data and referred to as ENV1. The data itself is formatted in IEEE 488.2 block format (1024
10                bytes long) and its integrity can be verified by computing a 16-bit cyclic redundancy check
                  and comparing the results to the stated (CSUM) value of 139.
11
                  Finally, the rise and fall times of the H trace have been computed and recorded in the data
12                set as 1.04 milliseconds and 0.86 milliseconds.

1       Introduction
        This volume defines the SCPI commands and behavior needed to implement functionality
        sets associated with common classes of instruments. Each chapter covers a particular
        instrument class. A class could be, for example, a power supply, voltmeter, or switcher. Each
        chapter stands by itself so a designer may focus on only the chapters that apply to a             1
        particular design.                                                                                2
1.1     Scope                                                                                             3
        This volume covers the major classes of electronic instruments supported by the commands          4
        and behaviors as defined in SCPI Volumes 1 through 3. This volume does not extend SCPI
        with unsupported or contradictory commands or behaviors.                                          5
        As new applications for SCPI are explored, additional chapters will be added.                     6
1.2     Definition of Terms
                                                                                                          7
        Functionality - an aspect of instrument operation which is described by SCPI commands and         8
        their associated behavior.
                                                                                                          9
                  Functionality set
                  A grouping of functionality which shall be implemented as a whole.
                                                                                                         10
                  Instrument class
                                                                                                         11
                  A generally recognized type of instrument, for example switcher, power supply,         12
                  or voltmeter.
                                                                                                         13
                  Base functionality
                  That functionality set required in an instrument of a given class.
                                                                                                         14
                  Additional functionality                                                               15
                  One or more functionality sets defined for an instrument class beyond the base         16
                  functionality.
                                                                                                         17
1.3     Purpose                                                                                          18
        This volume is designed to further the overall SCPI goal of reducing ATE program
        development time by:                                                                             19
                  Reducing the ATE product development time by guiding designers in the usage of         20
                  SCPI from the more familiar, instrument class point of view.                           21
                  Achieving a higher degree of consistency among implementations of the same             22
                  instrument class.
                                                                                                         23
1.3.1   Guiding Designers
        The Command Reference Volume describes commands that cover a wide variety of                     24
        instrument classes and technologies. Picking commands from this alphabetically sorted list       25
        appropriate for a particular instrument can be daunting.
                                                                                                         26


                                                                                   Introduction    1-1
                                           1999 SCPI Instrument Classes

                     This volume uses terms familiar to the designer to help relate SCPI to previous design
                     experiences. Volume 4 provides a translation from the SCPI Command Reference
                     vocabulary to the vocabulary common to an instrument class.
                     The Command Reference purposely presents certain subsystems in broad terms. For
     1               example, triggering is a function used in almost all instruments, but in slightly different
                     ways. This volume provides further guidance to designers on how to apply certain
 2                   subsystems, like TRIGger, to a particular instrument class.
 3       1.3.2       Achieving Consistency
 4                   Because SCPI covers many instrument classes, it cannot require all instruments to
                     implement all commands. It can, however, define an instrument base functionality by
 5                   specifying a relatively small set of commands and behaviors. A programmer can depend on a
 6                   level of consistency among SCPI instruments of the same class.
 7                   By staying within the base functionality, a programmer can avoid all Command Errors.
                     Execution errors are still possible. For example, this volume cannot specify
 8                   <numeric_value> ranges. The programmer, however, can use the required MIN/MAX
 9                   queries to establish range limits. Specific required values are shown where the parameter
                     type is <CHARACTER PROGRAM DATA>.
10
                     Additional functionality may be defined for some instrument classes. None of these
11                   functionality sets are required, but if any set is implemented it shall be implemented in its
12                   entirety.
13       1.4         Instrument Classification
14                   Each chapter defines base functionality for an instrument class. This base functionality is
                     designated with a keyword using SCPI program mnemonic rules. Keywords are also defined
15                   for additional functionality. An ongoing goal of the this volume is to further classify
16                   additional functionality for each instrument class.

17                   An instrument is classified using one or more base functionality keywords along with
                     optional additional functionality keywords. This combination of keywords is an
18                   <instrument_specifier>. Some instruments implement the SYSTem:CAPability? query,
19                   whose response is its <instrument_specifier>.
20       1.4.1       Syntax
                     The syntax of <instrument_specifier> is defined as:
21
22

<af_keyword> is an additional functionality keyword defined in the same instrument chapter       13
which defines the associated <bf_keyword>.
                                                                                                 14
Both <bf_keyword> and <af_keyword> use the mnemonic generation rules described in
Syntax & Style, 6.2.1 when constructing the keywords. The keywords have no short form,           15
but may have a numeric suffix. Only <bf_keyword> and <af_keyword> elements defined in            16
this volume may appear in the response to SYSTem:CAPability?.
                                                                                                 17
The <and_or_oper> is either ‘&’ (ASCII hexadecimal 26) or ‘|’ (ASCII hexadecimal 7C).
The ‘&’ operator connects functionalities which may be active concurrently. The ‘|’ operator     18
indicates that a choice of functionality must be made.                                           19
