 6       1.4.2       Examples
 7                   The simplest <instrument_specifier> describes an instrument with just one base
                     functionality. A power supply with no additional functionality might have an
 8                   <instrument_specifier> of:
 9                      (PSUPPLY)
10                   A simple digital multi-meter might contain several base functionalites, so its
11                   <instrument_specifier> could be:

12                      (DCVOLTMETER|ACVOLTMETER|OHMMETER)

13                   The operator, |, indicates that only one of the base functionalities is available at a time.

14                   A more sophisticated DMM could have an <instrument_specifier> like:
                        (DCVOLTMETER WITH(ETRIGGER&TERMINALS)|ACVOLTMETER
15                      WITH(ETRIGGER&TERMINALS) |DCAMMETER
16                      WITH(ETRIGGER&TERMINALS)|ACAMMETER WITH(ETRIGGER&TERMINALS)
                        |OHMMETER WITH(ETRIGGER&TERMINALS&OCOMPENSATED) |FOHMMETER
17                      WITH(ETRIGGER&TERMINALS&OCOMPENSATED))
18                   Within the <af_expression>, the operator, &, indicates all the additional functionalities are
19                   available simultaneously.

20                   An instrument may contain multiple base functionalities that are used at the same time. The
                     base functionalities may even be described in different chapters of this volume. A scanning
21                   voltmeter could be described with:
22                      (DCVOLTMETER&SWITCHER WITH SCAN)
23       1.5         Compliance
24                   An instrument that complies with SCPI even though it has less than base functionality for its
                     instrument class is still a SCPI instrument, and may be claimed by its manufacturer as such.
25                   However, the manufacturer may not use <instrument_specifier> to describe its instrument
26                   unless it meets the requirements of Volume 4.



         1-4     Introduction
                               1999 SCPI Instrument Classes

      Any product which uses an <instrument_specifier> to describes its capabilities and whose
      response to SYSTem:VERSion? is greater than or equal to 1994.0 shall also implement
      SYSTem:CAPability?
      Note that every instrument will likely have functionality not covered by this volume. The
      designer must still follow the requirements in other volumes when implementing SCPI for            1
      those functionalities.
                                                                                                         2
1.6   Chapter Organization                                                                               3
      Chapters are nominally organized into sections as follows, where x is the chapter number:
                                                                                                         4
                x.1                  Base Functionality
                x.1.1                Base Measurement Instructions (as applies)                          5
                x.1.2                Base Device-oriented Functions                                      6
                x.1.3                Base Status Reporting
                x.2                  Additional Functionality (as applies)                               7
                x.3                  Programming Examples                                                8
                x.4                  Instrument Class specific commands for CALibration
                x.5                  Instrument Class specific commands for DIAGnostics                  9
                x.6                  MEMory subsystem additions                                         10
      Some instrument classes naturally divide into major sub-classes. For example, meters fall         11
      into sub-classes of voltmeter, ammeter, ohmmeter, and others. In this situation, separate
      chapters or other variations on chapter organization may be used.                                 12
      In some instances, it is desired to standardize the way an Instrument or Instrument Class uses    13
      commands in the CALibration and/or DIAGnostic subsystem beyond the commands that are              14
      included in Volume II of SCPI for all instruments. In these cases, Instrument Class specific
      commands can be defined in the Instrument Classes volume for SCPI, but only for                   15
      CALibration and DIAGnostic commands. When this is the case, the commands will be listed           16
      as required commands in the Base Functionality or Extended functionality sections of the
      Instrument Class chapter, and then the commands will be defined in x.4 Instrument Class           17
      specific commands for CALibration and/or x.5 Instrument Class specific commands for               18
      DIAGnostics sections of Instrument Class chapter to which they apply.

18       2.1.3.1   OPERation
19                 :STATus:OPERation
                   For a chassis dynamometer, the bit of interest in the OPERation status structure is the
20                 CDYNO summary bit. While the chassis dynamometer is performing its function, bit 9
21                 (CDYNO summary) shall be used for the chassis dynamometer status. The fanned out
                   register is shown in Figure 2-5.
22
         2.1.3.1.1 CDYNo:CONDition?<16 bit integer word>
23                 :STATus:OPERation:CDYNo:CONDition?
24                 The Dynamometer Program Status Register contains 16 bits that indicate what operation is
                   being performed on the dynamometer. The most significant bit (bit 15) is always 0. The
25
                   dynamometer will be in one of the following processes at all times. All processes are
26                 mutually exclusive and are overlapped, (i.e. with overlapped processes, a command may be
                   sent while a process is executing) but will not be executed until that procedure is completed.

         2.1.3.2      QUEStionable

25                    For the chassis dynamometer, the bit of interest in the QUEStionable status structure is the
                      CDYNO summary bit. When the chassis dynamometer suspects the dynamometer

                      follows:
         2.1.3.2.1 CDYNo:CONDition?<16 bit integer word>
                      :STATus:QUEStionable:CDYNo:CONDition?
                      The Dynamometer Questionable Status Register contains 16 bits that indicate whether the
                      data being acquired is of questionable quality. The most significant bit (bit 15) is always 0.

 3       2.4.1     Dynamometer CALibration Subsystem
 4                 The Dynamometer CALibration subsystem contains the commands needed for calibrating or
                   verifying various components that affect a dynamometers’ measurement capabilities. This
 5                 includes load sensor zero, parasitic loss determination, base inertia determination, and
 6                 dynamometer warm-up.

         2.4.1.1   :BINertia
                   CALibration:BINertia
                   Base Inertia
                   For chassis dynamometers, this node describes the procedure to determine the base
                   mechanical inertia of the dynamometer roll system (all rotating mechanical components
                   outside of the control loop). This procedure consists of an acceleration and deceleration of

         2-18    Chassis Dynamometers
                              1999 SCPI Instrument Class Applications

         the dynamometer rolls, from which a mechanical inertia calculation is made. The                     1
         dynamometer is motored from an initial speed to a final speed at a given constant
         acceleration, and this interval is timed. Immediately, the dynamometer is motored back from
                                                                                                             2
         the final speed to the initial speed at the same constant acceleration (inverted), and this         3
         interval is timed. For this pair of intervals, the force transducer output is continuously
         measured, and the average interval force calculated. The average acceleration is calculated
                                                                                                             4
         using the interval initial and final speed values, and the interval time. This data is used to      5
         calculate the mechanical inertia (Inertia=Force/acceleration). The results are stored in the
         BaseINertia predefined table.
                                                                                                             6
2.4.1.1.1 :AVERage?
                                                                                                             7
         CALibration:BINertia:AVERage?                                                                       8
         This query returns the running average of all base inertia values acquired since the last
         CALibration:BINertia:INITiate was invoked.
                                                                                                             9
2.4.1.1.2 :HSPeed <numeric_value>
                                                                                                            10
         CALibration:BINertia:HSPeed                                                                        11
         High Speed
                                                                                                            12
         The higher magnitude speed (m/s) of the speed interval.
                                                                                                            13
         At *RST, this value is set to 16.
                                                                                                            14
2.4.1.1.3 :INITiate
         CALibration:BINertia:INITiate                                                                      15
         Begin motoring the dynamometer through the ACCeleration/deceleration pairs, using                  16
         :SOURce:ACCeleration as the acceleration/deceleration rate, from LSPeed to HSPeed and
         back, NRUNs times. All query commands must be accepted and responded to while this
                                                                                                            17
         command is executing. This command describes an event and therefore has no associated              18
         *RST condition.
                                                                                                            19
         When this command is initiated for dynamometers, the dynamometer must:
                                                                                                            20
         1. Check critical ancillaries, if any, for proper conditions: Brakes Off, Motor Contactor On,
                                                                                                            21
         parameters within dynamometer safety limits. For conditions that prohibit operation of this
         procedure, issue appropriate warning messages, and execute the Idle Procedure.                     22
         2. Set the DYNO operation condition register Base Inertia Procedure bit indicating the Base        23
         Inertia is executing. Note: The DYNO operation condition register will be further defined in
                                                                                                            24
         Volume 4.
                                                                                                            25
         3. Accelerate/decelerate the dynamometer through the speed intervals, recording time,
         average acceleration, average force for the specified number of runs. The data is placed in        26
         the BaseInertia table after each acceleration/deceleration is run. Update the
         :CALibration:BINertia:SDEViation value based on this run. End the procedure when the
         specified runs are complete.
         4. Clear the DYNO operation condition register Base Insrtia Procedure bit indicating the
         Base Inertia is not executing.


                                                                      Chassis Dynamometers           2-19
                                    1999 SCPI Instrument Class Applications

 1                 5. Issue the process complete message.
     2             6. Execute the Idle Procedure.
 3                 7. Update the on-line mechanical inertia value, if desired.

20       2.4.1.2   :PLOSs
21                 :CALibration:PLOSs
                   Parasitic Loss
22
                   For chassis dynamometers this node describes the commands associated with the parasitic
23
                   loss procedure. This procedure measures and, if requested, updates the parasitic loss
24                 corrections for the dynamometer. The parasitic losses are measured by operating the
                   dynamometer at various selected speeds and measuring the force required to maintain the
25
                   constant speed. This procedure uses the :MEMory table ’ParasiticLOSs’ that defines the
26                 speed points at which parasitic loss measurements are taken. The parasitic loss coefficients
                   are calculated at the end of the procedure and reside in the memory table PCOefficient.




         2-20   Chassis Dynamometers
                            1999 SCPI Instrument Class Applications

2.4.1.2.1 :APCoeff <numeric_value >,numeric_value>,<numeric_value>...                                       1
         :CALibration:PLOSs:APCoeff
         Active Parasitic Coefficients - APCoefficients
                                                                                                            2
         This is the presently active parasitic loss curve used by the dynamometer. The dynamometer
                                                                                                            3
         will maintain coefficients for forward and reverse operations. The appropriate values must         4
         be placed in the APCoeff memory, based on roll rotation. The Active Parasitic Coefficients
         set of retrieved will be based on the currently selected direction.
                                                                                                            5
2.4.1.2.2 :INITiate
                                                                                                            6
         :CALibration:PLOSs:INITiate                                                                        7
         This command starts the parasitic loss procedure. This is an overlapped command. This
         command describes an event and therefore has no associated *RST condition.
                                                                                                            8
         When this command is initiated for dynamometers, the dynamometer must:
                                                                                                            9
         1. Check critical ancillaries, if any, for proper conditions: Brakes Off, Motor Contactor On,
                                                                                                           10
         parameters within dynamometer safety limits. For conditions that prohibit operation of this       11
         procedure, issue appropriate warning messages, and execute the Idle Procedure.
                                                                                                           12
         2. Set the DYNO operation condition register Parasitic Loss Procedure bit indicating the
         Parasitic Loss procedure is executing. Note: The DYNO operation condition register will be
                                                                                                           13
         further defined in Volume 4.                                                                      14
         3. Accelerate dynamometer to the first speed point defined in the ParasiticLOSs memory            15
         table. Stabilize at speed point for defined stabilization time.
                                                                                                           16
         4. Average the force at the roll surface required to maintain the speed set point over the
         latency time. The average force value is placed in the ParasiticLOSs table for the specified
                                                                                                           17
         speed point. Continue until all speed points have been executed in the ParasiticLOSs table.       18
         The first zero speed in the ParasiticLOSs table ends the procedure.
                                                                                                           19
         5. Perform a curve fit on the ParasiticLOSs table data and place the coefficients in the
                                                                                                           20
         memory table PCoeff.
                                                                                                           21
         6. Clear the DYNO operation condition register Parasitic Loss Procedure bit indicating the
         parasitic loss procedure is not executing.                                                        22
         7. Issue the process complete message.                                                            23
         8. Execute the Idle Procedure.                                                                    24

         :CALibration:PLOSs:LATime

         Loss Averaging Time - sec

         At *RST, this value is set to 5.

 9       2.4.1.3   :WARMup
10                 CALibration:WARMup
                   This node controls parameters relating to the warmup of the device.
11
                   For chassis dynamometers, this node describes the procedure to set up the conditions
12                 required to ready the dynamometer for testing. The warm-up consists of running the
13                 dynamometer at a fixed speed over a period of time. Warm-up completion is defined by
                   either running the dynamometer for a fixed period of time, or by monitoring parasitic losses
14                 and comparing them to a target value tolerance.
15       2.4.1.3.1 :INITiate
16                 CALibration:WARMup:INITiate
                   Start the warmup procedure.
17
                   For chassis dynamometers, motor the dynamometer roll to SPEed, and hold this speed for a
18                 TIMeout period of time. All query commands must be accepted and responded to while this
19                 command is executing. This command describes an event and therefore has no associated
                   *RST condition.
20
                   When this command is initiated for dynamometers, the dynamometer must:
21
                   1. Check critical ancillaries, if any, for proper conditions: Brakes Off, Motor Contactor On,
22                 parameters within dynamometer safety limits. For conditions that prohibit operation of this
23                 procedure, issue appropriate warning messages, and execute the Idle Procedure.
24                 2. Set the DYNO operation condition register Warm up Procedure bit indicating the
                   Warm-up is executing. Note: The DYNO operation condition register will be further defined
25
                   in Volume 4.
26
                   3. Accelerate dynamometer to the speed point defined by :CALibration:WARMup:SPEed.
                   4. Average the force at the roll surface required to maintain the speed set point over
                   :CALIbrate:WARMup:LATime. The average force can be monitored by :SENSe:FORCe?
                   5. The procedure will end when the elapsed time is greater than
                   :CALibration:WARMup:TIMeout.

          6. Clear the DYNO operation condition register Warm up Procedure bit indicating the               1

3   Digital Meters
    A digital meter is a basic measuring instrument. It typically measures a single value at one
    point in time. This type of instrument is so general that it is first described generically.
    Attributes specific to a particular type of meter are described in their own subsections.
                                                                                                          1
    All SCPI compliant products implement the commands listed in Syntax & Style, 4.2.
                                                                                                          2
    Figure 3-1 shows an instrument model for a meter. It is derived from Command Reference,
    chapter 2. It is essentially the same as Figure 2-1 in Command Reference with various parts           3
    gray or dashed. The bold boxes and lines, solid and dashed, are described in this chapter. The        4
    FORMat and ROUTe blocks are shown with dashed lines because many meters use their
    default settings. *RST sets FORMat[:READings][:DATA] to ASCii and                                     5
    ROUTe:TERMinals to FRONt. The gray boxes are not described here. While a meter may                    6
    have MEMory, its functionaily is optional and thus not described.

    The CALCulate block is dashed because after *RST this block has no effect on the data.               21

3.1       Base Functionality
          This section describes the functionality all meters implement.
3.1.1     Base Measurement Instructions
          Since the basic function of a meter is to measure some quantity, it understands the
          measurement instructions in Command Reference, 3. A meter shall implement these                  1
          commands with the appropriate substitution for <meter_fn>.                                       2
          KEYWORD                  PARAMETERS                                                              3
          CONFigure
            [:SCALar]                                                                                      4
               :<meter_fn>         [<expected_value>[,<resolution>]]                                       5
          CONFigure?
          FETCh                                                                                            6
            [:SCALar]                                                                                      7
               [:<meter_fn>]?      [<expected_value>[,<resolution>]]
          READ                                                                                             8
            [:SCALar]                                                                                      9
               [:<meter_fn>]?      [<expected_value>[,<resolution>]]
          MEASure                                                                                         10
            [:SCALar]                                                                                     11
               :<meter_fn>?        [<expected_value>[,<resolution>]]
                                                                                                          12
          The syntax of these commands is found in chapter 3 of the Command Reference. Meters             13
          may accept parentheses and <source_list> as described by the full syntax.
                                                                                                          14
          The response from *RST;MEAS:<meter_fn>? is a single <NR1>, <NR2>, or <NR3>
          because *RST sets FORMat to ASCII, TRIGger:COUNt to 1, and ARM:COUNt to 1.                      15
          READ? and FETCh? shall return a <RESPONSE MESSAGE UNIT> containing                              16
          TRIGger:COUNt times ARM:COUNt numbers corresponding to that many measurements.                  17
          If ARM:COUNt is not implemented, its value is one. The timing of measurements is
          controlled by the other settings in the TRIGger subsystem.
                                                                                                          18
          The command sequence MEAS:<meter_fn>?;FETCH? shall return two identical
                                                                                                          19
          <RESPONSE MESSAGE UNIT> elements separated by a semicolon.                                      20

         3.1.1.2     The <expected_value> parameter
 5                   If <expected_value> is present and its value is not DEFault,
 6                   SENSe:<meter_fn>:RANGe[:UPPer] shall be set to the legal value equal to or just larger
                     than <expected_value>. SENSe:<meter_fn>:RANGe:AUTO shall be set OFF.
 7

 8                   SENSe:<meter_fn>:RANGe:AUTO shall be set ON and the instrument shall autorange to
 9                   the best possible range for the measurement.
10       3.1.1.3     The <resolution> parameter
                     If <resolution> is present and its value is not DEFault, SENSe:<meter_fn>:RESolution shall
11                   be set to the legal value equal to or just less than <resolution>.
12                   If <resolution> is not present or its value is DEFault, SENSe:<meter_fn>:RESolution shall
13                   be set to a legal value that gives a reasonably accurate result without taking excessively long.

          The default timing is generally to take a measurement as soon as possible.
          A meter shall implement these TRIGger commands.

                                                                                                            13

          instruments. Command Reference, chapter 20 defines the commands which control the status
          reporting structure.
                                                                                                            15
3.1.3.1   QUEStionable Status
                                                                                                            16
          When a meter is measuring DC volts or AC volts, the meter shall set bit 0, VOLTage, in the        17
          QUEStionable status structure when the meter suspects the voltage is of questionable
                                                                                                            18
          accuracy. When a meter is measuring DC current or AC current, the meter shall set bit 1,
          CURRent, in the QUEStionable status structure when the meter suspects the current is of           19
          questionable accuracy. When a meter is measuring ohms, the meter shall set either bit 0,
                                                                                                            20
          VOLTage, or bit 1, CURRent when the meter suspects either is of questionable accuracy.
                                                                                                            21
3.1.3.2   OPERation Status
          While the meter is performing one of the operations listed in the OPERation status structure,     22
          that bit shall be set in the condition register. Every meter shall report at least RANGing, bit
                                                                                                            23
          2, MEASuring, bit 4, and Waiting for TRIG, bit 5.

         3.3         Various Meter Classes
                     This section provides additional information and rules of behavior for specific meter classes.
         3.3.1       DC Voltmeter
                     DC voltmeters measure the average voltage level of the signal across their inputs.
 1
         3.3.1.1     Range
 2                   DC voltmeters shall measure negative as well as positive voltages symmetrically about zero.
     3               SENSe:RANGe[:UPPer] determines how far from zero measurements can be made. The
                     MINimum and MAXimum values for SENSe:RANGe[:UPPer] shall be positive. Since the
 4                   range is symmetric about zero, SENSe:RANGe:LOWer is not needed, but if implemented its
 5                   value shall be coupled to UPPer by the equation:
 6                      LOWer = -UPPer.

 7       3.3.1.2     SENSe Commands
                     SENSe:VOLTage[:DC] commands are found in Command Reference, 18.20.
 8
         3.3.2       AC RMS Voltmeter
 9                   AC RMS voltmeters measure the root mean square of the voltage level across their inputs.
10       3.3.2.1     Range
11                   Since the RMS of any signal is non-negative, the MINimum and MAXimum values for
                     SENSe:RANGe[:UPPer] shall be positive. SENSe:RANGe:LOWer is not needed.
12
         3.3.2.2     SENSe Commands
13                   SENSe:VOLTage:AC commands are found in Command Reference 1994, 18.21.
14       3.3.3       Ohmmeter
15                   Ohmmeters measure the resistance across their input terminals.

16                   Typically, a DC current is sourced and the DC voltage is measured. Resistance is calculated
                     by dividing the current into the voltage.
17
         3.3.3.1     SENSe Commands
18                   SENSe:RESistance commands are found in Command Reference 1994, 18.16.
19       3.3.3.2     4-wire Ohmmeter
20                   4-wire ohmmeters measure the resistance across two of their input terminals with the
                     assistance of two additional wires.
21
                     Typically, a DC current is sourced through one set of wires and the DC voltage is measured
22                   across the other set. As with a 2-wire ohms measurement, resistance is calculated by dividing
23                   the current into the voltage.
24       3.3.3.3     SENSe Commands
                     SENSe:FRESistance commands are found in Command Reference 1994, 18.16.
25
         3.3.4       DC Ammeter
26                   DC ammeters measure the average value of the current through their inputs.



         3-8     Digital Meters

3.3.4.1   Range
          DC ammeters shall follow the same constraints on RANGe as DC voltmeters.
3.3.4.2   SENSe Commands
          SENSe:CURRent[:DC] commands are found in Command Reference 1994, 18.6.

                                                                                                      1

         3.4        Programming Examples
                    This section discusses how a user might program a meter for certain applications. The
                    examples assume the meter is a DC voltmeter, but a meter of any type could have been used.
         3.4.1      Simple Measurement
 1                  In an application where the user wants to make a simple measurement with no special
 2                  consideration for signal conditioning or timing, the MEASure query is an excellent choice.
                    An example might be checking if a power supply voltage is at a proper level. The instrument
     3              might receive the following query to make a voltage measurement:
 4                     MEASure:VOLTage:DC?
 5                  The instrument autoranges to the best range and makes the measurement with a reasonable
 6                  resolution. A single value is returned as soon as possible. The instrument does not wait for
                    any other triggers.
 7
                    Another user might send:
 8
                       MEASure:VOLTage:DC? 5,.05
 9
                    A voltmeter that has 1, 10, and 100 volt ranges would be in the 10 volt range. Another
10                  voltmeter with 3, 30, and 300 volt ranges would use the 30 volt range. Resolution would
                    probably get set to 10 mv corresponding to 3 1/2 digits. Again the measurement is made as
11
                    soon as possible.
12
                    This same measurement could be made using low level commands.
13                     *RST
14                     SENSe:FUNCtion “VOLTage:DC”;VOLTage:RANGe 5V;RESolution .05V
                       INITiate;FETCh?
15
                    Note that *RST sets all TRIGger subsystem SOURce to IMMediate and COUNt to 1.
16
         3.4.2      Time Critical Measurement
17                  To use an external triggering signal, the user cannot use MEASure query because MEASure
18                  query sets TRIGger:SOURce to IMMediate. Instead, CONFigure and READ? with TRIGger
                    commands between them is the proper choice. The sequence:
19
                       CONFigure:VOLTage:DC 5V,.05V
20                     TRIGger:SOURce EXTernal
                       READ?
21
                    sets up the SENSe functions easily. The single TRIGger command modifies the triggering
22                  subsystem just enough to do the job. The READ query initiates a measurement which waits
23                  for the external trigger before returning the result.
24       3.4.3      Multiple Measurements
                    The overhead of sending commands may prevent taking measurements made close together
25                  in time using a separate MEASure query or READ? for each measurement. The instrument
26                  could, however, buffer the readings. The sequence:



         3-10    Digital Meters
                       1999 SCPI Instrument Classes

   CONFigure:VOLTage:DC 5V,.05V
   TRIGger:SOURce EXTernal;COUNt 10
   READ?
returns ten separate measurements taken when ten external triggers occur. A defensive
programmer would then send SYSTem:ERRor? and check for error -210, “Trigger error” or
                                                                                          1
-211, “Trigger ignored” to see if there were any problems with the triggering.

4   Digitizers
    A digitizer is an instrument designed primarily to measure time-swept voltage waveforms.
    Because a digitizer is primarily a sensing device, the SENSe root node is optional.
    All SCPI compliant products implement the commands listed in Syntax & Style, 4.2.                   1
    Figure 4-1 shows an instrument model for a digitizer. It is derived from Command                    2
    Reference, chapter 2. It is essentially the same as Figure 2-1 in Command Reference with
    various parts gray or dashed. The bold boxes and lines, solid and dashed, are described in          3
    this chapter. The ROUTe block are shown with dashed lines because many digitizers use               4
    their default settings.
                                                                                                        5
    The gray boxes are not described here. While a digitizer may have MEMory, its functionaily
    is optional and thus not described.                                                                 6
                                                                                                        7
                                                                                                        8
                                                                                                        9

                         Figure 4-1 Simplified Model of a Digitizer
                                                                                                       18

    Figure 4-2 shows how the “Measurement Function” block in Figure 4-1 is expanded in a
                                                                                                       20
    digitizer. It is the same as Figure 2-4 in Command Reference with some dashed and gray
    boxes. The CALCulate block is dashed because after *RST this block has no effect on the            21
    data. This chapter does not describe any CALCulate functions. The MEMory block is gray
                                                                                                       22
    because while a digitizer may contain this function, this chapter does not address it.

 9       4.1         Base Functionality
10                   This section describes the functionality all digitizers implement.

11                   The <bf_keyword> for a digitizer is DIGITIZER.

12                   Digitizer inputs are typically called channels. These are generally numbered 1, 2, 3, ... or
                     lettered A, B, C, .... Several SCPI commands in this section use numeric suffixes on header
13                   keywords or parameters. The intention is that these suffixes unify operations that apply to
14                   the associated channel.

15                   Two-channel capability is shown in the examples to illustrate this concept. A single channel
                     digitizer may be implemented by omitting the command and or parameter options with the
16                   numeric suffix 2. More than two channels may be implemented by extending the numeric
17                   suffix.
18       4.1.1       Base Measurement Instruction
                     The base functionality for a digitizer requires no measurement instructions (MEASure,
19                   CONFigure, READ, FETCh).
20       4.1.2       Base Device-oriented Functions
21                   The base functionality for digitizers shall contain the commands described in this section.
22       4.1.2.1     Input functions
23                   KEYWORD                   PARAMETER FORM                             SCPI Reference
24                   INPut[1]|INPut2                                                      Vol 2-11
                       :COUPling               AC | DC | GND                              Vol 2-11.3
25
26                   This command controls the coupling characteristics of the input to the amplifier.
                     At *RST, the coupling for digitizers shall be DC.


         4-2     Digitizers

          As previously mentioned, INPut1 is associated with the first input channel, and so on.

4.2       Programming Example
          The following set of commands sets up the digitizer to acquire a waveform on channel 1 for          2
          AC coupling, 10 peak to peak signal with a sample recorded every microsecond. The trigger           3
          source is channel 1 and is DC coupled, looking for a positive slope transition of 100
          millivolts. After setting up the digitizer the trigger system is initiated and the resultant        4
          captured waveform is returned to the controller in ASCII format.                                    5
          Longform version:                                                                                   6
             *RST                                                                                             7
             INPut:COUPling AC
             SENSe:VOLTage:DC:RANGE:PTPeak 10 V                                                               8
             SENSe:SWEep:TINTerval 1E-6 S
             SENSe:FUNCtion:CONCurrent OFF                                                                    9
             SENSe:FUNCtion:ON “XTIMe:VOLTage:DC 1"                                                          10
             TRIGger:SEQuence1:LEVel 0.1V
             INITiate:IMMediate:ALL                                                                          11
             SENSe:DATA?
                                                                                                             12
          Shortform version:
                                                                                                             13
             *RST
             INP:COUP AC                                                                                     14
             VOLT:RANG:PTP 10
             SWE:TINT 1E-6 S
                                                                                                             15
             FUNC:CONC 0;ON “XTIM:VOLT 1"                                                                    16
             TRIG:LEV 0.1
             INIT                                                                                            17
             DATA?
                                                                                                             18

5       Emissions Benches
        An emissions bench is a complex measuring device. It measures the constituent                       2
        concentration in a sample of gas introduced into the bench. It typically consists of several        3
        instruments, at least one of which is a gas analyzer, but also can include a mini-diluter, a gas
        divider, as well as temperature, pressure, and flow measurement instruments.                        4
        All SCPI compliant products implement the commands listed in Syntax and Style, 4.2.                 5
                                                                                                            6
                   Signal                       Measurement                                       data      7
                   Routing                                                         FORMat
                                                  Function                                        bus
                                                                                                            8
                                                                                                            9
                                                                                                           10
                                         TRIGger            MEMory                                         11
                                                                                                           12
                                                                                                           13
                   Signal                          Signal                                           data   14
                   Routing                       Generation                        FORMat           bus
                                                                                                           15
                       Figure 5-1 Simplified Model for an Emissions Bench
                                                                                                           16
                                                                                                           17
        As indicated in Figure 5-1 above, emissions benches make use of signal (gas) routing
                                                                                                           18
        commands, the TRIGger subsystem, extensive use of measurement function commands
        (using the :SENSe block), and extensive use of the :MEMory subsystem. In addition, the             19
        :CALibrate and :SYSTem subsystems are utilized in both standard and emissions
                                                                                                           20
        bench-specific ways.
                                                                                                           21
5.1     Base Functionality
        This section describes the base functionality for emissions benches.                               22
        The <bf_keyword> for an emissions bench is EBENCH.                                                 23
5.1.1   Base Measurement Instructions                                                                      24
        The base functionality for an emissions bench contains no commands from the                        25
        :MEASurement subsystem.
                                                                                                           26
5.1.2   Base Device-Oriented Functions
        The base functionality for an emissions bench include :SENSe, :MEMory, :TRIGger,
        :CALibration, :CONTrol, :SYSTem, :DIAGnostic, :INSTrument, and :ROUTe subsystems.
        It also defines device dependent :STATus bits and instructions for emissions benches. A
        SCPI-compliant emissions bench shall implement all of the commands listed in this section.

NOTE:
:SENSe:CORRection:CALCulate calculates the zero/span adjustment of the form
                                                                                        18
        y=mx+b
                                                                                        19
where        x = %FSRAW Data Value
                                                                                        20
             y = %FSADJ Data Value                                                      21
             m = Zero/Span Adjustment Slope Coefficient                                 22
             b = Zero/Span Adjustment Intercept Coefficient
                                                                                        23
and
                                                                                        24
             S0 − Z0
        m=                                                                              25
             Sm − Zm
             Z0Sm − ZmS0                                                                26
        b=
               Sm − Zm
where        Z0 = Zero Gas Expected
             Zm = Zero Gas Measured
             S0 = Span Gas Expected
             Sm = Span Gas Measured

         5.3.1     Zero/Span/Zero Procedure
     5             The following illustrates a possible command sequence for performing a zero/span/zero
 6                 procedure:

 7                     SCPI Command               Notes
                      :INST:DEFine:GROup “BENCH”,"CONC1","CONC2"
 8                    :INST:SELect “BENCH”
                                          Select desired analyzers
 9                    :SENSe:FUNCtion:CONCurrent ON
10                    :SENSe:FUNCtion “CONC1",”CONC1:SDEV","CONC2","CONC2:SDEV"
                                          Applies to selected analyzers; used in :SENS:DATA
11                    :SENSe:CORRection:ZERO:DTOLerance 5
                                          Allow 5% tolerance for zero drift
12                    :SENSe:CORRection:SPOint:DTOLerance 5
13                                        Allow 5% tolerance for set point (span) drift
                      :SENSe:CORRection:STATe OFF
14                                        New Z/S/Z needs uncorrected values;
                                          drift check would require :SENS:CORR:STATE ON
15                    :SENSe:CORRection:ZERO:ACQuire
16                                        request and execute zero procedure
                      :STATus:OPERation:INSTrument:ISUMmary1:BIT10:CALibrating?
17                                        Keep polling while bit 1 (zero) is set (CONC1)
                      :STATus:OPERation:INSTrument:ISUMmary2:BIT10:CALibrating?
18                                        Keep polling while bit 1 (zero) is set (CONC2)
19                    :STATus:QUEStionable:INSTrument:ISUMmary1:BIT10:CALibrating?
                                          0 = successful zero; Bit 1 set = failure
20                    :STATus:QUEStionable:INSTrument:ISUMmary2:BIT10:CALibrating?
                                          0 = successful zero; Bit 1 set = failure
21                    :SENSe:DATA?        Retrieve Zero Concentration Readings and SDEVs
22                    :MEMory:DATA?ZDRift Retrieve Zero Drifts
                      :SENSe:CORRection:SPOint:ACQuire
23                                        execute SPOint (span) procedure
                      *WAI                Alternative to polling;
24                                        wait for SPOint (span) operation to complete
25                    :STATus:QUEStionable:INSTrument:ISUMmary1:BIT10:CALibrating?
                                          0 = successful zero; Bit 2 set = failure
26                    :STATus:QUEStionable:INSTrument:ISUMmary2:BIT10:CALibrating?
                                          0 = successful zero; Bit 2 set = failure
                      :SENSe:DATA?        Retrieve Span Concentration Readings and SDEV’s
                      :MEMory:DATA?SDRift Retrieve Span Drifts
                      :SENSe:CORRection:CALCulate
                                          Calculate new m, b corrections (skip this if drift check)
                      :SENSe:CORRection:ZERO:ACQuire
                                          do re-zero

5.4       CALibration Subsystem (Bench Commands)                                                             1
          KEYWORD            PARAMETER FORM                      NOTES
          :CALibration                                                                                       2
            :LINearize                                                                                       3
            | :ACCept                                            [event]
            | :ACQuire                                           [event]                                     4
            | :AUTO          ONCE                                [event]                                     5
            | :CALCulate     AUTO | POLYnomial<n>
            |                | SRATional<n>                      [event]                                     6
            | :CURve                                                                                         7
            | | [:TYPE]      POLYnomial<n>
            | |              | SRATional<n>, <numeric_value>{,<numeric_value>}                               8
            | | :ZFORce      <Boolean>                                                                       9
            | :VERify
            | | :ACQuire                                         [event]                                    10
            | | :TOLerance   <numeric_value>                                                                11
            | | :TYPE        CCURve | NCURve
                                                                                                            12
5.4.1     :LINearize                                                                                        13
          CALibration:LINearize
                                                                                                            14
          The LINearize subsystem is used to produce a calibration curve used to linearize a non-linear
          instrument. An instance of this subsystem exists for each range in an instrument. The data        15
          defined and queried and the events will only be performed on the currently selected range         16
          and instrument.
                                                                                                            17
5.4.1.1   :ACCept
          CALibration:LINearize:ACCept                                                                      18
          ACCept causes an already-calculated or supplied set of coefficients to be placed into regular     19
          use by an instrument. This consists of replacing the “current” values with the “new” values.
          The current values can be obtained by querying :SENSe:CONCentration:RANGe:LSET?.                  20
5.4.2     :ACQuire                                                                                          21
          CALibration:LINearize:ACQuire
                                                                                                            22
          ACQuire causes the automatic collection of linearization data POINts for the currently
          selected range of the currently selected analyzer to begin. Results are placed in a predefined    23
          table as they are collected. This procedure stores the expected gas concentration, causes gas     24
          flow for the defined cutPOINts, waits for a stabilized reading of each one, and records the
          measured values. :SENSe:STABilize:STATe must be ON when this command is issued.                   25
          Gases are selected for the duration of the procedure.                                             26
5.4.2.1   :AUTO ONCE
          CALibration:LINearize:AUTO
          This command shall perform linearization based on a vendor defined procedure, including
          :CALibrate:LINearize:ACQuire and possibly other procedures, for example
          :SENSe:CORRection:ZERO and :SPOint. :SENSe:STABilize:STATe must be ON when this
          command is issued. Gases are selected for the duration of the procedure. This command is

                                                                            Emissions Benches        5-15
                                   1999 SCPI Instrument Class Applications

 1                 provided to allow the instrument to perform an automated linearization procedure according
                   to the manufacturer’s recommended practice.
 2
         5.4.2.2   :CALCulate AUTO|POLYnomial<n>|SRATional<n>
 3                 CALibration:LINearize:CALCulate
 4                 Using the results data stored in a predefined linearization table, calculate a linearization
                   curve. The results are placed in that table. A curve fit of type AUTO allows the device to
     5             calculate the curve fit according to the manufacturer’s recommended practice. A
 6                 POLYnomial<n> parameter shall limit the calculation to the specified polynomial curve
                   type. A SRATional<n> parameter shall limit the linearization to the specified simple rational
 7                 curve fit. The <n> designates the order of the curve. A curve fit can automatically be forced
 8                 through the origin, if :CALibration:LINearize:CURVe:ZFORce has been turned on. The
                   results can be stored in the instrument at a later time (see ACCept). An example of the
 9                 predefined table follows:
10                 LSI01R01
11
                     CPOint (%FS)          EXPected             RAW             CCURve           NCURve
12
                           6.7               10000              464646            10015           10001
13                        20.0               30000              484848            30109           30000
14                        33.3               50000              515151            49905           49999
15                        46.7               70000              525252            71004           70001
16                         60                90000              555555            89950           90005
17                        73.3              110000              565656           111070           110100

18                        86.7              130000              575859           129051           129999
                           100              150000              590101           150031           149000

         5.4.2.3   :CURVe
21                 CALibration:LINearize:CURVe

22                 This node controls analyzer curve fitting.

23       5.4.2.3.1 [:TYPE] POLYnomial<n> | SRATional<n>, <numeric_value>{,<numeric_value>}
                   CALibration:LINearize:CURVe[:TYPE]
24                 [:TYPE] sets or retrieves the information used to determine a calibration curve.
25                 The first parameter is the curve type, which consists of either POLYnomial for a polynomial
26                 curve fit or SRATional for a simple rational polynomial curve fit, followed by a positive
                   integer <n>, which is the curve order.
                   The additional parameters are the curve coefficients. These are listed starting with the 0th
                   order term. Note that the number of coefficients depends on the order of the curve - there are
                   exactly n+1 coefficients for a curve of order n. For example:
                      :CALibration:LINearize:CURVe:TYPE
                      POLY3,-0.117,-7.43,1.02,-0.034

         5-16   Emissions Benches
                             1999 SCPI Instrument Class Applications

          defines a calibration curve of type 3rd order polynomial and the four coefficients used.             1
          As a query, TYPE returns latest new pending curve fit type and calculated curve coefficients.        2
          If, as in the above example,                                                                         3
                   f(x) = − 0.117 − 7.43∗x + 1.02∗x2 − 0.034∗x3                                                4
          results from the curve fit, the returned curve values shall be:                                      5
             POLY3,-0.117,-7.43,1.02,-0.034
                                                                                                               6
          A third order simple rational polynomial
                                        x                                                                      7
                 f(x) =
                        0.81 − 2.0∗x + 1.17∗x2 + 0.02∗x3                                                       8
          shall be represented by the parameters                                                               9
             SRAT3,0.81,-2.0,1.17,0.02
                                                                                                              10
5.4.2.3.2 :ZFORce <Boolean>
          CALibration:LINearize:CURVe:ZFORce                                                                  11
          The setting of ZFORce (Zero FORce) determines whether or not a newly calculated curve               12
          will be fit such that the scalar polynomial term is 0. This affects the
          :CALibration:LINearize:CALCulate command.                                                           13
          At *RST, ZFORce is not changed.                                                                     14
5.4.2.4   :VERify                                                                                             15
          CALibration:LINearize:VERify
                                                                                                              16
          VERify causes the instrument to check the validity of a set of linearization coefficients by
          checking the difference from the concentration measured with the curve to the expected              17
          concentration of the verification gas.                                                              18
          This command is an event, and therefore has no *RST value associated with it.                       19
5.4.2.4.1 :ACQuire                                                                                            20
          CALibration:LINearize:VERify:ACQuire
          ACQuire causes the flow and stabilization of a verification gas to occur. First, verification       21
          gas flow is enabled, next a stabilized reading is taken, and finally the verification gas flow is   22
          disabled. The concentration determined from this procedure is compared against a known
          concentration stored in a designated table. If the difference between the expected                  23
          concentration of the verification gas and the concentration measured using the curve                24
          coefficients is greater than the tolerance value set by :CALibration:LINearize:VERify:TOL,
          then the appropriate questionable status bit is set.                                                25
          This command is an event, and therefore has no *RST value associated with it.                       26
5.4.2.4.2 :TOLerance <numeric_value>
          CALibration:LINearize:VERify:TOLerance
          TOLerance sets the allowable tolerance between the expected concentration of the
          verification gas and the concentration measured using the curve coefficients in % of full
          scale of the active range of the selected analyzer.


                                                                             Emissions Benches         5-17
                                    1999 SCPI Instrument Class Applications

 1                 At *RST, TOLerance is not changed.
 2       5.4.2.4.3 :TYPE
                   CALibration:LINearize:VERify:TYPE
 3                 TYPE selects the linearization coefficients to be verified. Possible types are:
 4                            CCURve - The curve coefficients currently in effect
     5                        NCURve - A newly calculated or downloaded set of coefficients that are not yet
 6                            in use.
 7                 At *RST, TYPE is set to CCURve.

         5.5.1.2   :CALCulate
24                 DIAGnostic:HUP:CALCulate

25                 Compare the direct zero value with the overflow zero value. These values and their
                   difference are stored in memory table HUPResults. The difference is compared with the
26                 value in memory table HUPTolerance. Error bit 4 of
                   :STATus:QUEStionable:INSTrument:ISUMmary5:BIT10 is set if the value of the difference
                   is outside of the tolerance values stored in HUPTolerance. These tolerance values are upper
                   and lower tolerance in ppm.
                   This command is an event, and therefore has no *RST value associated with it.

6         Emission Test Cell
          An Emission Test Cell consists of one or more computers and a set of instruments that are       2
          used to perform emissions testing. The instruments which are included in an ETCELL may          3
          include Emission Benches, Dynamometers, Sampling Systems, and other emissions
          measurement or other devices. In order to standardize the interfaces within the cell it is      4
          desirable that all instrument implement a core set of commands. These commands are              5
          described in this chapter.
                                                                                                          6
          All SCPI compliant Emission Test Cells shall implement the commands listed in Syntax &
          Style sections 4.2.                                                                             7
                                                                                                          8
6.1       Base Functionality
          This section describes the base functionality for an Emission Test Cell.                        9
          The <bf_keyword> for an Emissions Test Cell is ETCELL.                                         10
6.1.1     Base Measurement Instructions                                                                  11
          The base functionality for an ETCELL contains no commands from the MEASure subsystem.          12
6.1.2     Base Device-oriented Functions                                                                 13
          ETCELL compliant instruments shall include SYSTem commands, which set up and cause
          communication between instruments and the site computer and the set up and transfer of         14
          data from instruments.                                                                         15

6.3.2   Command Channel Example                                                                         1
        Assume the Site computer wants to configure an Emission Test Cell instrument to perform a
        reading and return the data. The following commands might be issued to the instrument to
                                                                                                        2
        perform this reading.                                                                           3
        Commands                                                                                        4
           SENSE:FUNCtion:CONCurrent ON                  Configure to sense data from                   5
                                                         more than one analyzer.
                                                                                                        6
           SENSe:FUNCtion “CONC1:TAL”,"CONC2:TAL", “CONC3:TAL”,"CONC4:TAL"
                              Select the required data.                                                 7
           SENSe:CONCentration:RANGe:AUTO ON
                              Set instrument to automatic range mode.                                   8
           INITiate           Start the measurement                                                     9
           SENSe:DATA?        Return data values for CONC1:TAL etc
                                                                                                       10
        By default, the result is returned in ASCII. The FORMat subsystem can be used to configure
        the instrument to send the data in various binary formats.                                     11
6.3.3   Two Channel Example                                                                            12
        This example illustrates how to configure the instrument to send continuously acquired data
                                                                                                       13
        on a separate channel from the SCPI command channel. This allows results to be
        continuously streamed back from the instrument to the controller.                              14
        Assume the controller wants the instrument to take data every 0.1 second, average the data     15
        over one second, buffer it then feed it out a second channel every 5 seconds.
                                                                                                       16
           Setup Sense functions to get modal data averaged over a second
           SENSe:FUNCtion:CONCurrent ON                                                                17
           SENSe:FUNCtion “CONC1 ON AVERage”,"CONC2 ON AVERage",                                       18
           “CONC3 ON AVERage”,"CONC4 ON AVERage"
           Setup averaging parameter for the modal data                                                19
           SENSe:AVERage:COUNt 10
           SENSe:AVERage:TCONtrol REPeat
                                                                                                       20
           SENSe:AVERage:TYPE SCALAR                                                                   21
           Turn the Averaging ON inside of the Sense block
           SENSe:AVERage:STATe ON                                                                      22
           Trigger Sequence will setup rates to sense the modal data
           TRIGger:SEQuence1:SOURce TIMer
                                                                                                       23
           TRIGger:SEQuence1:TIMer 0.1     set sampling rate of 0.1sec                                 24
           TRIGger:SEQuence2:LINK “TRIGger:SEQuence1"
           TRIGger:SEQuence2:ECOunt 10     set integration rate                                        25
                                           10 times 0.1=1sec
           TRIGger:SEQuence3:LINK ”TRIGger:SEQuence1"
                                                                                                       26
           TRIGger:SEQuence3:ECOunt 50     set transmission rate
                                           50 times 0.1=5sec
           Setup and connect on the communication socket
           SYStem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:ADDRess “123.45.67.89"
           SYStem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:PORT 701
           SYStem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:TYPE TCP


                                                                          Emission Test Cell     6-3

 1                      SYStem:COMMunicate:SOCKet:CONNect
                        Setup the Socket feed to data channel

                        ON AVERage".........

7   Power Supplies
    A power supply is a basic sourcing instrument. It typically supplies a constant voltage or
    current at significant power levels to energize an electrical circuit. Because a power supply is
    primarily a source, the SOURce root node is optional.
                                                                                                        1
    All SCPI compliant products implement the commands listed in Syntax & Style section 4.2.
                                                                                                        2
    Figure 7-1 shows an instrument model for a power supply. It is derived from Command
    Reference, Chapter 2. It is essentially the same as Figure 2-1 in Command Reference with            3
    various parts shaded or dashed. The shaded boxes are not described here. While a power              4
    supply may have a MEMory subsystem, its operation is not described. The TRIGger block is
    dashed because not all power supplies have that functionality. While a power supply                 5
    contains FORMat and Signal Routing functionality, their behaviors generally follow the              6
    *RST setting. These blocks are not described so they are dashed.
                                                                                                        7
                                                                                                        8
                                                                                                        9

                                                                                                       12
                                                                                                       13
                                                                                                       14
                                                                                                       15
                                                                                                       16
                                                                                                       17
                      Figure 7-1 Simplified Model for a Power Supply
                                                                                                       18
                                                                                                       19
    Figure 7-2 shows how the “Signal Generation” block in Figure 7-1 is expanded in a power
                                                                                                       20
    supply. It is the same as Figure 2-5 in Command Reference with some shaded and dashed
    boxes. The MEMory block is shaded because while a power supply may contain this                    21
    function, this chapter does not address it. The CALCulate block is dashed and its behavior
                                                                                                       22
    not described. It behaves according to the *RST value.

                    This section describes the base functionality for power supplies.
12
                    The <bf_keyword> for a DC power supply is DCPSUPPLY.
13
         7.1.1      Base Measurement Instructions
14                  The base functionality for a power supply contains no measurement instructions.
15       7.1.2      Base Device-oriented Functions
16       7.1.2.1    Outputs
17                  A power supply shall have at least one output which can be turned on and off. This OUTPut
                    subsystem command shall be implemented.
18
                    KEYWORD                  PARAMETER FORM                             SCPI Reference
19                  OUTPut                                                              Vol 2-15
20                   [:STATe]                <Boolean>                                  Vol 2-15.12
21                  As stated in Command Reference, *RST sets the output state to off.
22       7.1.2.2    SOURce subsystem
23                  A power supply shall provide control of voltage and current by implementing these
                    commands.
24
25
26


         7-2     Power Supplies
                                   1999 SCPI Instrument Classes

          KEYWORD                PARAMETER FORM                             SCPI Reference
          [SOURce]                                                          Vol 2-19
            :CURRent                                                        Vol 2-19.5
              [:LEVel]                                                      Vol 2-19.5.4
                 [:IMMediate]                                               Vol 2-19.5.4.1
                    [:AMPLitude] <numeric_value>                            Vol 2-19.5.4.1.1
                                                                                                           1
            :VOLTage                                                        Vol 2-19.23                    2
              [:LEVel]                                                      Vol 2-19.23.4
                 [:IMMediate]                                               Vol 2-19.23.4.1
                                                                                                           3
                    [:AMPLitude] <numeric_value>                            Vol 2-19.23.4.1.1              4
          A power supply can operate in one of two modes: voltage source or current source. The
                                                                                                           5
          mode of operation depends on the load connected to it. When a power supply is operating as       6
          a voltage source, the :VOLTage command sets the output voltage and the :CURRent
          command sets the current limit. When a power supply is operating as a current source, the
                                                                                                           7
          :VOLTage command sets the voltage limit and the :CURRent command sets the output                 8
          current.
                                                                                                           9
          If the :CURRent and :VOLTage commmands are implemented as overlapped commands, the
          associated Pending-Operation flags shall be reported in the No-Operation-Pending flag. The
                                                                                                          10
          operation started by the :CURRent command completes when the output current has reached         11
          the programmed current value or when the voltage limit has been reached. Likewise, the
          operation started by the :VOLTage command completes when the output voltage has
                                                                                                          12
          reached the programmed voltage value or the current limit has been reached.                     13
          At *RST a power supply is required to set the voltage and current to “safe” conditions. This    14
          is generally achieved by setting them to their values closest to zero.
                                                                                                          15
7.1.3     Base Status Reporting
          All SCPI power supplies shall implement the status reporting structure described in Syntax
                                                                                                          16
          & Style, Status Reporting. Command Reference, STATus Subsystem defines the commands             17
          which shall be used to control the status reporting structure.
                                                                                                          18
7.1.3.1   QUEStionable
                                                                                                          19
          For a power supply, the bits of interest in the QUEStionable status structure are VOLTage
          and CURRent. When a power supply is operating as a voltage source, bit 1 (CURRent) shall        20
          be set. When a power supply is operating as a current source, bit 0 (VOLTage) shall be set.
                                                                                                          21
          When the output is unregulated, both bits shall be set (for example, while the output is
          changing to a new programmed value).                                                            22
7.1.3.2   OPERation                                                                                       23
          The base functionality of a power supply adds no requirements for this register.
                                                                                                          24
                                                                                                          25
                                                                                                          26
